attributes.references: CMS MS-DRG Definitions Manual; 3M HIS Grouper; CMS IPPS; HAC Reduction Program

attributes.name: chronic_condition_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this diagnosis represents a chronic condition as defined by CMS Chronic Condition Warehouse (CCW) or clinical classification standards. True = chronic condition. Supports population health management, care management program enrollment, HEDIS chronic disease measure attribution, and SDOH analysis.
attributes.references: CMS Chronic Condition Warehouse (CCW); NCQA HEDIS Chronic Disease Measures; AHRQ Clinical Classifications Software

attributes.name: coded_date
attributes.description: The date on which the ICD-10-CM code was assigned to this diagnosis by the HIM coding team. Used for coding productivity tracking, CDI program metrics, and revenue cycle timeliness reporting. Sourced from 3M HIS and Epic Resolute coding workflows.
attributes.references: AHIMA Coding Productivity Standards; 3M HIS; CMS Timely Filing Requirements

attributes.name: coding_provider_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the clinician or coder who assigned or attested this diagnosis code. Used for audit trails, CDI accountability, RAC audit defense, and provider-level coding quality reporting. Sourced from 3M HIS and Epic ClinDoc coding workflows.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; HIPAA Administrative Simplification; OIG Compliance; 3M HIS

attributes.name: coding_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of this diagnosis record within the HIM/CDI coding lifecycle. 'pending' indicates awaiting coder review; 'coded' indicates initial code assignment; 'validated' indicates coder-confirmed; 'queried' indicates a CDI query has been issued; 'amended' indicates a post-bill correction; 'final' indicates billing-ready. Drives revenue cycle workflow and CDI query management in 3M HIS and Epic Resolute.
attributes.references: AHIMA Coding Guidelines; 3M HIS CDI Workflow; CMS RAC Audit Requirements; OIG Compliance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this visit diagnosis record was first created in the source system or ingested into the Silver layer. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED canonical category requirement.
attributes.references: HIPAA Audit Controls 45 CFR §164.312(b); HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; SOC 2

attributes.name: diagnosis_rank
attributes.description: Clinical ranking of this diagnosis by severity or clinical significance within the encounter, as assigned by the coding team or clinical documentation system. Distinct from diagnosis_seq_num (billing sequence); this rank reflects clinical priority for care management and quality reporting purposes.
attributes.references: AHIMA Clinical Documentation Improvement; 3M HIS CDI; Epic ClinDoc

attributes.name: diagnosis_seq_num
attributes.description: Ordinal position of this diagnosis within the encounter's diagnosis list. Sequence 1 typically denotes the principal diagnosis. Used for claim form ordering (UB-04 diagnosis fields), DRG grouping logic, and quality measure attribution. Aligns with LINE_SEQUENCE canonical category.
attributes.references: CMS UHDDS; UB-04 Claim Form FL 67; CMS-1500 Box 21; 3M HIS Grouper

attributes.name: diagnosis_source
attributes.description: Identifies who or what originated this diagnosis record. 'physician' = entered by the treating clinician; 'coder' = assigned by HIM coding staff; 'cdi_specialist' = added via CDI query resolution; 'system' = auto-populated by clinical decision support; 'imported' = received via HIE or external system. Supports audit trail and coding accountability.
attributes.references: AHIMA CDI Practice Standards; OIG Compliance; HL7 FHIR R4 Condition.recorder; Epic ClinDoc

attributes.name: diagnosis_type
attributes.description: Classification of the diagnosis role within the encounter. 'admitting' is the reason for admission; 'principal' is the condition chiefly responsible for the stay after study; 'secondary' are comorbidities and complications; 'discharge' is the final coded diagnosis at discharge; 'working' is a provisional diagnosis during the encounter; 'final' is the confirmed diagnosis post-workup. Drives DRG assignment and UB-04/CMS-1500 claim form population.
attributes.references: CMS Uniform Hospital Discharge Data Set (UHDDS); UB-04 Claim Form; CMS-1500; UHDDS Principal Diagnosis Definition

attributes.name: drg_code
attributes.description: The MS-DRG or APR-DRG code assigned to the encounter as influenced by this diagnosis. Populated after DRG grouping by 3M HIS or CMS grouper. Central to inpatient reimbursement under IPPS and case mix index (CMI) calculation.
attributes.references: CMS MS-DRG Definitions Manual; 3M APR-DRG Grouper; CMS IPPS; UB-04 FL 71

attributes.name: drg_relevance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this diagnosis code contributes to the DRG assignment for this encounter. True = this diagnosis is a complication/comorbidity (CC) or major complication/comorbidity (MCC) that affects DRG grouping and reimbursement. Critical for revenue cycle optimization and CDI program targeting.
attributes.references: CMS MS-DRG Grouper; 3M APR-DRG; CMS IPPS; UHDDS CC/MCC Definitions

attributes.name: drg_type
attributes.description: Specifies the DRG classification system used: MS-DRG (Medicare Severity DRG, CMS), APR-DRG (All Patient Refined DRG, 3M), or IR-DRG (International Refined DRG). Determines the reimbursement methodology and payer applicability.
attributes.references: CMS MS-DRG; 3M APR-DRG; WHO IR-DRG; CMS IPPS

attributes.name: encounter_diagnosis_comment
attributes.description: Free-text clinical comment or qualifier associated with this diagnosis record, as entered by the coding team or clinician. May include specificity notes, CDI query resolution rationale, or coding clarifications. Classified as restricted PHI per HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; AHIMA CDI; Epic ClinDoc; 3M HIS

attributes.name: encounter_diagnosis_source_code
attributes.description: The native identifier for this diagnosis record in the source operational system (e.g., Epic ClinDoc diagnosis ID or Cerner PowerChart diagnosis ID). Supports ETL lineage, data reconciliation, and source system audit trails in the Silver layer.
attributes.references: Epic ClinDoc; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR R4; HITRUST CSF Data Lineage

attributes.name: external_cause_code
attributes.description: ICD-10-CM external cause code (V, W, X, Y codes) documenting the cause, place of occurrence, activity, and status for injury and poisoning diagnoses. Required for trauma registries, injury surveillance, workers' compensation claims, and public health reporting.
attributes.references: ICD-10-CM External Cause Codes (V00-Y99); CMS Coding Guidelines; AHRQ Injury Surveillance; State Trauma Registry Requirements

attributes.name: hai_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this diagnosis represents a healthcare-associated infection (HAI) such as CLABSI, CAUTI, or SSI. True = HAI diagnosis. Triggers HAI surveillance workflows, CMS HAC Reduction Program payment adjustments, and TJC infection control reporting.
attributes.references: CMS HAC Reduction Program; The Joint Commission Infection Control Standards; CDC NHSN HAI Definitions; AHRQ

attributes.name: hcc_category_code
attributes.description: The specific CMS HCC category code to which this ICD-10-CM diagnosis maps. Populated only when hcc_flag is True. Used for risk score calculation in Medicare Advantage, ACO, and MIPS/APM programs. Sourced from CMS HCC mapping crosswalk tables.
attributes.references: CMS HCC Risk Adjustment Model V28; CMS-HCC Crosswalk; MACRA; CMS Medicare Advantage

attributes.name: hcc_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this ICD-10-CM diagnosis code maps to a CMS Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) used for risk adjustment in Medicare Advantage and ACO programs. True = this diagnosis contributes to the patient's HCC risk score. Critical for population health management, value-based care contracting, and capitation payment accuracy.
attributes.references: CMS HCC Risk Adjustment Model; CMS-HCC V28; MACRA APM Framework; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: icd10_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Code
attributes.description: The ICD-10-CM diagnosis code assigned to this visit. Drives DRG grouping, quality measure attribution, risk adjustment (HCC mapping), and medical billing. Sourced from Epic ClinDoc and validated through 3M HIS coding workflows. Conforms to WHO ICD-10-CM code format.
attributes.references: WHO ICD-10-CM; CMS ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines; 3M HIS Grouping; AMA

attributes.name: icd10_description
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Diagnosis Description
attributes.description: Full clinical description of the ICD-10-CM diagnosis code as defined by the WHO/CMS code set. Provides human-readable context for the coded diagnosis. Used in clinical documentation, reporting, and CDI workflows.
attributes.references: WHO ICD-10-CM; CMS ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines; 3M HIS

attributes.name: icd10_version
attributes.description: The fiscal year version of the ICD-10-CM code set used to assign this diagnosis code (e.g., FY2024). ICD-10-CM is updated annually by CMS/CDC. Ensures accurate code interpretation across fiscal year transitions and supports historical data analysis.
attributes.references: CMS ICD-10-CM Annual Updates; CDC ICD-10-CM Tabular List; WHO ICD-10

attributes.name: mental_health_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this diagnosis is classified as a mental health or behavioral health condition per ICD-10-CM Chapter 5 (F-codes). True = mental/behavioral health diagnosis. Supports behavioral health program management, parity compliance reporting, and population health segmentation.
attributes.references: ICD-10-CM Chapter 5 Mental and Behavioral Disorders; Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA); CMS Behavioral Health Strategy

attributes.name: onset_date
attributes.description: The date on which the diagnosed condition first manifested or was first identified, as documented in the clinical record. Supports longitudinal disease tracking, chronic condition management, POA determination, and population health analytics. Aligns with BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP canonical category.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Condition.onset; Epic ClinDoc; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: poa_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the diagnosis condition was present at the time of inpatient admission. Values: Y=Yes (present on admission), N=No (not present on admission), U=Unknown, W=Clinically undetermined, 1=Exempt from POA reporting. Required by CMS for inpatient claims on UB-04. Impacts HAI reporting, VBP penalties, and hospital-acquired condition (HAC) payment adjustments.
attributes.references: CMS POA Reporting Guidelines; UB-04 FL 67 POA Indicator; IPPS HAC Reduction Program; The Joint Commission HAI Standards

attributes.name: primary_diagnosis_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this diagnosis is designated as the primary/principal diagnosis for the encounter. True = primary diagnosis. Provides a quick boolean filter for analytics and reporting without requiring sequence number logic. Complements diagnosis_seq_num and diagnosis_type.
attributes.references: CMS UHDDS Principal Diagnosis Definition; UB-04 FL 67; AHIMA Coding Guidelines

attributes.name: quality_measure_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this diagnosis contributes to one or more quality measure denominators or numerators (e.g., HEDIS, MIPS, VBP, TJC core measures). True = this diagnosis is relevant to at least one active quality measure. Supports quality reporting, MIPS scoring, and VBP program management.
attributes.references: NCQA HEDIS; CMS MIPS; CMS VBP Program; The Joint Commission Core Measures; MACRA

attributes.name: reportable_condition_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this diagnosis is a notifiable/reportable condition requiring mandatory reporting to public health authorities (e.g., state health departments, CDC). True = reportable. Supports public health surveillance, regulatory compliance, and HIE reporting obligations.
attributes.references: State Departments of Health Reportable Disease Lists; CDC National Notifiable Diseases; HIPAA Public Health Disclosure Exception 45 CFR §164.512(b)

attributes.name: resolved_date
attributes.description: The date on which the diagnosed condition was resolved, abated, or no longer active, as documented in the clinical record. Null if the condition is ongoing. Used for chronic disease management, care plan updates, and longitudinal patient health tracking.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Condition.abatement; Epic ClinDoc; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: sdoh_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this diagnosis code represents a Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) factor (e.g., Z-codes for housing instability, food insecurity, transportation barriers). True = SDOH-related diagnosis. Supports population health management, care coordination, and CMS SDOH reporting initiatives.
attributes.references: CMS SDOH Strategy; ICD-10-CM Z-Codes for SDOH; AHRQ SDOH Framework; Healthy People 2030

attributes.name: snomed_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) Code
attributes.description: The SNOMED CT concept identifier mapped to this ICD-10-CM diagnosis code. Supports clinical interoperability, HL7 FHIR-based HIE data exchange, and clinical decision support. Populated via ICD-10 to SNOMED CT crosswalk. Used in FHIR Condition resources for interoperability.
attributes.references: SNOMED International; HL7 FHIR R4 Condition.code; NLM SNOMED CT US Edition; HHS Interoperability Rule

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this visit diagnosis record was sourced. Supports data lineage, ETL audit, and multi-system reconciliation in the Silver lakehouse layer.
attributes.references: HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; Epic ClinDoc; Cerner Millennium; 3M HIS

attributes.name: substance_use_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this diagnosis represents a substance use disorder (SUD) per ICD-10-CM codes. True = substance use disorder diagnosis. Supports SUD program management, 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality compliance, and population health analytics.
attributes.references: ICD-10-CM SUD Codes; 42 CFR Part 2 (Confidentiality of SUD Records); SAMHSA; CMS Opioid Strategy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this visit diagnosis record was last modified in the source system or Silver layer. Supports change data capture, audit trail, and RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED canonical category requirement.
attributes.references: HIPAA Audit Controls 45 CFR §164.312(b); HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; SOC 2

products.name: visit_procedure
products.description: Encounter-level procedure record capturing all procedures performed during a visit. Includes CPT/HCPCS procedure code, ICD-10-PCS code (for inpatient), procedure description, procedure date and time, performing provider NPI, procedure sequence number, principal procedure flag, laterality, anesthesia type, and OR/procedure room reference. Supports charge capture, DRG grouping, quality measurement, and surgical case tracking. Sourced from Epic OpTime, ClinDoc, and Cerner SurgiNet.
products.reference: CPT / HCPCS / ICD-10-PCS

attributes.name: visit_procedure_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each procedure record performed during a patient visit. Primary key for the visit_procedure data product in the encounter domain.

attributes.name: audit_finding_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_finding. Business justification: Procedure coding audit findings (unbundling, medical necessity, modifier errors, upcoding) must reference the specific procedure record being challenged. Enables direct linkage from compliance finding

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Procedures are performed in specific departments/cost centers. Essential for activity-based costing, OR suite profitability analysis, procedural revenue tracking, and CPT-based cost allocation for dep

attributes.name: cpt_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.cpt_code. Business justification: Essential procedure coding workflow—every CPT code on a visit procedure must validate against the official CPT reference for claims submission, reimbursement calculation, RVU assignment, and NCCI edit

attributes.name: hcpcs_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.hcpcs_code. Business justification: Required for HCPCS procedure coding—DME, supplies, drugs, and non-physician services must reference official HCPCS codes for billing, coverage determination, and reimbursement. Critical for outpatient

attributes.name: icd_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.icd_code. Business justification: Inpatient procedure coding workflow—ICD-10-PCS codes must validate against the official ICD-10 code set for inpatient claims submission, DRG grouping, and quality measure reporting. Required for hospi

attributes.name: interventional_procedure_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to radiology.interventional_procedure. Business justification: Interventional radiology procedures (biopsies, drainages, embolizations) are billable encounter procedures requiring linkage for charge capture, procedural documentation, and outcomes tracking. IR pro

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Procedures consume specific supplies, devices, and implants that must be documented for billing (CDM charge codes), regulatory compliance (UDI tracking for implantables), and procedure cost analysis.

attributes.name: mpi_record_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient on whom the procedure was performed. Supports patient-level procedure history, quality measurement, and population health analytics.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR R4 Patient Resource; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: or_suite_id
attributes.description: Reference to the operating room or procedure room where the procedure was performed. Supports OR utilization reporting, room turnover analysis, and facility capacity planning.
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission Environment of Care Standards

attributes.name: primary_visit_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinician who performed the procedure. Used for provider-level quality reporting, credentialing validation, and RVU attribution.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; HL7 FHIR R4 Practitioner Resource; MIPS/MACRA Reporting

attributes.name: privileging_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to provider.privileging. Business justification: Enables retrospective verification that performing clinician held valid privileges for the specific procedure at the facility on the procedure date. Required for peer review, quality assurance audits,

attributes.name: research_study_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to research.research_study. Business justification: Research billing requires distinguishing study-mandated procedures from standard-of-care for coverage analysis and sponsor billing. Protocol compliance monitoring needs to verify required procedures w

attributes.name: snomed_concept_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.snomed_concept. Business justification: Procedure terminology mapping—SNOMED codes on procedures must reference official SNOMED CT for clinical documentation, interoperability, and data exchange with external systems. Required for USCDI com

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent encounter/visit during which this procedure was performed. Links the procedure to the ADT event, visit type, and associated clinical and billing context.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter Resource; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet

attributes.name: anesthesia_type
attributes.description: Type of anesthesia administered during the procedure. Drives anesthesia CPT code selection, anesthesia time unit billing, ASA physical status documentation, and OR case complexity classification.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Anesthesia Guidelines; ASA Physical Status Classification; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet

attributes.name: asa_class
attributes.business_glossary_term: American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Physical Status Classification
attributes.description: ASA physical status classification assigned by the anesthesiologist prior to the procedure, reflecting the patient's overall health status. Used for anesthesia risk stratification, surgical case complexity scoring, and outcomes risk adjustment.
attributes.references: ASA Physical Status Classification System; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; AHRQ Risk Adjustment

attributes.name: body_site
attributes.description: Anatomical location or body site where the procedure was performed, coded using SNOMED CT body structure concepts. Supports surgical safety documentation, quality measure stratification, and clinical analytics.
attributes.references: SNOMED CT Body Structure Hierarchy; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.bodySite; The Joint Commission Universal Protocol

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Reason code or description explaining why a scheduled procedure was cancelled (e.g., patient not ready, equipment unavailable, surgeon unavailable, insurance denial). Populated only when is_cancelled is true. Supports root cause analysis and OR efficiency improvement.
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission OR Performance Metrics

attributes.name: charge_amount
attributes.description: Gross charge amount posted to the patient account for this procedure based on the CDM. Represents the billed amount before contractual adjustments, payer discounts, or patient responsibility. Used in revenue cycle management and financial reporting.
attributes.references: CMS CDM; Epic Resolute HB/PB; Cerner Revenue Cycle; GAAP/FASB Revenue Recognition

attributes.name: charge_code
attributes.description: Internal charge code from the Charge Description Master (CDM) mapped to this procedure. Links the clinical procedure to the revenue cycle for charge capture, pricing, and claim generation in Epic Resolute or Cerner Revenue Cycle.
attributes.references: CMS CDM Requirements; Epic Resolute HB/PB; Cerner Revenue Cycle; OIG Compliance Guidance

attributes.name: complication_description
attributes.description: Free-text or coded description of the complication that occurred during or after the procedure. Populated only when complication_flag is true. Used for clinical documentation, quality review, and risk management reporting.
attributes.references: AHRQ PSI; CMS VBP; CDC NHSN; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.complication

attributes.name: complication_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a complication was documented as occurring during or immediately following the procedure. Triggers CDI query workflow, quality event review, and HAI/PSI surveillance reporting.
attributes.references: AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators (PSI); CMS VBP; CDC NHSN; The Joint Commission

attributes.name: consent_obtained_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether informed consent was documented as obtained from the patient or legal guardian prior to the procedure. Required for regulatory compliance, malpractice risk management, and The Joint Commission accreditation standards.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.13; EMTALA

attributes.name: cpt_code
attributes.description: AMA CPT code identifying the procedure for professional billing, charge capture, and payer adjudication. Required on CMS-1500 claims. Drives RVU calculation and reimbursement.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Coding Standards; CMS-1500; CMS Physician Fee Schedule

attributes.name: cpt_modifier_1
attributes.description: Primary CPT modifier appended to the procedure code to indicate special circumstances (e.g., 50=bilateral, LT=left side, RT=right side, 22=increased procedural services, 59=distinct procedural service). Required for accurate claim adjudication.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Modifier Guidelines; CMS-1500; CMS Correct Coding Initiative (CCI)

attributes.name: cpt_modifier_2
attributes.description: Secondary CPT modifier providing additional claim specificity when a single modifier is insufficient. Used in conjunction with cpt_modifier_1 for complex billing scenarios per CMS Correct Coding Initiative.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Modifier Guidelines; CMS-1500; CMS Correct Coding Initiative (CCI)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this procedure record was first created in the source system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and regulatory compliance documentation per HIPAA and The Joint Commission medical record requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; The Joint Commission MR.01.01.01; ISO 27001

attributes.name: drg_relevant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this procedure influences the DRG assignment for the inpatient encounter. Flagged by the 3M grouper or equivalent DRG grouping engine. Critical for inpatient revenue integrity and CDI prioritization.
attributes.references: CMS IPPS DRG Grouping; 3M Health Information Systems Grouping; CMS MS-DRG Definitions Manual

attributes.name: hcpcs_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Code
attributes.description: HCPCS Level II code used when a CPT code is not applicable, primarily for supplies, durable medical equipment, and non-physician services billed to Medicare/Medicaid. Complements CPT on UB-04 and CMS-1500 claims.
attributes.references: CMS HCPCS Coding; UB-04; CMS-1500; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: icd10_pcs_code
attributes.description: ICD-10-PCS code assigned for inpatient procedures. Required for inpatient DRG grouping, UB-04 institutional claims, and CMS inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS) reimbursement. Not applicable for outpatient encounters.
attributes.references: WHO ICD-10-PCS; CMS IPPS; UB-04; 3M Health Information Systems Grouping

attributes.name: implant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a medical device or implant was used during the procedure. Triggers UDI (Unique Device Identifier) documentation requirements per FDA regulations and supply chain charge capture workflows.
attributes.references: FDA UDI Rule 21 CFR Part 830; The Joint Commission; CMS Conditions of Participation; Infor Lawson Supply Chain

attributes.name: is_cancelled
attributes.description: Indicates whether a scheduled procedure was cancelled before execution. Used for OR cancellation rate reporting, scheduling efficiency analysis, and revenue impact assessment.
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission OR Performance Metrics

attributes.name: is_elective
attributes.description: Indicates whether the procedure was scheduled as elective (non-urgent) versus emergent or urgent. Supports surgical scheduling analytics, OR block time management, and payer prior authorization workflows.
attributes.references: CMS Elective Surgery Definitions; Epic Cadence; Cerner SurgiNet Scheduling

attributes.name: is_principal_procedure
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is the principal procedure performed for the encounter, as defined by the Uniform Hospital Discharge Data Set (UHDDS). The principal procedure is the one most closely related to the principal diagnosis and drives DRG assignment for inpatient cases.
attributes.references: CMS UHDDS; CMS IPPS; UB-04 FL 74; 3M Health Information Systems Grouping

attributes.name: laterality
attributes.description: Body side on which the procedure was performed. Required for correct CPT modifier assignment (RT/LT/50), surgical safety checklists, and wrong-site surgery prevention per The Joint Commission Universal Protocol.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Modifiers RT/LT/50; The Joint Commission Universal Protocol; CMS-1500; UB-04

attributes.name: performing_provider_npi
attributes.description: 10-digit NPI of the performing provider as required on CMS-1500 and UB-04 claims. Stored denormalized here for claim generation and audit purposes, as the NPI is a regulatory billing requirement independent of the provider master record.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; CMS-1500 Box 24J; UB-04 FL 56; HIPAA

attributes.name: procedure_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the procedure was performed. Used for charge capture date-of-service, quality measure denominator identification, and surgical case scheduling analytics.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.performed[x]; AMA CPT

attributes.name: procedure_description
attributes.description: Full clinical description of the procedure as documented in the source system (Epic ClinDoc, OpTime, or Cerner SurgiNet). Provides human-readable context for the CPT/HCPCS/ICD-10-PCS code.
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.code.text

attributes.name: procedure_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the procedure was completed (closure for surgical cases, or final clinical action for non-surgical). Combined with start timestamp to derive procedure duration for OR utilization and case costing.
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission OR Metrics

attributes.name: procedure_number
attributes.description: Externally visible, human-readable identifier assigned to this procedure record within the source system (e.g., Epic OpTime case number or Cerner SurgiNet procedure order number). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit.
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.identifier

attributes.name: procedure_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the procedure began (knife-to-skin for surgical cases, or first clinical action for non-surgical). Used for OR utilization analysis, case duration calculation, and scheduling efficiency reporting.
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; The Joint Commission OR Metrics

attributes.name: procedure_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the procedure record per HL7 FHIR Procedure.status value set. Drives charge capture eligibility, quality measure inclusion/exclusion, and CDI workflow routing.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.status; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet

attributes.name: procedure_type
attributes.description: High-level classification of the procedure category. Supports operational reporting, OR scheduling, charge master (CDM) mapping, and departmental cost allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: surgical|diagnostic|therapeutic|anesthesia|radiology|laboratory|nursing|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet; CMS CDM; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.category

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: Number of times this procedure was performed or units billed within the encounter. Used for charge capture accuracy, claim line quantity reporting, and utilization analysis.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Billing Guidelines; CMS-1500 Box 24G; UB-04 FL 46

attributes.name: rvu_total
attributes.description: Total RVU for the procedure, comprising work RVU, practice expense RVU, and malpractice RVU components per the CMS Physician Fee Schedule. Used for overall provider productivity benchmarking and reimbursement modeling.
attributes.references: CMS Physician Fee Schedule; MACRA/MIPS; AMA RVU Update Committee (RUC)

attributes.name: rvu_work
attributes.description: Physician work RVU assigned to this procedure per the CMS Physician Fee Schedule. Represents the time, skill, and intensity of the physician's work. Used for provider productivity measurement, compensation modeling, and MIPS performance reporting.
attributes.references: CMS Physician Fee Schedule; MACRA/MIPS; AMA RVU Update Committee (RUC)

attributes.name: sequence_number
attributes.description: Ordinal position of this procedure within the encounter, used to distinguish principal from secondary procedures on claims. Sequence 1 typically denotes the principal procedure for DRG grouping and IPPS reimbursement.
attributes.references: CMS IPPS DRG Grouping; UB-04 FL 74; 3M Health Information Systems Grouping

attributes.name: snomed_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) Procedure Code
attributes.description: SNOMED CT concept identifier for the procedure, providing a clinically precise, interoperable representation beyond CPT/ICD-10-PCS. Supports HIE data exchange, FHIR-based interoperability, and clinical decision support.
attributes.references: SNOMED International; HL7 FHIR R4 Procedure.code; ONC Interoperability Rule

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this procedure record was sourced. Supports data lineage, ETL reconciliation, and audit traceability across Epic OpTime, Epic ClinDoc, Cerner SurgiNet, and other source systems.
attributes.references: HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; NIST Cybersecurity Framework; HL7 FHIR R4 Provenance Resource

attributes.name: source_system_procedure_code
attributes.description: Native identifier of this procedure record in the originating source system (e.g., Epic OpTime case ID, Cerner SurgiNet order ID). Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational EHR system.
attributes.references: HITRUST CSF; HL7 FHIR R4 Provenance Resource; Epic OpTime; Cerner SurgiNet

attributes.name: surgical_approach

attributes.description: Room number assigned to the patient at the time of this status change. Relevant for bed assignment, transfer, and discharge events. Supports bed management and capacity planning.
attributes.references: Epic ADT; Cerner Millennium ADT; Joint Commission EC.02.06.01

attributes.name: sequence_number
attributes.description: Ordinal sequence number of this status change event within the visit lifecycle, starting at 1. Enables chronological ordering of status transitions for a given visit without relying solely on timestamps.
attributes.references: HL7 ADT Event Sequencing; Epic ADT; Cerner Millennium ADT

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record that originated this status change event (e.g., Epic ADT, Cerner Millennium ADT, MEDITECH Expanse, manual entry, HL7 interface). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Provenance Resource; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: source_system_event_code
attributes.description: The native event or transaction identifier from the originating source system (e.g., Epic ADT event ID, Cerner Millennium event ID). Used for cross-system reconciliation, deduplication, and ETL lineage tracking.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Provenance Resource; Epic ADT; Cerner Millennium ADT; HITRUST CSF

attributes.name: status_change_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded narrative reason entered by the user or system explaining why the visit status was changed (e.g., 'Patient arrived at ED triage', 'Bed assigned in ICU', 'Patient left without being seen'). Supports operational workflow auditing.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; Epic ADT; Cerner Millennium ADT

attributes.name: status_change_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the visit status transition occurred. Principal event timestamp for this record. Used for LOS milestone tracking, throughput analysis, and ADT event sequencing.
attributes.references: HL7 ADT A01-A08 MSH-7 Message Date/Time; Epic ADT; Cerner Millennium ADT; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this visit status history record was last modified in the data platform. Used for incremental ETL processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) Audit Controls; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF

products.name: triage_assessment
products.description: ED and urgent care triage assessment record capturing triage acuity level (ESI 1-5), chief complaint, triage timestamp, triage nurse NPI, vital signs at triage (BP, HR, RR, temp, SpO2, pain score), mode of arrival (ambulance, walk-in, helicopter, police), triage category (emergent, urgent, semi-urgent, non-urgent), and LWBS (Left Without Being Seen) flag. Supports ED throughput metrics, door-to-provider time quality measures, and EMTALA compliance. Sourced from Epic ClinDoc ED module and Cerner PowerChart ED.
products.reference: ESI Triage Algorithm / ACEP Triage Guidelines

attributes.name: triage_assessment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the triage assessment record in the Silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the facility (ED or urgent care location) where the triage assessment was conducted. Supports multi-site throughput and capacity analytics.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; Joint Commission EC Standards

attributes.name: clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the licensed nurse or clinician who performed the triage assessment. Used for accountability, staffing analytics, and EMTALA compliance tracking.
attributes.references: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: mpi_record_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient who was triaged. Core party reference linking the triage assessment to the Master Patient Index (MPI).
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Patient Resource; HIPAA 45 CFR §164

attributes.name: osha_exposure_incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.osha_exposure_incident. Business justification: Exposure incidents in ED/triage settings (needlesticks, blood/body fluid exposure) require linkage to the triage encounter for root cause analysis, source patient testing coordination, and OSHA 300 lo

attributes.name: prior_triage_assessment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original triage assessment record when this record is a reassessment. Enables linkage of reassessment chains for acuity escalation tracking and waiting room safety analytics.
attributes.references: Joint Commission NPSG; Epic ClinDoc ED Module; Cerner PowerChart ED

attributes.name: triage_nurse_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Triage nurses are often RNs tracked in workforce (not provider domain). Required for ED staffing models, competency validation (ESI certification), and labor productivity. Complements existing clinici

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent Emergency Department (ED) or urgent care encounter for which this triage assessment was performed. Links triage to the broader encounter lifecycle.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter Resource; Epic ClinDoc ED Module

attributes.name: acuity_change_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or structured reason documented by the triage nurse when the ESI acuity level is changed during a reassessment. PHI under HIPAA. Used for clinical quality review and patient safety event analysis.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; Joint Commission NPSG; AHRQ ED Safety Guidelines

attributes.name: ama_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient left the ED Against Medical Advice (AMA) after triage but before completing the full ED visit. Distinct from LWBS — AMA occurs after provider contact. Used for risk management, quality reporting, and EMTALA compliance.
attributes.references: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; Joint Commission; CMS Conditions of Participation; AMA Policy

attributes.name: arrival_mode
attributes.description: Method by which the patient arrived at the ED or urgent care facility. Includes ground ambulance, air transport (helicopter), walk-in, police transport, private vehicle, or inter-facility transfer. Used for EMTALA compliance, acuity benchmarking, and EMS coordination analytics.
attributes.references: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; UB-04 FL 38; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: chief_complaint
attributes.description: Free-text or structured description of the patient's primary reason for presenting to the ED or urgent care, as stated by the patient or documented by the triage nurse. Protected Health Information (PHI) under HIPAA. Used for clinical documentation, coding, and population health analytics.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter.reasonCode; ICD-10-CM Guidelines

attributes.name: chief_complaint_code
attributes.description: Standardized SNOMED CT (Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms) code representing the chief complaint. Enables structured clinical analytics, interoperability, and population health reporting across systems.
attributes.references: SNOMED CT International Edition; HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter.reasonCode; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: diastolic_bp_mmhg
attributes.description: Diastolic blood pressure measurement recorded at triage, expressed in millimeters of mercury (mmHg). Used alongside systolic BP for hemodynamic assessment and ESI acuity scoring. PHI under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; LOINC 8462-4; Joint Commission NPSG; AHA Clinical Guidelines

attributes.name: door_arrival_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time the patient physically arrived at the ED or urgent care facility (door time). Used as the baseline for door-to-triage and door-to-provider time quality measures reported to CMS.
attributes.references: CMS ED Throughput Quality Measures; EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; Joint Commission

attributes.name: esi_level
attributes.description: Emergency Severity Index (ESI) triage acuity score assigned by the triage nurse, ranging from 1 (most critical/immediate) to 5 (least urgent/non-urgent). Drives resource allocation, bed assignment priority, and ED throughput analytics. Defined by AHRQ ESI Triage Algorithm.
attributes.references: AHRQ ESI Triage Algorithm v4; CMS ED Quality Measures; Joint Commission

attributes.name: glasgow_coma_score
attributes.description: Total Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score assessed at triage, ranging from 3 (deep unconsciousness) to 15 (fully alert). Used for neurological status assessment, ESI acuity determination, and trauma triage protocols. PHI under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; LOINC 35088-4; AHRQ ESI Triage Algorithm v4; ACS Trauma Guidelines

attributes.name: heart_rate_bpm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Heart Rate (HR) in Beats Per Minute (BPM)
attributes.description: Heart rate (pulse) measured at triage, expressed in beats per minute (BPM). Key vital sign for ESI acuity determination and identification of hemodynamic instability. PHI under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; LOINC 8867-4; AHRQ ESI Triage Algorithm v4

attributes.name: interpreter_language
attributes.description: Primary language for which interpretation services are required, using ISO 639-1 two-letter language codes (e.g., 'es' for Spanish, 'zh' for Chinese). Supports LEP compliance reporting and interpreter resource planning.
attributes.references: ISO 639-1; CMS LEP Policy; Title VI Civil Rights Act; HHS Office for Civil Rights

attributes.name: interpreter_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient requires language interpretation services during the triage assessment. Supports compliance with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act and CMS Limited English Proficiency (LEP) requirements.
attributes.references: Title VI Civil Rights Act; CMS LEP Policy; Joint Commission RI Standards; HHS Office for Civil Rights

attributes.name: isolation_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient requires isolation precautions at triage (e.g., airborne, droplet, contact, or neutropenic precautions). Drives bed assignment workflows, infection control protocols, and Healthcare-Associated Infection (HAI) prevention measures.
attributes.references: CDC Isolation Precautions Guidelines; Joint Commission IC Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation; OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard

attributes.name: isolation_type
attributes.description: Type of isolation precaution required for the patient as determined at triage. Drives room assignment, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and infection control workflows.
attributes.references: CDC Isolation Precautions Guidelines 2007; Joint Commission IC Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: lwbs_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient left the ED without being seen by a provider after triage (LWBS). Key ED throughput quality metric reported to CMS and used for EMTALA compliance monitoring and operational improvement initiatives.
attributes.references: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; CMS ED Throughput Quality Measures; Joint Commission; AHRQ

attributes.name: lwbs_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time the patient departed the ED without being seen by a provider, when the LWBS flag is true. Used to calculate time-to-LWBS and identify peak demand periods contributing to patient walkouts.
attributes.references: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; CMS ED Throughput Quality Measures; Joint Commission

attributes.name: mental_health_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient's chief complaint or triage assessment involves a primary mental health or behavioral health concern. Used for ED behavioral health throughput analytics, psychiatric bed management, and EMTALA psychiatric screening compliance.
attributes.references: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; CMS Behavioral Health Integration; Joint Commission BHC Standards; SAMHSA

attributes.name: pain_scale_type
attributes.description: Type of validated pain assessment scale used to obtain the pain score at triage. Distinguishes between numeric rating scale (NRS), Wong-Baker FACES (pediatric), FLACC (non-verbal), verbal descriptor, or behavioral observation scales.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Pain Management Standards; AHRQ; Epic ClinDoc ED Module

attributes.name: pain_score
attributes.description: Patient-reported pain intensity score at triage, typically on a 0–10 numeric rating scale (NRS) or equivalent validated scale (e.g., Wong-Baker FACES for pediatric patients). Used for ESI acuity determination and Joint Commission pain management compliance. PHI under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; LOINC 72514-3; Joint Commission Pain Management Standards; AHRQ ESI Triage Algorithm v4

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this triage assessment record was first created in the source system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF; Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this triage assessment record was most recently modified in the source system. Used for change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF; Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: respiratory_rate_bpm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Respiratory Rate (RR) in Breaths Per Minute
attributes.description: Respiratory rate measured at triage, expressed in breaths per minute. Used for ESI acuity scoring and identification of respiratory distress. PHI under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; LOINC 9279-1; AHRQ ESI Triage Algorithm v4

attributes.name: sepsis_alert_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a sepsis screening alert was triggered at triage based on vital signs and clinical criteria (e.g., SIRS criteria, qSOFA). Supports SEP-1 bundle compliance reporting to CMS and Joint Commission sepsis quality measures.
attributes.references: CMS SEP-1 Quality Measure; Joint Commission Sepsis Standards; Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines; AHRQ

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this triage assessment record was sourced. Supports data lineage, ETL audit, and multi-system reconciliation in the Silver layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: Native record identifier from the originating operational system (Epic ClinDoc or Cerner PowerChart ED) for this triage assessment. Enables cross-system traceability and supports Health Information Exchange (HIE) reconciliation.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; HL7 FHIR R4 Identifier; HITRUST CSF

attributes.name: spo2_percent
attributes.description: Peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) measured by pulse oximetry at triage, expressed as a percentage. Critical indicator for respiratory status and ESI acuity level assignment. PHI under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; LOINC 59408-5; AHRQ ESI Triage Algorithm v4; Joint Commission NPSG

attributes.name: stroke_alert_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a stroke alert protocol was activated at triage based on presenting symptoms (e.g., FAST criteria). Supports door-to-CT and door-to-needle time quality measures for stroke care reported to The Joint Commission and CMS.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Stroke Certification Standards; CMS Stroke Quality Measures; AHA/ASA Stroke Guidelines

attributes.name: systolic_bp_mmhg
attributes.description: Systolic blood pressure measurement recorded at triage, expressed in millimeters of mercury (mmHg). Critical vital sign for ESI acuity determination and clinical decision support. PHI under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; LOINC 8480-6; Joint Commission NPSG; AHA Clinical Guidelines

attributes.name: temperature_celsius
attributes.description: Body temperature measured at triage, expressed in degrees Celsius. Used for ESI acuity determination, sepsis screening, and infection surveillance. PHI under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; LOINC 8310-5; AHRQ ESI Triage Algorithm v4; CDC Sepsis Guidelines

attributes.name: temperature_route
attributes.description: Anatomical route used to obtain the body temperature measurement at triage (e.g., oral, rectal, axillary, tympanic, temporal). Affects clinical interpretation of temperature values.
attributes.references: LOINC 8327-9; Epic ClinDoc ED Module; Cerner PowerChart ED

attributes.name: trauma_activation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a trauma team activation was initiated at or following triage. Used for trauma registry reporting, ACS trauma center verification, and ED resource utilization analytics.
attributes.references: ACS Committee on Trauma; Joint Commission Trauma Standards; State Trauma Registry Requirements

attributes.name: trauma_level
attributes.description: Level of trauma team activation triggered at triage (Level 1 = full activation for most critical injuries, Level 2 = partial activation, Level 3 = consult/standby). Drives resource deployment and trauma registry classification.
attributes.references: ACS Committee on Trauma; State Trauma Registry Requirements; Joint Commission Trauma Standards

attributes.name: triage_category
attributes.description: Categorical classification of triage acuity corresponding to the ESI level. Supports ED throughput reporting, staffing models, and payer analytics. Values align with standard ED triage nomenclature.
attributes.references: AHRQ ESI Triage Algorithm; CMS ED Throughput Measures; Joint Commission

attributes.name: triage_completed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the triage assessment was fully documented and completed by the triage nurse. Used to calculate triage duration and nurse productivity metrics.
attributes.references: Epic ClinDoc ED Module; CMS ED Throughput Measures

attributes.name: triage_number
attributes.description: Externally visible, human-readable identifier for the triage assessment record as assigned by the source system (Epic ClinDoc or Cerner PowerChart ED). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trails.
attributes.references: Epic ClinDoc ED Module; Cerner PowerChart ED

attributes.name: triage_nurse_npi
attributes.description: National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the licensed nurse or clinician who performed the triage assessment. Required for EMTALA compliance documentation and provider-level quality reporting. Sourced from Epic ClinDoc or Cerner PowerChart ED.
attributes.references: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; HIPAA NPI Final Rule 45 CFR §162.406; CMS NPI Registry

attributes.name: triage_reassessment_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this triage record represents a reassessment of a previously triaged patient (e.g., patient condition changed while waiting). Supports tracking of acuity escalation events and waiting room safety monitoring.
attributes.references: Joint Commission NPSG; AHRQ ED Safety Guidelines; Epic ClinDoc ED Module

attributes.name: triage_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the triage assessment record. Indicates whether triage documentation is in progress, finalized, subsequently amended, or voided.
attributes.references: Epic ClinDoc ED Module; HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter.status

attributes.name: triage_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the triage assessment was initiated by the triage nurse. This is the principal business event timestamp used to calculate door-to-triage time and ED throughput quality measures.
attributes.references: CMS ED Throughput Quality Measures; EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; Joint Commission NPSG

attributes.name: weight_kg
attributes.description: Patient weight measured or reported at triage, expressed in kilograms. Used for medication dosing calculations, pediatric weight-based protocols, and clinical decision support. PHI under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; LOINC 29463-7; Joint Commission Medication Management Standards

products.name: readmission
products.description: Readmission tracking record linking an index (original) encounter to a subsequent readmission encounter within a defined time window (7, 30, 90 days). Captures index visit FK, readmission visit FK, days between discharge and readmission, readmission type (planned, unplanned), readmission diagnosis ICD-10, CMS readmission measure category (HRRP — Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program), preventability assessment, root cause category, and care gap identified. Supports CMS HRRP penalty avoidance, quality reporting, care management program targeting, and post-discharge intervention effectiveness analysis.
products.reference: CMS HRRP / Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program

attributes.name: readmission_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the readmission tracking record linking an index encounter to a subsequent readmission encounter.
attributes.references: CMS Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP); HL7 FHIR Encounter Resource

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the facility where the readmission encounter occurred. Supports facility-level HRRP penalty calculation and Joint Commission reporting.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; The Joint Commission; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: clinician_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the attending physician responsible for the readmission encounter. Used for provider-level quality reporting and MIPS performance attribution.
attributes.references: CMS MIPS; NPI Registry; HL7 FHIR Practitioner Resource

attributes.name: compliance_regulatory_submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_submission. Business justification: Readmission data is directly submitted to CMS for Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP) penalty calculation. Specific readmission records are referenced in regulatory submissions. Core CMS qu

attributes.name: demographics_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the patient record. Links the readmission pair to the Master Patient Index (MPI) for population health analytics and care management targeting.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; CMS HRRP; HL7 FHIR Patient Resource

attributes.name: index_drg_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.drg. Business justification: Readmission tracking—index admission DRG must reference official DRG definition for HRRP penalty calculation, excess readmission ratio reporting, and quality measure validation. Required for CMS readm

attributes.name: payer_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the payer (insurance plan) responsible for the index encounter. Used to segment readmission rates by payer for value-based contract performance reporting and ACO/HMO/PPO analytics.

attributes.name: readmission_encounter_visit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the subsequent encounter that qualifies as a readmission within the defined time window following the index discharge.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; HL7 FHIR Encounter Resource

attributes.name: readmission_visit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the original (index) inpatient encounter from which the readmission window is measured. The index encounter is the hospitalization that preceded the readmission.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines; HL7 FHIR Encounter Resource

attributes.name: aco_attributed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient was attributed to an Accountable Care Organization (ACO) at the time of the index encounter. ACO-attributed readmissions have direct financial implications under shared savings and risk-based contracts.

attributes.name: admission_date
attributes.description: Date the patient was admitted for the readmission encounter. Used to calculate days between discharge and readmission and to determine which time-window cohort (7, 30, 90 days) the readmission falls into.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; UB-04 Form Locator 12; HL7 ADT A01

attributes.name: admit_source
attributes.description: Source through which the patient was admitted for the readmission encounter (e.g., Emergency Department, physician referral, transfer from another facility). Supports analysis of care transition failure points.
attributes.references: UB-04 Form Locator 15; HL7 ADT A01; CMS HRRP

attributes.name: care_gap_identified
attributes.description: Specific care gap identified during readmission review that contributed to the readmission event. Used to drive post-discharge intervention program design and care management outreach. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: no_follow_up_appointment|medication_reconciliation_gap|no_discharge_instructions|no_post_acute_referral|no_care_gap — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NCQA HEDIS; CMS HRRP; AHRQ Care Transitions; The Joint Commission

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this readmission tracking record was first created in the system, typically triggered by the ADT discharge event or quality review workflow initiation.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR AuditEvent; ISO 8601; HIPAA Audit Controls 45 CFR §164.312

attributes.name: days_to_readmission
attributes.description: Number of calendar days elapsed between the index discharge date and the readmission admission date. Core metric for HRRP cohort assignment and post-discharge intervention effectiveness analysis.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; AHRQ Quality Indicators; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: drg_code
attributes.description: MS-DRG code assigned to the readmission encounter by the grouper. Used for financial impact analysis of readmissions on reimbursement and for HRRP penalty cost modeling.
attributes.references: CMS MS-DRG Grouper; 3M Health Information Systems; CMS IPPS

attributes.name: estimated_penalty_amount
attributes.description: Estimated financial penalty amount (in USD) attributable to this readmission under the CMS Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program. Used for revenue cycle impact analysis and CFO-level financial reporting. Confidential business financial data.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; 42 CFR §412.154; GAAP; FASB ASC 954

attributes.name: follow_up_appointment_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date of the first post-discharge follow-up appointment after the index encounter. Used to assess timeliness of follow-up care and its correlation with readmission prevention.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; NCQA HEDIS Transitions of Care; Epic Cadence

attributes.name: follow_up_appointment_scheduled
attributes.description: Indicates whether a follow-up outpatient appointment was scheduled prior to or at the time of index discharge. A key care gap indicator; absence is associated with higher 30-day readmission risk.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; NCQA HEDIS; The Joint Commission Transitions of Care

attributes.name: hrrp_excess_readmission_ratio
attributes.business_glossary_term: Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP) Excess Readmission Ratio
attributes.description: CMS-calculated ratio of predicted to expected readmissions for the applicable HRRP measure category. A ratio greater than 1.0 indicates excess readmissions subject to payment penalty. Sourced from CMS IPPS final rule calculations.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; 42 CFR §412.154; CMS IPPS Final Rule

attributes.name: hrrp_measure_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP) Measure Category
attributes.description: CMS HRRP condition-specific measure category assigned to the readmission. AMI=Acute Myocardial Infarction, HF=Heart Failure, PN=Pneumonia, COPD=Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, THA_TKA=Total Hip/Knee Arthroplasty, CABG=Coronary Artery Bypass Graft, other=does not fall under a specific HRRP measure. Drives CMS penalty calculation and quality reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: AMI|HF|PN|COPD|THA_TKA|CABG|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; 42 CFR §412.154; CMS Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS)

attributes.name: index_discharge_date
attributes.description: Date the patient was discharged from the index (original) inpatient encounter. Serves as the start of the readmission measurement window per CMS HRRP methodology.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; UB-04 Form Locator 16; ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines

attributes.name: index_discharge_disposition
attributes.description: Discharge disposition code from the index encounter indicating where the patient was discharged to. Critical for identifying post-acute care failures as a readmission root cause and for HRRP exclusion logic (e.g., AMA, expired). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: home|home_health|snf|ltach|rehab|hospice|ama|expired — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: UB-04 Form Locator 17; CMS HRRP; HL7 ADT A03

attributes.name: index_los_days
attributes.description: Number of inpatient days for the index encounter. Used in readmission risk stratification and to assess whether short LOS contributed to the readmission.
attributes.references: CMS IPPS; ALOS Benchmarking; The Joint Commission

attributes.name: index_primary_icd10_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Index Primary International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Diagnosis Code
attributes.description: Primary ICD-10-CM diagnosis code from the index encounter. Used to determine HRRP measure category eligibility and to analyze clinical patterns driving readmissions.
attributes.references: WHO ICD-10-CM; CMS HRRP; 3M Health Information Systems Grouping

attributes.name: is_hrrp_applicable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP) Applicable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this readmission is subject to CMS HRRP penalty calculation. False when the readmission meets CMS exclusion criteria (e.g., planned readmission, transfer, AMA discharge, death during index stay).
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; 42 CFR §412.154; CMS IPPS Final Rule

attributes.name: is_related_to_index
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinically Related to Index Encounter Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the readmission diagnosis is clinically related to the index encounter's principal diagnosis, as determined by clinical documentation review or CDI query outcome. Supports root cause analysis and preventability assessment.
attributes.references: AHRQ Quality Indicators; CMS HRRP; CDI Program Standards

attributes.name: los_days
attributes.description: Number of inpatient days for the readmission encounter. Used for financial impact analysis and to assess severity of the readmission event.
attributes.references: CMS IPPS; ALOS Benchmarking; The Joint Commission

attributes.name: medication_reconciliation_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether medication reconciliation was completed at the time of index discharge. Medication discrepancies are a leading cause of preventable readmissions; this flag supports MAR audit and quality reporting.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission NPSG.03.06.01; CMS HRRP; AHRQ Medication Reconciliation

attributes.name: payer_type
attributes.description: Classification of the payer for the index encounter. Medicare is the primary payer subject to CMS HRRP penalties. Segmentation by payer type enables value-based contract performance analysis across HMO, PPO, ACO, and government programs.

attributes.name: preventability_assessment
attributes.description: Clinical determination of whether the readmission was potentially preventable through improved care coordination, discharge planning, or post-discharge follow-up. Drives care management program targeting and quality improvement initiatives.
attributes.references: AHRQ Prevention Quality Indicators (PQI); CMS HRRP; The Joint Commission

attributes.name: primary_icd10_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Readmission Primary International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Diagnosis Code
attributes.description: Primary ICD-10-CM diagnosis code assigned at the readmission encounter. Core field for determining whether the readmission is related to the index condition and for CMS HRRP measure attribution.
attributes.references: WHO ICD-10-CM; CMS HRRP; AMA CPT; 3M Health Information Systems

attributes.name: readmission_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the readmission record within the quality review and HRRP adjudication process. 'pending_review' indicates awaiting clinical validation; 'confirmed' indicates validated readmission; 'excluded' indicates meets CMS exclusion criteria; 'appealed' indicates under payer or CMS appeal; 'closed' indicates final disposition reached.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP; The Joint Commission; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: readmission_type
attributes.description: Classification of the readmission as planned or unplanned per CMS HRRP methodology. Planned readmissions (e.g., scheduled chemotherapy, elective procedures) are excluded from HRRP penalty calculations. Unplanned readmissions are subject to CMS penalty assessment.
attributes.references: CMS HRRP Planned Readmission Algorithm; ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines

attributes.name: review_completed_date
attributes.description: Date on which the clinical quality review of this readmission record was completed by the quality or CDI team. Supports workflow management and regulatory reporting timeliness tracking.

products.name: visit_coverage
products.description: This association product represents the insurance coverage relationship between a patient visit and a payer. It captures the coordination of benefits when multiple payers cover a single visit, tracking coverage sequence (primary, secondary, tertiary), eligibility verification status, prior authorization details, and financial responsibility allocation. Each record links one visit to one payer with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific coverage instance.. Existence Justification: In healthcare operations, a single patient visit routinely involves multiple insurance payers through coordination of benefits (COB)—primary, secondary, and tertiary coverage. Each payer relationship requires distinct eligibility verification, prior authorization tracking, coverage sequencing, and financial responsibility determination. Conversely, each payer covers thousands of visits across the healthcare organization. The visit-payer relationship is an operational business entity actively managed during registration, admission, and billing workflows.

products.name: visit_recall_impact
products.description: This association product represents the patient safety tracking relationship between visit and recall_notice. It captures the regulatory-required tracking of which patient visits were potentially affected by medical supply recalls, the notification and remediation workflow status for each visit-recall combination, and the clinical assessment of patient impact. Each record links one visit to one recall_notice with attributes that exist only in the context of this patient safety investigation and notification workflow.. Existence Justification: In healthcare operations, a single patient visit can be affected by multiple different recall notices if multiple recalled products were used during the encounter (e.g., different implants, devices, or supplies). Conversely, a single recall notice affects multiple patient visits—every patient who received the recalled product must be identified, notified, and clinically assessed. The healthcare organization must actively manage each visit-recall combination as a distinct patient safety investigation with its own notification status, clinical review, and remediation workflow.
