attributes.references: CMS Discharge Planning Rule 42 CFR §482.43; TJC RC.02.04.01; Epic ClinDoc Discharge Planning Flowsheet

attributes.name: fall_risk_level
attributes.description: Clinician-assigned fall risk stratification based on Morse Fall Scale, Hendrich II, or equivalent validated tool. Drives fall prevention care plan interventions and is a required safety metric under TJC National Patient Safety Goals (NPSG.09.02.01).
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.09.02.01; Morse Fall Scale; Hendrich II Fall Risk Model; CMS Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) Reduction Program

attributes.name: iadl_score
attributes.business_glossary_term: Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) Score
attributes.description: Sub-score measuring the patient's ability to perform Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) such as managing medications, finances, transportation, meal preparation, and housekeeping. Assessed via Lawton IADL Scale. Critical for community discharge planning.
attributes.references: Lawton IADL Scale; CMS OASIS-E Section M; Epic ClinDoc IADL Flowsheet

attributes.name: is_baseline_assessment
attributes.description: Indicates whether this assessment represents the initial baseline functional status evaluation for the patient within the current episode of care. Baseline assessments anchor longitudinal functional trajectory analysis and rehabilitation goal-setting.
attributes.references: CMS MDS 3.0 Assessment Reference Date; CMS OASIS-E Start of Care Assessment; Epic ClinDoc Assessment Sequencing

attributes.name: mobility_score
attributes.description: Sub-score quantifying the patient's mobility status including ambulation, transfers, stair climbing, and wheelchair use. Derived from FIM motor subscale, Barthel mobility items, or Berg Balance Scale. Informs physical therapy referrals and fall risk management.
attributes.references: CMS MDS 3.0 Section G; FIM Motor Subscale; Berg Balance Scale; Epic ClinDoc Mobility Flowsheet

attributes.name: mobility_status
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the patient's overall mobility level using CMS MDS-aligned coding. Supports post-acute care placement criteria, physical therapy orders, and fall prevention protocols.
attributes.references: CMS MDS 3.0 Section G; CMS OASIS-E; Epic ClinDoc Mobility Assessment

attributes.name: mrn
attributes.description: The Medical Record Number assigned to the patient by the healthcare organization. Used as the primary patient identity anchor across clinical systems and for cross-system reconciliation via the Master Patient Index (MPI).
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; Epic MPI; HL7 FHIR R4 Patient.identifier

attributes.name: nutritional_status
attributes.description: Clinician-assessed nutritional status of the patient as determined during functional assessment. Malnutrition directly impacts functional recovery, wound healing, and rehabilitation outcomes. Supports dietitian referrals and care plan development.
attributes.references: CMS MDS 3.0 Section K; ASPEN Malnutrition Criteria; TJC Nutritional Screening Standards; Epic ClinDoc Nutrition Flowsheet

attributes.name: pain_level
attributes.description: Patient-reported pain intensity score on a standardized numeric rating scale (NRS 0–10) or equivalent validated tool (Wong-Baker FACES, FLACC). Functional pain assessment is integral to ADL performance and mobility evaluation. Required by TJC pain management standards.
attributes.references: TJC Pain Management Standards; CMS MDS 3.0 Section J; Epic ClinDoc Pain Assessment Flowsheet

attributes.name: phq9_score
attributes.description: Total score from the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) depression screening tool, ranging from 0 to 27. Scores of 5, 10, 15, and 20 represent mild, moderate, moderately severe, and severe depression thresholds respectively. Required for HEDIS MDD measures and CMS quality reporting.
attributes.references: PHQ-9 (Kroenke & Spitzer); HEDIS MDD Measure; CMS MIPS Quality Measure 370; Epic ClinDoc PHQ-9 SmartForm

attributes.name: pressure_injury_risk
attributes.description: Risk stratification for pressure injury (decubitus ulcer) development based on Braden Scale or Norton Scale score. Supports wound prevention care planning and is tracked as a Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) under CMS quality programs.
attributes.references: Braden Scale; CMS HAC Reduction Program; TJC NPSG; Epic ClinDoc Skin Assessment Flowsheet

attributes.name: prior_level_of_function
attributes.description: Patient's functional status prior to the current illness, injury, or hospitalization as reported by patient, family, or prior care records. Establishes rehabilitation goals and discharge planning targets. Standard component of physical and occupational therapy evaluations.
attributes.references: CMS IRF-PAI; APTA Clinical Practice Guidelines; Epic ClinDoc PT/OT Evaluation Template

attributes.name: rehabilitation_potential
attributes.description: Clinician's assessment of the patient's potential to improve functional status through rehabilitation services. Influences therapy authorization, post-acute care placement, and Medicare skilled care eligibility determinations.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Benefit Policy Manual Chapter 15; CMS IRF Coverage Criteria; Epic ClinDoc Therapy Evaluation

attributes.name: score_interpretation
attributes.description: Clinically validated categorical interpretation of the total assessment score based on the tool's published scoring bands. Supports rapid clinical triage, care plan development, and post-acute care placement decisions.
attributes.references: AHRQ Functional Assessment Tools; CMS MDS 3.0; Epic ClinDoc Clinical Decision Support

attributes.name: sdoh_domain_flags

attributes.name: sdoh_screening_result

Supports population health management and care coordination referrals.
attributes.references: CMS SDOH Framework; AHRQ SDOH Compendium; HL7 FHIR Gravity Project; Epic Healthy Planet SDOH Screening

attributes.name: total_score

attributes.name: care_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.care_plan. Business justification: Nursing assessments (admission assessments, shift assessments, discharge assessments) inform care plan development and updates. Linking nursing_assessment.care_plan_id → care_plan.care_plan_id establi

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the healthcare facility (hospital, clinic, or outpatient center) where this nursing assessment was conducted.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; Epic ClinDoc Facility Context

attributes.name: imaging_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to radiology.imaging_order. Business justification: Nursing assessments identify acute changes requiring immediate imaging (respiratory distress→chest X-ray, neuro change→head CT). Essential for rapid response protocols and acute care pathways.

attributes.name: improvement_initiative_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.improvement_initiative. Business justification: Nursing assessment compliance is a common quality initiative (fall risk assessment completion, pressure injury risk assessment). Direct linkage enables tracking initiative impact. Essential for nursin

attributes.name: mar_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacy.mar_record. Business justification: Nursing assessments (pain, respiratory status, skin integrity) documented alongside medication administration for clinical correlation. Required for nursing documentation standards and medication admi

attributes.name: mpi_record_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient who is the subject of this nursing assessment. Links to the master patient record.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; Epic ClinDoc Patient Context

attributes.name: patient_safety_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.patient_safety_event. Business justification: Safety events (falls, pressure injuries) trigger review of nursing assessments to identify missed risk factors. Root cause analysis requires linking events to prior assessments. Essential for safety e

attributes.name: primary_nursing_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the licensed nurse (RN or LPN) who completed and signed this nursing assessment. Used for accountability, staffing analytics, and Joint Commission compliance.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Nursing Standards; Epic ClinDoc Flowsheet Author

attributes.name: record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to consent.consent_record. Business justification: Nursing assessments include sensitive data (restraint use, mental status, fall risk) requiring documented consent for interventions. Joint Commission standards mandate consent for restraints; mental h

attributes.name: resulting_diet_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to order.diet_order. Business justification: Nursing assessments drive diet orders. Real workflow: swallow assessment shows aspiration risk, triggers pureed diet order. Essential for nutrition care compliance, aspiration prevention protocols, sp

attributes.name: reviewed_test_result_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.test_result. Business justification: Nursing assessments review recent lab results for care planning (potassium levels→cardiac monitoring). Role prefix 'reviewed_' indicates assessment input. Essential for nursing flowsheet integration a

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical encounter (inpatient admission, ED visit, or outpatient visit) during which this nursing assessment was performed.
attributes.references: Epic ClinDoc Encounter Context; HL7 FHIR Encounter Resource

attributes.name: assessment_interval_hours
attributes.description: The required reassessment interval in hours as defined by the care setting protocol and assessment type (e.g., every 4 hours for ICU, every 8 hours for medical-surgical). Used to monitor reassessment compliance and timeliness.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Reassessment Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation; Epic ClinDoc Flowsheet Frequency

attributes.name: assessment_notes
attributes.description: Free-text narrative clinical notes entered by the assessing nurse to supplement structured assessment findings. May include abnormal findings, patient responses, and clinical reasoning. Contains Protected Health Information (PHI).
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; The Joint Commission (TJC) Clinical Documentation Standards; Epic ClinDoc Nursing Notes

attributes.name: assessment_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the nursing assessment record. Indicates whether the assessment is actively being documented, finalized, amended after completion, or voided. Supports Joint Commission compliance audits.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Documentation Standards; Epic ClinDoc Flowsheet Status

attributes.name: assessment_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the nursing assessment was clinically performed (real-world event time). Distinct from documentation or record creation timestamps. Critical for shift-based quality metrics and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Nursing Documentation Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: assessment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the nursing assessment by its clinical purpose and timing. Drives workflow routing, documentation requirements, and quality metric calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Admission|Shift Change|Discharge|Head-to-Toe|Fall Risk|Skin Integrity|Restraint|Pressure Injury|Discharge Readiness|Pain — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Nursing Assessment Standards; Epic ClinDoc Flowsheet Templates

attributes.name: braden_score
attributes.description: Numeric pressure injury risk score calculated using the Braden Scale (range 6–23). Lower scores indicate higher risk. Required for pressure injury prevention protocol activation and CMS HAC reporting.
attributes.references: CMS HAC Reduction Program — Pressure Ulcer; The Joint Commission (TJC) Skin Assessment Standards; AHRQ Pressure Ulcer Prevention Guidelines

attributes.name: cardiovascular_status
attributes.description: Documented cardiovascular assessment findings including heart rate regularity and rhythm. Core component of the head-to-toe nursing assessment and cardiac monitoring documentation.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Clinical Assessment Standards; Epic ClinDoc Cardiovascular Flowsheet

attributes.name: care_recommendations
attributes.description: Nursing care recommendations and planned interventions documented as part of the assessment (e.g., reposition every 2 hours, initiate fall prevention bundle, consult wound care). Feeds into the nursing care plan.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Care Planning Standards (PC.01.02.03); CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: care_setting
attributes.description: The clinical care setting in which the nursing assessment was performed (e.g., Inpatient, Intensive Care Unit (ICU), Emergency Department (ED), Outpatient). Drives assessment template selection and quality metric stratification.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; The Joint Commission (TJC) Environment of Care Standards

attributes.name: completed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the nurse finalized and signed the nursing assessment in the EHR. Used to measure documentation timeliness and compliance with shift-completion requirements.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Nursing Documentation Standards; Epic ClinDoc Flowsheet Sign-off

attributes.name: continence_status
attributes.description: Patient's urinary and bowel continence status as documented in the nursing assessment. Relevant to Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infection (CAUTI) prevention protocols and skin integrity management.
attributes.references: CMS HAC Reduction Program — CAUTI; The Joint Commission (TJC) CAUTI Prevention Standards; AHRQ CAUTI Prevention Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this nursing assessment record was first created in the source system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; ISO 27001; Epic ClinDoc Audit Log

attributes.name: discharge_barriers
attributes.description: Free-text or structured documentation of identified barriers to patient discharge (e.g., awaiting placement, transportation, caregiver availability, Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) factors). Supports care coordination and discharge planning workflows.
attributes.references: CMS Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP); The Joint Commission (TJC) Discharge Planning Standards

attributes.name: discharge_readiness_score
attributes.description: Numeric score from a validated discharge readiness assessment tool (e.g., Readiness for Hospital Discharge Scale) indicating the patient's preparedness for discharge. Supports discharge planning, Length of Stay (LOS) management, and readmission reduction initiatives.
attributes.references: CMS Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP); The Joint Commission (TJC) Discharge Planning Standards; AHRQ Discharge Planning Guidelines

attributes.name: fall_risk_category
attributes.description: Categorical fall risk classification derived from the fall risk score (Low, Moderate, High). Drives nursing care plan interventions, bed alarm activation, and fall prevention bundle compliance reporting.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) NPSG 09.02.01; CMS HAC Reduction Program

attributes.name: fall_risk_score
attributes.description: Numeric fall risk score calculated from the validated fall risk assessment tool (e.g., Morse Fall Scale, Hendrich II). Drives fall prevention protocol activation and care plan interventions. Required for Joint Commission NPSG.09.02.01.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) National Patient Safety Goal (NPSG) 09.02.01; CMS Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) Reduction Program

attributes.name: fall_risk_tool
attributes.description: The validated fall risk assessment instrument used to calculate the fall risk score (e.g., Morse Fall Scale, Hendrich II Fall Risk Model). Ensures comparability of scores across units and facilities.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) NPSG 09.02.01; AHRQ Fall Prevention Guidelines

attributes.name: iv_access_type
attributes.description: Type of intravenous access device present and assessed during the nursing assessment (Peripheral IV, Central Line, PICC, Port, or None). Critical for Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infection (CLABSI) prevention bundle compliance and HAI reporting.
attributes.references: CMS HAC Reduction Program — CLABSI; The Joint Commission (TJC) CLABSI Prevention Standards; CDC NHSN CLABSI Definitions

attributes.name: iv_site_condition
attributes.description: Condition of the intravenous access site as assessed by the nurse (Patent, Infiltrated, Phlebitis, Occluded, Removed). Drives IV site care interventions and CLABSI prevention bundle documentation.
attributes.references: CMS HAC Reduction Program — CLABSI; The Joint Commission (TJC) Infusion Therapy Standards; INS Infusion Therapy Standards of Practice

attributes.name: joint_commission_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether this nursing assessment meets all applicable Joint Commission documentation requirements for the assessment type (e.g., all required fields completed, completed within required timeframe). Used for quality reporting and survey readiness.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Nursing Assessment Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this nursing assessment record was most recently modified in the source system. Supports change detection, incremental ETL loads, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; ISO 27001; Epic ClinDoc Audit Log

attributes.name: mobility_status
attributes.description: Patient's functional mobility level as assessed by the nurse (Independent, Assisted, Dependent, Bedrest, Ambulating). Informs fall prevention, pressure injury prevention, and physical therapy referral decisions.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Functional Assessment Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: mrn
attributes.description: The Medical Record Number (MRN) assigned to the patient by the facility's Master Patient Index (MPI). Provides a human-readable patient identifier for clinical staff and HIM workflows.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; CMS Conditions of Participation; Epic MPI

attributes.name: neurological_status
attributes.description: Documented neurological status of the patient at the time of assessment, reflecting level of consciousness and orientation. Core component of head-to-toe nursing assessment and change-of-condition monitoring.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Clinical Assessment Standards; AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators

attributes.name: nursing_unit
attributes.description: The specific nursing unit or department (e.g., 4 North Medical-Surgical, MICU, PACU) where the patient was located at the time of the assessment. Used for unit-level quality benchmarking and staffing analysis.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Nursing Unit Standards; Epic ClinDoc Department Context

attributes.name: nutrition_status
attributes.description: Nursing assessment of the patient's nutritional status and feeding method. Drives dietary consult referrals and nutrition care plan interventions. Supports malnutrition quality reporting.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Nutritional Assessment Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation; AHRQ Malnutrition Quality Measures

attributes.name: orientation_level
attributes.description: Patient orientation level documented during neurological assessment: x1 (person), x2 (person and place), x3 (person, place, and time), x4 (person, place, time, and event). Standard clinical notation used in nursing documentation.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Clinical Assessment Standards; Epic ClinDoc Neurological Flowsheet

attributes.name: pain_scale_type
attributes.description: The validated pain assessment scale used to obtain the pain score (e.g., Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), FLACC for pediatric/non-verbal patients, Critical Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT)). Required for clinical interpretation of pain scores.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Pain Assessment Standards; AHRQ Pain Management Guidelines

attributes.name: pain_score
attributes.description: Numeric pain intensity score documented by the nurse using a validated pain scale (e.g., Numeric Rating Scale 0–10, FLACC, CPOT). Required by The Joint Commission for all patient assessments. Drives pain management interventions.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Pain Assessment and Management Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: patient_education_provided
attributes.description: Indicates whether patient and/or family education was provided during this nursing assessment encounter. Required documentation for Joint Commission and CMS patient education standards.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Patient Education Standards (PC.02.03.01); CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: pressure_injury_location
attributes.description: Anatomical body site location of the identified pressure injury (e.g., sacrum, coccyx, heel, occiput). Documented using standardized anatomical terminology. Required for wound care documentation and HAC reporting.
attributes.references: NPIAP Staging Guidelines; CMS HAC Reduction Program; Epic ClinDoc Wound Assessment Flowsheet

attributes.name: pressure_injury_stage
attributes.description: National Pressure Injury Advisory Panel (NPIAP) staging classification for any identified pressure injury (Stage 1 through Stage 4, Unstageable, or Deep Tissue Pressure Injury). Required for CMS Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) reporting and quality metrics.
attributes.references: National Pressure Injury Advisory Panel (NPIAP) Staging Guidelines; CMS HAC Reduction Program; The Joint Commission (TJC) Wound Assessment Standards

attributes.name: respiratory_status
attributes.description: Documented respiratory status of the patient including breathing pattern and effort. Part of the head-to-toe body system assessment. Triggers escalation protocols when abnormal.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Clinical Assessment Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: restraint_indication
attributes.description: Clinical justification documented by the nurse for restraint application (e.g., risk of self-harm, removal of life-sustaining devices, violent behavior). Required by CMS and Joint Commission for every restraint episode.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation §482.13(e); The Joint Commission (TJC) Restraint Standards

attributes.name: restraint_type
attributes.description: Type of restraint applied to the patient as documented in the restraint assessment (Physical, Chemical, Soft Limb, Vest, Mitts, or None). Required for CMS Conditions of Participation restraint documentation and Joint Commission compliance.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation §482.13(e); The Joint Commission (TJC) Restraint and Seclusion Standards

attributes.name: safety_check_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the nursing safety check (e.g., bed in lowest position, call light within reach, side rails up, ID band verified) was completed and documented as part of this assessment. Supports Joint Commission National Patient Safety Goal compliance.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) National Patient Safety Goals (NPSG); CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: skin_integrity_status
attributes.description: Overall skin integrity assessment finding indicating whether the patient's skin is intact or compromised. Triggers wound care protocols and pressure injury prevention bundles. Required for HAI reporting.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Wound Care Standards; CMS HAC Reduction Program — Pressure Ulcer Category

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this nursing assessment was sourced (e.g., Epic ClinDoc, Cerner PowerChart). Supports data lineage and ETL traceability.
attributes.references: Epic ClinDoc; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; MEDITECH Expanse

attributes.name: source_system_assessment_code
attributes.description: The native identifier of this nursing assessment record in the originating Electronic Health Record (EHR) system (e.g., Epic ClinDoc flowsheet row ID or Cerner PowerChart documentation ID). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Epic ClinDoc Flowsheet; Cerner PowerChart Documentation

products.name: hai_event
products.description: Healthcare-Associated Infection (HAI) surveillance event records tracking CLABSI, CAUTI, SSI, MRSA, C. difficile, and VAP events per NHSN (National Healthcare Safety Network) definitions. Captures infection type, NHSN definition criteria met, event date, device days, patient days, unit/location, causative organism, antibiotic susceptibility, linked procedure (for SSI), infection preventionist review status, and reporting status. Sourced from Epic infection control modules and dedicated surveillance systems (e.g., Theradoc, ICNet). Required for CMS HAI reporting, VBP penalty calculations, and state mandatory reporting. Domain ownership note: clinical domain owns the HAI event as a clinical occurrence; quality domain owns the aggregate surveillance metrics and benchmarking — global architect should confirm this boundary.
products.reference: NHSN HAI Surveillance

attributes.name: hai_event_id

attributes.name: bed_id

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the healthcare facility (hospital, campus, or care site) where the HAI event occurred. Required for facility-level NHSN reporting and CMS Value-Based Purchasing (VBP) penalty calculations.
attributes.references: CMS HAI Reporting; NHSN Facility Survey; The Joint Commission (TJC) Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the infection preventionist (IP) clinician responsible for reviewing, confirming, and submitting this HAI event to NHSN. Required for audit trail and regulatory accountability.
attributes.references: NHSN Patient Safety Component Protocol; APIC Infection Prevention Standards

attributes.name: corrective_action_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.corrective_action. Business justification: HAI events trigger corrective actions (process improvements, staff education). Direct linkage enables tracking corrective action effectiveness. Essential for infection prevention quality improvement a

attributes.name: cost_center_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.diagnosis. Business justification: Healthcare-Associated Infection (HAI) surveillance events result in infection diagnoses being documented in the patient record. Linking hai_event.diagnosis_id → diagnosis.diagnosis_id connects the inf

attributes.name: improvement_initiative_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.improvement_initiative. Business justification: HAI reduction is a primary quality improvement focus. Initiatives link to specific HAI events for root cause analysis and intervention tracking. Essential for infection prevention quality improvement

attributes.references: NHSN SSI Protocol; CMS HAI Reporting

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: HAIs linked to specific devices/supplies for root cause analysis, NHSN reporting, and regulatory compliance. Enables infection control supply tracking, device-associated infection surveillance, and qu

attributes.name: microbiology_culture_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.microbiology_culture. Business justification: HAI events identified/confirmed by positive cultures - infection control core process. Role prefix 'diagnostic_' indicates event confirmation. Required for NHSN reporting and outbreak investigation. R

attributes.name: mpi_record_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient who experienced the Healthcare-Associated Infection (HAI) event. Links to the master patient record for demographic and clinical context.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164; NHSN Patient Safety Component Protocol

attributes.name: outbreak_id
attributes.description: Identifier linking this HAI event to a specific outbreak investigation record when outbreak_flag is True. Enables grouping of related HAI events for epidemiological analysis and root cause investigation.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; The Joint Commission (TJC) Infection Control Standards

attributes.name: patient_safety_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.patient_safety_event. Business justification: HAI events are a subset of patient safety events. Many organizations track HAIs within their safety event system for unified reporting and root cause analysis. Essential for integrated safety reportin

attributes.name: response_clinical_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to order.clinical_order. Business justification: HAI events trigger response orders. Real workflow: CLABSI identified, orders placed for line removal and antibiotics. Essential for infection control tracking, HAI response protocol compliance, NHSN r

attributes.name: susceptibility_result_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.susceptibility_result. Business justification: Antibiotic selection for HAI treatment based on susceptibility results. Essential for antibiotic stewardship and MDRO tracking. Removes denormalized resistance profile data in favor of proper FK relat

attributes.name: treatment_drug_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacy.drug_master. Business justification: Healthcare-acquired infections treated with specific antimicrobials. Antibiotic stewardship programs track drug-bug relationships, resistance patterns, and treatment outcomes. Required for NHSN report

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the inpatient encounter during which the HAI event was identified. Used to correlate infection events with admission, discharge, and clinical documentation.
attributes.references: NHSN Patient Safety Component Protocol; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: attributed_los_days
attributes.description: Number of additional inpatient days clinically attributed to this HAI event beyond the expected Length of Stay (LOS). Used for cost-of-infection analysis, quality improvement, and VBP impact assessments. Distinct from total encounter LOS.
attributes.references: AHRQ HAI Cost Studies; CMS VBP Program; CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this HAI event record was first created in the system of record or ingested into the lakehouse silver layer. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and NHSN submission timeliness tracking.

attributes.name: device_days
attributes.description: Total number of device-days (central line days, catheter days, or ventilator days) for the patient during the relevant surveillance period. Used as the denominator in NHSN device-associated infection rate calculations (infections per 1,000 device days).
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: Type of invasive device associated with the HAI event. Applicable for device-associated infections: central line (CLABSI), urinary catheter (CAUTI), mechanical ventilator (VAP). Set to 'none' for non-device-associated infections such as SSI, MRSA bacteremia, or CDI.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Device-Associated Module; CMS HAI Reporting

attributes.name: event_date
attributes.description: The date on which the Healthcare-Associated Infection (HAI) event was identified or the infection onset date as defined by NHSN criteria. This is the principal real-world event date used for NHSN reporting, rate calculations, and CMS submission windows.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current workflow lifecycle status of the HAI event record. Tracks progression from initial identification through infection preventionist review, NHSN submission, and any subsequent amendments. Drives quality and compliance dashboards.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting; The Joint Commission (TJC) Infection Control Standards

attributes.name: hac_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this HAI event qualifies as a Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) under CMS payment policy, potentially triggering a payment reduction or penalty. True = qualifies as HAC; False = does not meet HAC criteria.
attributes.references: CMS Hospital-Acquired Conditions (HAC) Reduction Program; CMS VBP Program; OIG Fraud and Abuse Guidelines

attributes.name: infection_onset_setting
attributes.description: Clinical setting in which the infection is determined to have originated: inpatient (hospital-acquired), outpatient, community-acquired, long-term care facility (LTCF), or unknown. Supports NHSN attribution rules and population health analysis.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting; AHRQ HAI Prevention

attributes.name: infection_type
attributes.description: Classification of the HAI event per NHSN definitions: Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infection (CLABSI), Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infection (CAUTI), Surgical Site Infection (SSI), Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia, Clostridioides difficile Infection (CDI), or Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP). Drives NHSN module routing and CMS VBP penalty calculations.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting; CMS VBP Program

attributes.name: ip_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which the infection preventionist completed their clinical review of this HAI event. Used for workflow tracking, timeliness metrics, and audit trail documentation.
attributes.references: APIC Infection Prevention Standards; CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual

attributes.name: ip_review_notes
attributes.description: Free-text clinical notes entered by the infection preventionist during review of this HAI event. May include rationale for confirmation, rejection, or amendment of the event classification. Supports CDI and quality review workflows.
attributes.references: APIC Infection Prevention Standards; The Joint Commission (TJC) Infection Control Standards

attributes.name: ip_review_status
attributes.description: Status of the infection preventionist's clinical review of this HAI event. Tracks whether the IP has reviewed, approved, or disputed the event classification prior to NHSN submission. Required for regulatory audit trails.
attributes.references: APIC Infection Prevention Standards; CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; The Joint Commission (TJC) IC Standards

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this HAI event record, including status changes, IP review updates, NHSN submission updates, or clinical amendments. Required for change data capture (CDC) and audit compliance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001; NIST Cybersecurity Framework

attributes.name: mrn
attributes.description: Medical Record Number (MRN) of the patient associated with this HAI event. Denormalized from the patient record to support infection surveillance workflows and NHSN submission without requiring a join.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164; NHSN Patient Safety Component Protocol; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: nhsn_definition_met
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) Definition Criteria Met
attributes.description: Indicates whether this event meets the CDC NHSN surveillance definition criteria for the specified infection type. True = confirmed HAI per NHSN criteria; False = under review or criteria not fully met. Determines reportability to CMS and state health departments.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: nhsn_event_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) Event Number
attributes.description: Unique event number assigned by the CDC National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) upon submission of this HAI event. Used for regulatory tracking, CMS reporting reconciliation, and state mandatory reporting.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: nhsn_procedure_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) Procedure Code
attributes.description: NHSN-specific procedure category code for the operative procedure linked to an SSI event (e.g., COLO for colon surgery, HPRO for hip prosthesis). Distinct from CPT codes; used specifically for NHSN SSI risk index calculation and benchmarking.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN SSI Protocol; CDC NHSN Operative Procedure Codes

attributes.name: nhsn_reporting_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) Reporting Status
attributes.description: Indicates the submission and acceptance status of this HAI event with the CDC National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN). Tracks whether the event has been reported, accepted, or rejected by NHSN. Critical for CMS HAI reporting compliance and VBP penalty avoidance.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting Requirements; CMS VBP Program

attributes.name: nhsn_submission_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) Submission Date
attributes.description: Date on which this HAI event was submitted to the CDC National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN). Used to verify timely reporting compliance with CMS and state mandatory reporting deadlines.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting Requirements; State Departments of Health

attributes.name: outbreak_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this HAI event has been associated with a declared infection outbreak investigation at the facility. True = linked to an active or closed outbreak; False = sporadic/isolated event. Supports epidemiological cluster analysis.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; The Joint Commission (TJC) Infection Control Standards; AHRQ HAI Prevention

attributes.name: patient_days
attributes.description: Total number of patient-days in the unit or facility during the surveillance period associated with this HAI event. Used as the denominator for non-device-associated infection rates (e.g., CDI, MRSA per 10,000 patient days) per NHSN methodology.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting

attributes.name: patient_outcome
attributes.description: Clinical outcome of the patient attributed to or associated with this HAI event: recovered, transferred to higher level of care, expired, or unknown. Used for mortality analysis, quality reporting, and NHSN outcome tracking.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting; AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators

attributes.name: present_on_admission
attributes.description: Indicates whether the infection was present at the time of hospital admission (True) or developed after admission (False). HAI events by definition should be False (post-admission onset). Used for HAC (Hospital-Acquired Condition) determination and CMS payment adjustments.
attributes.references: CMS Hospital-Acquired Conditions (HAC) Policy; NHSN Patient Safety Component Protocol; HIPAA 45 CFR §162

attributes.name: secondary_infection_type
attributes.description: Secondary or co-occurring HAI type when a patient experiences more than one concurrent infection event (e.g., a patient with both CLABSI and CAUTI). Nullable; populated only when a secondary infection is clinically documented and meets NHSN criteria.
attributes.references: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual; CMS HAI Reporting

attributes.name: source_system

products.name: procedure_equipment_usage
products.description: This association product represents the operational usage event between a clinical procedure and a specific equipment asset. It captures the actual deployment and utilization of biomedical equipment during surgical and interventional procedures. Each record links one procedure_event to one equipment_asset with timestamps, sterilization tracking, implant traceability, and malfunction reporting that exist only in the context of this specific usage instance. Supports OR utilization analytics, biomedical engineering maintenance correlation, FDA device event reporting (MDR), and TJC equipment management compliance.. Existence Justification: In healthcare operations, surgical and interventional procedures routinely deploy multiple equipment assets simultaneously (surgical table, anesthesia machine, robotic system, imaging equipment, infusion pumps, patient monitors), and each capital equipment asset is used across hundreds of procedures over its lifecycle. Clinical staff actively document equipment usage during procedure execution for charge capture, sterilization tracking, implant traceability, and malfunction reporting. This is an operational M:N relationship managed as part of the clinical workflow.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

A procedure may use multiple equipment assets, only some of which are implants. The implant_used_flag and udi belong in the association to track which specific equipment assets were implanted, enabling FDA traceability at the device level rather than just the procedure level.]

attributes.name: usage_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the equipment was deployed and began being used during the procedure. Critical for utilization tracking and equipment availability management.

products.name: plan_care_coordination
products.description: This association product represents the enrollment and coordination relationship between a patient's care plan and the health insurance plan(s) covering that care. It captures payer-specific care management requirements, authorization status, and program participation for each care plan-health plan combination. Each record links one care plan to one health plan with attributes that exist only in the context of this payer-specific care coordination relationship.. Existence Justification: In healthcare operations, a single care plan frequently requires coordination with multiple health insurance plans when patients have dual coverage (Medicare + Medicaid, primary + secondary insurance, or Medicare Advantage + supplemental). Each health plan imposes distinct care management requirements, authorization processes, quality measures, and program enrollment criteria for the same underlying care plan. Conversely, a health plan's care management program tracks multiple care plans across its member population. Care coordinators actively manage these plan-specific coordination records, updating authorization status, program enrollment, and payer-specific goals as part of operational care delivery workflows.

domains.name: order
domains.description: Manages the full lifecycle of clinical orders including CPOE (Computerized Physician Order Entry) for lab, radiology, pharmacy, and referral orders. Tracks order status, priority, routing, and fulfillment. Integrates with Epic Orders, Beaker (LIS), Radiant (RIS), and Willow (pharmacy) as the operational order management backbone.

products.name: clinical_order
products.description: Core master record for every clinical order entered via CPOE (Computerized Physician Order Entry) in Epic Orders or Cerner Millennium. Captures the authoritative order identity, ordering provider NPI, patient MRN, order type (lab, radiology, pharmacy, referral, nursing, dietary, consult), order priority (STAT, routine, urgent, timed), order mode (verbal, written, electronic), clinical indication (ICD-10 coded), ordering datetime, start and stop datetimes, order source system, order set membership flag, parent order reference for linked/chained orders, current order status, and order class (inpatient, outpatient, ED, ambulatory). SSOT for all clinical order identity, metadata, and type/priority classification across the enterprise. Absorbs order_type and order_priority reference attributes as embedded enums. All modality-specific attributes are owned by extension products (lab_order, radiology_order, pharmacy_order, referral_order).

attributes.description: Human-readable name or description of the ordered item or service as displayed in the EHR (e.g., 'CBC with Differential', 'Chest X-Ray PA and Lateral', 'Metoprolol 25mg PO'). Sourced from the Charge Description Master (CDM) or order catalog.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; CDM (Charge Description Master); LOINC; SNOMED CT

attributes.name: order_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable order identifier assigned by the source system (Epic Orders or Cerner Millennium). Used for cross-system reconciliation, audit trails, and communication with clinical staff. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this transaction.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.identifier

attributes.name: order_priority
attributes.description: Clinical urgency classification for the order. STAT indicates immediate action required; timed indicates a specific scheduled execution time. Embedded enum per product design specification. Drives turnaround time (TAT) SLA monitoring.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.priority; TJC Order Management Standards

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current workflow lifecycle state of the clinical order. Drives downstream fulfillment routing and reporting. Values align with Epic Orders and HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest status codes.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.status; The Joint Commission (TJC) Order Management Standards

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the clinical order by modality or service category. Determines routing to the appropriate fulfillment system: Beaker (LIS) for lab, Radiant (RIS) for radiology, Willow for pharmacy, etc. Embedded enum per product design specification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: lab|radiology|pharmacy|referral|nursing|dietary|consult — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.category; LOINC; CPT (AMA)

attributes.name: ordering_provider_npi
attributes.description: 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the clinician who placed the order. Stored denormalized on the order for regulatory reporting, claims submission, and audit purposes per CMS requirements. Distinct from the FK to the provider master.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA 45 CFR §162.408; CMS-1500; UB-04

attributes.name: patient_mrn
attributes.description: Medical Record Number (MRN) of the patient for whom the order was placed. Stored denormalized on the order for cross-system reconciliation, HL7 ADT message processing, and regulatory audit trails. Sourced from the Master Patient Index (MPI).
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR R4; Epic MPI; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: quantity_ordered
attributes.description: Numeric quantity of the ordered item or service (e.g., number of lab panels, number of imaging views, medication dose quantity). Unit of measure is captured in quantity_unit. Used for supply chain, pharmacy dispensing, and charge capture.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.quantity

attributes.name: quantity_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the quantity_ordered field (e.g., 'mg', 'mL', 'units', 'each', 'tablet'). Follows UCUM (Unified Code for Units of Measure) standards for interoperability with HL7 FHIR.
attributes.references: UCUM (Unified Code for Units of Measure); HL7 FHIR R4; Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this clinical order originated. Supports data lineage, ETL reconciliation, and multi-system enterprise integration. Values correspond to the enterprise EHR systems in use.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; MEDITECH Expanse; HL7 FHIR R4

attributes.name: start_datetime
attributes.description: Datetime when the order is scheduled to begin or when fulfillment should commence. For timed orders, this is the precise execution start time. Distinct from order_datetime (when placed) and order_datetime (when entered).
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.occurrencePeriod.start

attributes.name: stop_datetime
attributes.description: Datetime when the order expires, is discontinued, or fulfillment should cease. Critical for pharmacy and nursing orders to prevent over-administration. Nullable for one-time orders.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.occurrencePeriod.end

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this clinical order record was last modified in the enterprise data lakehouse. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED field for change tracking, incremental ETL processing, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 27001; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; HITRUST CSF; SOC 2

products.name: order_status_history
products.description: Immutable audit trail of every lifecycle event for a clinical order, including status transitions, modifications (dose, frequency, route, priority changes), amendments, corrections, renewals, and discontinuations. Captures event type, previous and new values, modification details, the datetime of each event, the user or system that triggered it, reason codes, clinical justification, co-signature requirements for modifications, modifying provider NPI, and the source system event. SSOT for all order lifecycle changes — no other product in this domain records order state transitions or modifications. Supports HIPAA audit compliance, CDI (Clinical Documentation Improvement), medication reconciliation, and clinical quality review.
products.reference: Epic Orders Status Audit / HL7 ORC Segment

attributes.name: order_status_history_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each order lifecycle event record in the immutable audit trail. Primary key for this append-only event log.

attributes.name: clinical_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent clinical order whose lifecycle event is being recorded. Links this history record to the originating order in the order management system (Epic Orders / Cerner Millennium).

attributes.name: cpoe_alert_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the Clinical Decision Support (CDS) alert (drug-drug interaction, allergy, dosing alert, duplicate order) that was triggered and may have prompted this lifecycle event. Null if no CDS alert was associated. Supports CDS effectiveness analysis and alert fatigue reporting.
attributes.references: ONC 21st Century Cures Act; Epic CDS; AHRQ Patient Safety

attributes.name: demographics_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient associated with the clinical order. Required for HIPAA audit compliance and PHI traceability across all order lifecycle events.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR R4 Patient Resource

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user (clinician, pharmacist, nurse, or system account) who triggered this lifecycle event. Distinct from the ordering provider — captures who made the change, not who originally placed the order. Core field for HIPAA audit accountability.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); Epic Orders Audit Log; OIG Compliance

attributes.name: org_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical department or fulfillment unit (lab, pharmacy, radiology, nursing unit) that received this order event for execution. Supports departmental workload analysis and order routing audit.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.performer

attributes.name: primary_order_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinician who originally placed the order. Used for accountability tracking and CPOE audit trails.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; CPOE Standards

attributes.name: primary_order_message_log_id
attributes.description: The HL7 message control ID (MSH-10) of the HL7 v2 or FHIR message that triggered or communicated this order lifecycle event. Supports interoperability audit trails and Health Information Exchange (HIE) reconciliation.
attributes.references: HL7 v2.x MSH-10; HL7 FHIR R4 MessageHeader.id; HIE Standards

attributes.name: set_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the clinical order set or protocol from which the parent order was generated, if applicable. Supports analysis of order set adherence and protocol-driven order modification patterns.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium; AHRQ Clinical Decision Support

attributes.name: source_system_event_message_log_id
attributes.description: The native event or audit record identifier from the originating operational system (Epic, Cerner, etc.). Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the source EHR audit log for reconciliation and dispute resolution.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 AuditEvent.id; HITRUST CSF; ETL Lineage Standards

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical encounter (visit, admission, or ED episode) during which this order lifecycle event occurred. Supports encounter-level order audit and CDI review.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter Resource; Epic Orders

attributes.name: cds_alert_overridden
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Decision Support (CDS) Alert Overridden Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Clinical Decision Support (CDS) alert was overridden by the provider when this event was triggered. True = alert was acknowledged and overridden; False = alert was not overridden or no alert was present. Critical for patient safety audit and alert override rate reporting.
attributes.references: ONC 21st Century Cures Act; AHRQ Patient Safety; Joint Commission NPSG

attributes.name: cosignature_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this order modification or event requires a co-signature from a supervising or authorizing provider before the change takes effect. Applies to resident/trainee orders and controlled substance modifications per institutional policy.
attributes.references: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.24; DEA 21 CFR Part 1306

attributes.name: cosignature_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the required co-signature was completed by the supervising provider. Null if co-signature has not yet been obtained. Used to measure co-signature turnaround time for compliance reporting.
attributes.references: Joint Commission MS.06.01.03; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.24

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this history record was first written to the lakehouse silver layer. Represents the ETL ingestion time, distinct from event_timestamp (the real-world clinical event time). Used for data pipeline monitoring and late-arrival detection.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; HITRUST CSF; Data Lineage Standards

attributes.name: dea_schedule
attributes.description: The DEA controlled substance schedule (CI through CV) applicable to the medication order at the time of this event. Populated only when is_controlled_substance is True. Determines regulatory handling requirements.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308; Controlled Substances Act

attributes.name: discontinuation_type
attributes.description: Classifies the reason category for order discontinuation when event_type is DISCONTINUATION. AMA = Against Medical Advice. Supports medication reconciliation, discharge planning, and quality reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: COMPLETED|PROVIDER_DISCONTINUED|PATIENT_REFUSED|AMA|FORMULARY|DUPLICATE|PROTOCOL — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.statusReason; Joint Commission MM.04.01.01; AMA Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which this lifecycle event becomes clinically effective (e.g., when a renewed order becomes active, when a hold is lifted). May differ from event_timestamp when events are scheduled or backdated. Supports medication administration record (MAR) reconciliation.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.occurrenceDateTime; Epic Orders; MAR Standards

attributes.name: event_sequence_number
attributes.description: Monotonically increasing sequence number for all lifecycle events belonging to the same parent order. Enables chronological ordering of events within an order's history and detection of out-of-order event delivery from source systems.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 AuditEvent; Epic Orders Audit Log; Data Lineage Standards

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which this lifecycle event occurred in the clinical system. This is the authoritative real-world event time, distinct from record audit timestamps. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); HL7 FHIR R4 AuditEvent.recorded

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Discriminator classifying the kind of lifecycle event recorded. STATUS_CHANGE = workflow state transition; MODIFICATION = dose/frequency/route/priority change; AMENDMENT = clinical content update; CORRECTION = error correction; RENEWAL = order re-authorization; DISCONTINUATION = order stopped; COSIGN_REQUEST = co-signature required; COSIGN_COMPLETED = co-signature fulfilled. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: STATUS_CHANGE|MODIFICATION|AMENDMENT|CORRECTION|RENEWAL|DISCONTINUATION|COSIGN_REQUEST|COSIGN_COMPLETED — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Task.status; Epic Orders Event Types; Joint Commission RC.02.01.01

attributes.name: hipaa_audit_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Audit Category
attributes.description: HIPAA-defined audit event category for this order lifecycle event, used for compliance reporting to OCR and internal privacy audits. Classifies the event as an access, modification, disclosure, correction, or deletion of PHI per HIPAA Security Rule requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); OCR Audit Protocol; HITRUST CSF Control 09.aa

attributes.name: is_amendment
attributes.description: Indicates whether this event represents a formal clinical amendment to the order record (as opposed to a routine status change or system-generated update). True = formal amendment requiring clinical documentation. Supports HIM and CDI amendment tracking.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.01.03.01; HIM Standards; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.526

attributes.name: is_controlled_substance
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order subject to this lifecycle event involves a DEA-scheduled controlled substance. True = controlled substance order. Triggers enhanced audit requirements and DEA compliance tracking.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1306; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); State Pharmacy Boards

attributes.name: is_verbal_order
attributes.description: Indicates whether this order event was initiated as a verbal or telephone order requiring subsequent written authentication. True = verbal/telephone order; False = directly entered CPOE order. Tracked for Joint Commission verbal order compliance.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.24(c)(1)(ii)

attributes.name: modified_field_name
attributes.description: The name of the specific clinical order field that was changed during a MODIFICATION, AMENDMENT, or CORRECTION event (e.g., 'dose', 'frequency', 'route', 'quantity', 'priority', 'start_date', 'stop_date', 'indication'). Null for pure status transitions.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Audit Log; Cerner Millennium Audit Trail; CDI Standards

attributes.name: modifying_provider_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the licensed provider who triggered this event, when the modifying user is a credentialed clinician. Denormalized from the provider record to preserve the NPI value at the time of the event for regulatory audit purposes. Required for CMS and OIG compliance reporting.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); OIG

attributes.name: modifying_user_role
attributes.description: The clinical or operational role of the user who triggered this lifecycle event at the time of the event. Supports role-based audit analysis and compliance review (e.g., identifying unauthorized order modifications). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PHYSICIAN|NURSE|PHARMACIST|RESIDENT|SYSTEM|ADMIN|TECHNICIAN — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(a)(1); Joint Commission; OIG Compliance

attributes.name: new_status
attributes.description: The order workflow status immediately after this lifecycle event. Together with previous_status, defines the state transition that occurred. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DRAFT|PENDING|ACTIVE|HOLD|SUSPENDED|COMPLETED|DISCONTINUED|CANCELLED|EXPIRED|ERROR — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.status; Epic Orders Status Codes

attributes.name: new_value
attributes.description: The value of the modified clinical field immediately after this modification event. Paired with previous_value to form a complete before/after audit record. Contains PHI when the field relates to medication or clinical details.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); CDI Standards

attributes.name: order_number
attributes.description: The human-readable, externally visible order identifier (e.g., Epic order number, Cerner accession number) at the time of this event. Denormalized from the order header to support direct lookup in audit reports without joining to the order table.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium; Joint Commission RC.01.02.01

attributes.name: order_priority
attributes.description: The priority level of the order at the time of this event. Captures the priority as it existed at this point in the lifecycle, enabling detection of priority escalations or de-escalations over time.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.priority; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the clinical order category at the time of this event. Determines routing to downstream fulfillment systems: LAB → Beaker/LIS; RADIOLOGY → Radiant/RIS; PHARMACY → Willow; REFERRAL → Cadence. Denormalized here to support event-level analytics without joining back to the order header. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: LAB|RADIOLOGY|PHARMACY|REFERRAL|PROCEDURE|NURSING|DIET|CONSULT — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.category; Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium

attributes.name: override_reason
attributes.description: The structured or free-text reason provided by the provider when overriding a Clinical Decision Support (CDS) alert associated with this order event. Populated only when cds_alert_overridden is True. Supports patient safety review and quality improvement programs.
attributes.references: ONC 21st Century Cures Act; AHRQ Patient Safety; Joint Commission NPSG.03.06.01

attributes.name: previous_status
attributes.description: The order workflow status immediately before this lifecycle event. Enables reconstruction of the full state machine history and supports CDI review and medication reconciliation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DRAFT|PENDING|ACTIVE|HOLD|SUSPENDED|COMPLETED|DISCONTINUED|CANCELLED|EXPIRED|ERROR — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.status; Epic Orders Status Codes

attributes.name: previous_value
attributes.description: The value of the modified clinical field (dose, frequency, route, priority, quantity, etc.) immediately before this modification event. Stored as a string to accommodate heterogeneous field types across order categories. Populated only for MODIFICATION, AMENDMENT, and CORRECTION event types. Contains PHI when the field relates to medication or clinical details.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); CDI Standards

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Structured reason code explaining why this lifecycle event occurred (e.g., CLINICAL_CHANGE, PATIENT_REQUEST, PROVIDER_CORRECTION, DUPLICATE_ORDER, ALLERGY_ALERT, DRUG_INTERACTION, FORMULARY_SUBSTITUTION, PROTOCOL_CHANGE). Sourced from the EHR reason code catalog. Supports CDI and quality review workflows.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.reasonCode; Epic Orders; Joint Commission

attributes.name: reason_text
attributes.description: Free-text clinical justification or narrative explanation provided by the user or system for this lifecycle event. Supplements the structured reason_code with provider-authored context. May contain PHI when clinical rationale references patient-specific information.
attributes.references: Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); CDI Standards

attributes.name: renewal_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential counter indicating which renewal iteration this event represents for the parent order. Starts at 1 for the first renewal. Null for non-renewal events. Supports chronic medication management and long-term order tracking.
attributes.references: Epic Willow; Cerner PharmNet; Joint Commission MM.04.01.01

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record that generated this lifecycle event. Identifies the originating EHR module for data lineage and reconciliation purposes (e.g., EPIC_ORDERS for physician CPOE, WILLOW for pharmacy verification, BEAKER for lab order processing, RADIANT for radiology order management). attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 AuditEvent.source; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: transmission_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which this order event was transmitted to the downstream fulfillment system (Beaker, Radiant, Willow, etc.). Null if transmission is not required or has not yet occurred.

attributes.name: transmission_status

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this history record was last updated in the lakehouse silver layer. Although the event log is intended to be immutable, this field captures any correction or reprocessing events applied to the record for data quality purposes.

attributes.name: verbal_order_authentication_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which a verbal or telephone order was authenticated (signed) by the ordering provider. Null for non-verbal orders. Must occur within the timeframe required by Joint Commission standards (typically 24-48 hours).

attributes.name: workstation_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the clinical workstation, device, or terminal from which this order lifecycle event was initiated. Supports HIPAA access audit trails and security incident investigation.
