attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date after which the referral authorization is no longer valid and services cannot be rendered under this referral. Triggers re-authorization workflows and patient outreach when approaching expiry.
attributes.references: CMS Prior Authorization Rules; Epic EHR Resolute PB; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management

attributes.name: first_available_date
attributes.description: The earliest available appointment date offered by the receiving provider at the time the referral was processed. Used to measure access to specialty care and network adequacy.
attributes.references: NCQA HEDIS Access and Availability Measures; CMS Network Adequacy Standards; Salesforce Health Cloud

attributes.name: is_stat_order
attributes.description: Indicates whether the referral order was placed as a STAT (immediate/urgent) order requiring expedited processing and scheduling. Distinct from urgency_level as this is the operational flag used by scheduling and authorization workflows.
attributes.references: Epic EHR CPOE; Joint Commission; EMTALA

attributes.name: loop_closed_date
attributes.description: The date on which the referral communication loop was closed, meaning the referring provider received the specialist's consultation report or outcome documentation.
attributes.references: NCQA HEDIS; NCQA PCMH Standards; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management

attributes.name: mrn
attributes.description: The patient's Medical Record Number (MRN) as assigned by the facility's Master Patient Index (MPI). Included on the referral for cross-system patient identification and payer submission.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; Epic EHR MPI; Joint Commission Patient Identification Standards

attributes.name: order_placed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the referring provider placed the referral order via Computerized Physician Order Entry (CPOE) in the Electronic Health Record (EHR). This is the principal business event timestamp for the referral lifecycle.
attributes.references: Epic EHR CPOE; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.authoredOn; Joint Commission Documentation Standards

attributes.name: order_source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which the referral order was originated or ingested into the lakehouse. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and multi-system integration auditing.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; Salesforce Health Cloud; HL7 FHIR; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current workflow lifecycle state of the referral order. Drives downstream processing in Salesforce Health Cloud and Epic Orders. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|active|accepted|declined|completed|cancelled|expired — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.status; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management

attributes.name: plan_type
attributes.description: The type of health insurance plan governing the referral authorization requirements. HMO and POS plans typically require referrals; PPO plans may not. Drives authorization workflow logic. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HMO|PPO|POS|EPO|Medicare|Medicaid|self_pay — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CMS; NCQA; Epic EHR Resolute PB; HIPAA 45 CFR §162

attributes.name: receiving_facility_name
attributes.description: Name of the external facility or organization where the referred services will be rendered. Captured when the receiving provider is affiliated with an external organization not in the internal provider master.
attributes.references: Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; Epic EHR Orders Module; CMS Provider Enrollment

attributes.name: receiving_provider_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the specialist or receiving provider to whom the patient is referred. Required for payer authorization and claims adjudication.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA 45 CFR §162.406; CMS-1500; UB-04

attributes.name: referral_disposition
attributes.description: The outcome or final disposition of the referral as reported by the receiving provider. Indicates whether the specialist accepted, declined, completed, or the patient did not attend. Used for referral loop closure tracking and quality reporting.
attributes.references: Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; Epic EHR Orders Module; NCQA HEDIS; Joint Commission

attributes.name: referral_loop_closed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the referring provider has received and acknowledged the specialist's consultation report, closing the referral communication loop. A key quality metric for NCQA HEDIS and PCMH accreditation.
attributes.references: NCQA HEDIS; NCQA PCMH Standards; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; Epic EHR Healthy Planet

attributes.name: referral_number
attributes.description: Externally visible, human-readable business identifier for the referral order. Used in payer communications, patient correspondence, and cross-system tracking (e.g., Salesforce Health Cloud, Epic Orders). Format: REF- followed by 10 digits.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; CMS-1500 Claim Form

attributes.name: referral_reason_description
attributes.description: Free-text clinical narrative describing the reason for the referral, supplementing the ICD-10 code. Captures clinical context not fully expressed by the diagnosis code, such as symptom progression, treatment failure, or specific clinical question for the specialist.
attributes.references: Epic EHR ClinDoc; Joint Commission Documentation Standards; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.reasonCode

attributes.name: referral_source
attributes.description: The clinical setting or care context from which the referral originated. Indicates whether the referral was initiated by a Primary Care Physician (PCP), Emergency Department (ED), inpatient unit, specialist, patient self-referral, or care program enrollment.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: referral_type
attributes.description: Categorizes the nature of the referral: to a specialist, external provider, care program, second opinion, or for a specific diagnostic workup. Used for operational routing and analytics segmentation.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.category

attributes.name: referring_provider_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the referring provider as registered with CMS. Required on CMS-1500 and UB-04 claim forms and payer authorization requests.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA 45 CFR §162.406; CMS-1500; UB-04

attributes.name: scheduled_appointment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the patient's appointment with the receiving specialist or provider has been scheduled. Used to measure time-to-appointment and referral fulfillment timeliness.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Cadence; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; NCQA HEDIS Access and Availability Measures

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the referral order record was last modified in the lakehouse Silver layer. Supports change detection and incremental processing.

attributes.name: urgency_level
attributes.description: Clinical priority level assigned to the referral order by the referring provider. Drives scheduling priority at the receiving provider and payer authorization turnaround time requirements. Values: routine, urgent, stat, emergent.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Orders Module; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.priority; Joint Commission; EMTALA

attributes.name: visits_used
attributes.description: The number of authorized visits that have been consumed against this referral to date. Compared against authorized_visits to determine remaining utilization and trigger re-authorization alerts.
attributes.references: Epic EHR Resolute PB; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; CMS Prior Authorization Rules

products.name: set
products.description: Master record for pre-defined, evidence-based bundles of clinical orders (order sets) and their governing clinical protocols and care pathways. Captures order set name, clinical indication, specialty, version number, effective and expiration dates, approval status, approving committee, evidence-based guideline reference, associated DRG or care pathway, active/inactive flag, protocol governance attributes (governance level — guideline, consensus, regulatory mandate), clinical condition or diagnosis trigger (ICD-10), applicable care setting, owning clinical department, evidence level, parent protocol hierarchy, and approval workflow status. SSOT for both the executable order bundle and the clinical policy that governs its activation. Managed in Epic Orders and Cerner Millennium.
products.reference: Epic Order Set / Cerner Order Set Catalog

attributes.name: set_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the order set record in the lakehouse Silver layer. Primary key for the order_set data product.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the healthcare facility or campus where this order set is deployed and available for use. Supports multi-facility health system deployments where order sets may be facility-specific or enterprise-wide.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; CMS Facility Certification; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: cms_measure_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Measure ID
attributes.description: CMS quality measure identifier associated with this order set when is_cms_core_measure is True (e.g., 'SEP-1', 'VTE-1', 'STK-1'). Enables direct linkage to regulatory reporting requirements and Value-Based Purchasing (VBP) program metrics.
attributes.references: CMS Core Measures; Joint Commission (TJC) ORYX; HEDIS; NCQA

attributes.name: compliance_policy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.policy. Business justification: Order sets implement clinical policies (antibiotic stewardship policy, opioid prescribing policy). Direct policy-to-protocol relationship ensures order sets enforce organizational standards and regula

attributes.name: compliance_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: Order sets implement evidence-based protocols satisfying specific compliance programs (sepsis bundles for CMS SEP-1, VTE prophylaxis for Joint Commission). Direct link between clinical protocols and r

attributes.name: default_appointment_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to scheduling.appointment_type. Business justification: Order sets designed for specific appointment types (annual wellness visit order set, pre-operative order set) standardize care delivery. Linking order sets to appointment types enables protocol-driven

attributes.name: drg_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.drg. Business justification: DRG-based order sets support case management, utilization review, and cost containment initiatives. Links protocol to DRG master for expected LOS management, resource utilization tracking, and bundled

attributes.name: form_template_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to consent.consent_form_template. Business justification: Clinical order sets (surgical protocols, chemotherapy regimens) specify required consent forms. Protocol-driven consent management ensures correct consent template is presented when order set is activ

attributes.name: health_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to insurance.health_plan. Business justification: Health systems create plan-specific order sets for value-based care contracts, formulary compliance, and coverage optimization. Real-world process: clinical informatics teams build order sets aligned

attributes.name: icd_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.icd_code. Business justification: Order set activation logic depends on diagnosis-driven protocol triggering. Links to ICD-10 master enables automated clinical pathway initiation, evidence-based care delivery, and quality measure comp

attributes.name: parent_protocol_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent order set or protocol in a hierarchical protocol structure, enabling nested care pathway hierarchies (e.g., a sub-protocol within a broader sepsis management protocol). Null for top-level order sets with no parent.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR PlanDefinition

attributes.name: research_study_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to research.research_study. Business justification: Research protocols often define standardized order sets for study visits (baseline labs, imaging sequences, assessments). Linking order_set to research_study supports protocol adherence, study-specifi

attributes.name: set_approved_by_provider_clinician_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the physician or clinical leader who formally approved the order set on behalf of the approving committee. Supports governance accountability and regulatory audit requirements.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC); CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: set_clinician_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the clinician or clinical informaticist who originally authored and submitted the order set for governance review. Links to the provider master for accountability and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HIPAA Security Rule; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: specialty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to provider.specialty. Business justification: Order sets are specialty-specific clinical protocols (cardiology admission order sets, oncology treatment pathways). Healthcare organizations maintain specialty-based order set libraries, track specia

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the approving clinical committee formally approved the current version of the order set. Establishes the official governance record for audit and regulatory reporting purposes.
attributes.references: Joint Commission (TJC); CMS Conditions of Participation; HIM Governance

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval workflow status of the order set within the clinical governance process. Drives whether the order set is available for provider use in CPOE. 'draft' = under development; 'pending_review' = submitted to approving committee; 'approved' = active and available; 'retired' = superseded; 'suspended' = temporarily withdrawn.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC); CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: approving_committee
attributes.description: Name of the clinical governance committee or body responsible for reviewing and approving the order set (e.g., 'Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee', 'Medical Executive Committee', 'Clinical Quality Council'). Required for Joint Commission accreditation and CMS Conditions of Participation compliance.
attributes.references: Joint Commission (TJC); CMS Conditions of Participation; Medical Staff Bylaws

attributes.name: care_pathway_name
attributes.description: Name of the clinical care pathway or protocol bundle with which this order set is associated (e.g., 'Sepsis Care Pathway', 'Hip Replacement Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Pathway'). Links the executable order bundle to the broader clinical protocol framework.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC); AHRQ

attributes.name: care_setting
attributes.description: Clinical care setting in which the order set is intended to be used. Restricts order set availability to appropriate clinical contexts within the EHR. 'inpatient' = admitted patients; 'outpatient' = clinic/ambulatory; 'emergency' = Emergency Department (ED); 'icu' = Intensive Care Unit (ICU); 'surgical' = Operating Room (OR)/perioperative; 'observation' = observation status.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: clinical_indication
attributes.description: Free-text or structured description of the clinical condition, diagnosis, or scenario that triggers activation of this order set (e.g., 'Suspected sepsis with organ dysfunction', 'Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction'). Complements the ICD-10 trigger code.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; SNOMED CT; HL7 FHIR

attributes.name: compliance_rate_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of triggered clinical scenarios where the order set was activated by providers, as reported by the EHR analytics module. Sourced from Epic reporting or Cerner analytics — not computed in the lakehouse. Supports HEDIS, MIPS, and VBP quality measure reporting.
attributes.references: CMS MIPS; HEDIS; NCQA; VBP Program; Joint Commission (TJC) ORYX

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the order set record was first created in the source system or lakehouse. Supports audit trail requirements per HIPAA Security Rule, Joint Commission, and HIM governance policies.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164); Joint Commission (TJC); HIM Governance

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the order set version becomes clinically effective and available for provider use in CPOE. Aligns with the approved go-live date established by the governing clinical committee.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: evidence_level
attributes.description: Strength of clinical evidence supporting the order set, using standard evidence grading. 'A' = strong evidence from multiple randomized controlled trials; 'B' = moderate evidence; 'C' = limited evidence; 'D' = very limited evidence; 'expert_consensus' = based on expert opinion in absence of trials. Supports quality measurement and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: AHRQ Evidence-Based Practice; NCQA; Joint Commission (TJC); ACC/AHA Evidence Classification

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the order set version expires and is no longer valid for clinical use. Null indicates no scheduled expiration. Triggers mandatory review workflow when approaching expiration per clinical governance policy.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC); NCQA

attributes.name: fhir_plan_definition_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) PlanDefinition ID
attributes.description: HL7 FHIR PlanDefinition resource identifier corresponding to this order set, enabling interoperability with Health Information Exchange (HIE) platforms and external clinical decision support systems. Aligns with HL7 FHIR R4 PlanDefinition resource.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 PlanDefinition; ONC 21st Century Cures Act; HIE Standards

attributes.name: governance_level
attributes.description: Classification of the governance authority underpinning the order set protocol. 'guideline' = based on published clinical practice guidelines; 'consensus' = based on institutional expert consensus without external guideline; 'regulatory_mandate' = required by CMS, Joint Commission, or other regulatory body (e.g., CMS Core Measures, EMTALA requirements).
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; Joint Commission (TJC); OIG; AHRQ

attributes.name: guideline_reference
attributes.description: Citation or reference to the external clinical practice guideline, systematic review, or regulatory mandate that underpins the order set (e.g., 'Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 Guidelines', 'AHA/ACC STEMI Management Guidelines 2023', 'CMS Sepsis Core Measure SEP-1'). Supports clinical documentation improvement (CDI) and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: AHRQ; NCQA; CMS Core Measures; Joint Commission (TJC) ORYX; WHO

attributes.name: includes_lab_orders
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set bundle contains laboratory orders routed to Beaker (LIS) or equivalent Laboratory Information System (LIS). True = lab orders present; False = no lab orders included.

attributes.name: includes_pharmacy_orders
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set bundle contains medication orders routed to Willow (pharmacy) or equivalent pharmacy system. True = pharmacy/medication orders present; False = no pharmacy orders included. Relevant for DEA controlled substance tracking.
attributes.references: Epic Willow; Cerner PharmNet; DEA Controlled Substances; NDC Standards

attributes.name: includes_radiology_orders
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set bundle contains radiology/imaging orders routed to Radiant (RIS) or equivalent Radiology Information System (RIS). True = radiology orders present; False = no radiology orders included.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant (RIS); Cerner RadNet; PACS Standards

attributes.name: includes_referral_orders
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set bundle contains referral orders to specialists or ancillary services. True = referral orders present; False = no referral orders included. Supports care coordination and transitions of care workflows.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set is currently active and available for selection in the CPOE workflow. True = active and selectable by providers; False = inactive and hidden from the order entry interface. Distinct from approval_status — an approved order set may be temporarily deactivated without retiring it.

attributes.name: is_cms_core_measure
attributes.business_glossary_term: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Core Measure Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this order set is directly associated with a CMS Core Measure or quality reporting requirement (e.g., SEP-1 Sepsis Bundle, VTE Prophylaxis). True = linked to a CMS Core Measure; False = not a CMS Core Measure order set. Supports quality measurement and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: CMS Core Measures; Joint Commission (TJC) ORYX; AHRQ; VBP Program

attributes.name: is_hipaa_sensitive
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Sensitive Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set is associated with HIPAA-sensitive clinical categories requiring enhanced access controls (e.g., behavioral health, substance use disorder, HIV/AIDS, reproductive health). True = sensitive category requiring additional PHI protections; False = standard clinical order set.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164); 42 CFR Part 2 (Substance Use Disorder); OCR HIPAA Enforcement

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent clinical review of the order set, regardless of whether a version change resulted. Supports mandatory periodic review cycles (typically annual) required by Joint Commission and institutional policy.
attributes.references: Joint Commission (TJC); NCQA; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Date by which the next mandatory clinical review of the order set must be completed. Drives governance workflow alerts and ensures compliance with periodic review requirements per Joint Commission and institutional policy.
attributes.references: Joint Commission (TJC); NCQA; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: order_count
attributes.description: Total number of individual clinical orders (lab, radiology, pharmacy, nursing, referral) included in the order set bundle. Provides a quick indicator of order set complexity and scope for provider review.

attributes.name: order_set_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the order set within the source system (e.g., Epic Orders catalog ID or Cerner Millennium order set mnemonic). Used for cross-system referencing and integration with Beaker (LIS), Radiant (RIS), and Willow (pharmacy).

attributes.name: order_set_type
attributes.description: Classification of the order set by its clinical purpose in the care continuum. 'admission' = admission orders bundle; 'discharge' = discharge planning orders; 'procedure' = pre/intra/post-procedure orders; 'condition' = condition-specific management bundle; 'preventive' = preventive care protocol; 'transition' = transitions of care orders.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: owning_department
attributes.description: Name of the clinical department or service line that owns and is responsible for maintaining the order set (e.g., 'Department of Cardiology', 'Emergency Medicine', 'Pharmacy'). Establishes accountability for content governance and periodic review.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: population_age_group
attributes.description: Target patient age group for which the order set is clinically appropriate. Restricts order set availability to appropriate patient populations in CPOE. 'pediatric' = patients under 18; 'adult' = 18-64; 'geriatric' = 65+; 'neonatal' = newborns; 'all' = all age groups.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; AAP Pediatric Guidelines; CMS

attributes.name: renal_adjustment_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order set contains medications requiring renal function-based dose adjustments (e.g., creatinine clearance-based dosing). True = renal adjustment logic embedded; False = no renal adjustment required. Supports clinical decision support (CDS) alerts in CPOE.
attributes.references: Epic Willow; Cerner PharmNet; FDA Drug Labeling; AHRQ Medication Safety

attributes.name: set_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the order set's clinical purpose, intended patient population, and scope of included orders. Supports clinical documentation improvement (CDI) and provider education.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: set_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the pre-defined, evidence-based order set bundle as displayed in the Computerized Physician Order Entry (CPOE) interface (e.g., 'Sepsis Bundle — Adult ICU', 'Community-Acquired Pneumonia Admission Orders').
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; CPOE Standards

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which the order set was sourced. 'epic' = Epic Orders/CPOE; 'cerner' = Cerner Millennium PowerChart; 'meditech' = MEDITECH Expanse; 'manual' = manually entered outside a standard EHR system.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; MEDITECH Expanse; HL7 FHIR

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Native identifier of the order set in the originating operational system (e.g., Epic Orders internal record ID, Cerner Millennium order set catalog ID). Supports ETL lineage tracking and cross-system reconciliation.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HL7 FHIR

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the order set record in the source system or lakehouse. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and ETL incremental load processing.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164); Joint Commission (TJC); HIM Governance; ISO 27001

attributes.name: usage_count
attributes.description: Cumulative count of the number of times this order set version has been activated by providers in CPOE. Supports utilization analytics, adoption tracking, and clinical quality improvement initiatives. Not a calculated aggregate — sourced directly from the EHR order set activation log.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HEDIS; NCQA Quality Reporting

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Semantic version number of the order set (e.g., '1.0', '2.3', '3.1.2'). Incremented upon each approved revision to support version control, audit trails, and rollback capabilities per Health Information Management (HIM) governance requirements.
attributes.references: Epic Orders; Cerner Millennium PowerChart; HIM Governance

attributes.name: weight_based_dosing
attributes.description: Indicates whether any pharmacy orders within the order set use weight-based dosing calculations (e.g., mg/kg). True = weight-based dosing required; False = fixed dosing. Critical for pediatric and oncology order sets and for pharmacy safety validation in Willow/PharmNet.
attributes.references: Epic Willow; Cerner PharmNet; DEA; FDA Drug Safety

products.name: set_item
products.description: Individual order line within an order set, defining each component order that is pre-configured for a care pathway. Captures the parent order set, sequence number, order type, default values (dose, frequency, priority, route), mandatory vs. optional flag, conditional inclusion logic (e.g., if lab value exceeds threshold then include order), conditional logic trigger criteria, age/weight/diagnosis-based inclusion rules, clinical rationale, and alternative order options. Enables granular management of order set content and supports clinical decision support (CDS) rule evaluation at the item level. SSOT for the composition and conditional logic of order set bundles.
products.reference: Epic Order Set Component / Cerner Order Set Detail

attributes.name: set_item_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the order set item. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: primary_set_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user who created this order set item. Supports accountability and audit requirements for clinical content governance.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Governance

attributes.name: set_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent order set that contains this item. Links this item to its containing order set bundle.

attributes.name: age_max_years
attributes.description: Maximum patient age in years for which this order item is appropriate. Used for age-based inclusion rules. Null indicates no maximum age restriction.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Age Restrictions

attributes.name: age_min_years
attributes.description: Minimum patient age in years for which this order item is appropriate. Used for age-based inclusion rules. Null indicates no minimum age restriction.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Age Restrictions

attributes.name: alternative_order_options
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of alternative order codes that can be substituted for this item. Supports clinical flexibility and formulary management.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Alternatives

attributes.name: body_site
attributes.description: Anatomical location where the procedure or specimen collection should be performed. Uses standardized anatomical terminology.
attributes.references: SNOMED CT Body Structure, HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.bodySite

attributes.name: clinical_rationale
attributes.description: Evidence-based justification for including this order in the care pathway. May reference clinical guidelines, protocols, or best practices. Supports clinical decision support.

attributes.name: collection_method
attributes.description: Method by which the specimen should be collected for laboratory orders (e.g., venipuncture, clean catch, biopsy). Ensures proper specimen quality.

attributes.name: condition_expression
attributes.description: Formal expression defining the conditional logic criteria (e.g., age > 65, weight < 50kg, diagnosis = ICD-10:E11.9). Uses clinical decision support (CDS) rule syntax.

attributes.name: condition_type
attributes.description: Category of conditional logic applied to this item. Determines which patient data elements are evaluated for inclusion/exclusion decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: age_based|weight_based|diagnosis_based|lab_value|allergy|medication_interaction|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: conditional_inclusion_logic
attributes.description: Rule expression defining when this item should be automatically included or excluded from the order set. Evaluated at order set activation time based on patient context.

attributes.name: contrast_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether contrast media should be used for radiology imaging orders. Affects patient preparation and allergy screening requirements.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this order set item record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: default_dose
attributes.description: Pre-configured dose amount for medication orders. May include numeric value and unit (e.g., 500 mg, 10 mL). Can be overridden at order entry.

attributes.name: default_duration
attributes.description: Pre-configured duration for time-limited orders (e.g., 7 days, 2 weeks). Primarily used for medication orders with a defined treatment period.

attributes.name: default_frequency
attributes.description: Pre-configured administration or execution frequency for this order (e.g., BID, TID, QD, Q4H). Primarily used for medication and nursing orders.

attributes.name: default_priority
attributes.description: Pre-configured priority level for this order item. Can be overridden by the ordering provider at the time of order entry.

attributes.name: default_quantity
attributes.description: Pre-configured quantity for orders that require a count or volume (e.g., number of units to dispense, volume of fluid to administer).

attributes.name: default_route
attributes.description: Pre-configured administration route for medication orders (e.g., oral, intravenous, intramuscular, subcutaneous). Can be overridden at order entry.

attributes.name: diagnosis_criteria
attributes.description: ICD-10 diagnosis codes or diagnosis categories that must be present for this item to be included. Supports comma-separated list for multiple diagnoses.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this order set item is no longer available for use. Null indicates the item remains effective indefinitely. Supports order set retirement and updates.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this order set item becomes available for use. Supports versioning and phased rollout of order set changes.

attributes.name: instruction_text
attributes.description: Additional instructions or guidance for the ordering provider or fulfillment team. Displayed during order entry and on order requisitions.

attributes.name: is_default_selected
attributes.description: Indicates whether this item is pre-selected by default when the order set is opened. Providers can deselect optional items.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Configuration

attributes.name: is_mandatory
attributes.description: Indicates whether this order item must be included when the order set is activated. True means the item cannot be deselected by the ordering provider.
attributes.references: Epic Orders Module - Order Set Item Configuration

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this order set item record was most recently updated. Supports change tracking and version control.

attributes.name: laterality

products.name: fulfillment
products.description: Transactional record capturing the completion or execution of a clinical order by the fulfilling department, serving as the order domain's acknowledgment that downstream work was performed. Captures fulfillment datetime, fulfilling provider or technician, fulfillment location, fulfillment method, actual vs. ordered quantity, partial fulfillment indicator, fulfillment notes, exception reason if the order was not fulfilled as ordered, fulfillment status, and turnaround time (order-to-fulfillment elapsed time). Bridges the order intent (clinical_order) with the result or dispensing event in downstream domains (laboratory, radiology, pharmacy). Detailed result data (lab values, imaging reports, dispensing records) is owned by the respective downstream domain — laboratory, radiology, or pharmacy.

products.name: verbal_order
products.description: Operational record capturing verbal orders, telephone orders, and all co-signature/countersignature events for clinical orders requiring dual authorization. For verbal/telephone orders: captures receiving nurse or clinician, ordering provider identity, order content, datetime received, read-back confirmation flag, read-back datetime, authentication deadline (typically 24-48 hours per TJC/CMS policy), authentication datetime, and authentication status. products.name: cpoe_alert
products.description: Operational record of every clinical decision support (CDS) alert fired during CPOE order entry within the order domain workflow. Captures alert type (drug-drug interaction, drug-allergy, duplicate order, dose range check, contraindication, formulary substitution, critical lab value), alert severity (hard stop, soft stop, informational), alert trigger details, provider response (accepted, overridden, modified), override reason code, alert fire datetime, and the clinical_order that triggered the alert. Placed in the order domain because alerts are generated as part of the CPOE ordering workflow and require real-time integration with order entry screens; downstream CDS rule management and knowledge base maintenance are owned by the clinical/quality domain. Supports medication safety surveillance, alert fatigue analysis, CMS Meaningful Use CDS requirements, and CDS optimization programs.

products.name: drug_master

Serves as the pharmacy-owned SSOT for drug attributes consumed by prescribing, dispensing, administration, and inventory workflows. Distinct from reference domain NDC code sets — this product adds pharmacy-operational attributes (formulary status, ISMP flags, hazardous drug classification). Sourced from Epic Willow and Cerner PharmNet drug dictionaries.

attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug requires dosing adjustments or special considerations for geriatric patients due to altered pharmacokinetics or increased sensitivity.

attributes.name: hazardous_drug_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug is classified as hazardous per NIOSH criteria, requiring special handling, personal protective equipment, and disposal procedures to protect healthcare workers.

attributes.name: hepatic_dosing_adjustment_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug requires dosing adjustments for patients with hepatic impairment or liver disease.

attributes.name: ismp_high_alert_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institute for Safe Medication Practices (ISMP) High-Alert Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug is classified as high-alert by ISMP, meaning it carries heightened risk of causing significant patient harm when used in error.

attributes.name: lactation_risk_category
attributes.description: The classification indicating the drug's safety profile for use during breastfeeding and potential risks to nursing infants.
attributes.references: FDA Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule

attributes.name: lasa_drug_pairs
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of drug names that are commonly confused with this drug due to similar appearance or pronunciation, used for clinical decision support and error prevention.

attributes.name: lasa_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug has been identified as having look-alike or sound-alike characteristics with other medications, requiring additional safety measures to prevent confusion.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this drug master record was most recently modified or updated.

attributes.name: light_sensitive_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug is photosensitive and requires protection from light exposure during storage and handling.

attributes.name: manufacturer_labeler_code
attributes.description: The first segment of the NDC identifying the labeler or manufacturer, assigned by the FDA.

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: The name of the pharmaceutical company or labeler responsible for manufacturing and distributing the drug product.

attributes.name: multi_dose_vial_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug is packaged as a multi-dose vial that can be used for multiple patient administrations, requiring special dating and handling protocols.

attributes.name: ndc
attributes.description: FDA-assigned National Drug Code uniquely identifying the drug product, including labeler, product, and package segments. The authoritative pharmaceutical product identifier in the United States.

attributes.name: package_size
attributes.description: The quantity of drug units contained in the standard package or container (e.g., 100 tablets, 10 mL vial, 30-day supply).

attributes.name: package_type
attributes.description: The type of container or packaging in which the drug is supplied (e.g., Bottle, Blister Pack, Vial, Ampule, Syringe, Box).

attributes.name: pediatric_approved_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug has FDA approval for use in pediatric populations with established dosing and safety data.

attributes.name: pregnancy_category
attributes.description: The FDA pregnancy category or Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule (PLLR) classification indicating the drug's safety profile for use during pregnancy.
attributes.references: FDA Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule

attributes.name: refrigeration_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug requires refrigerated storage conditions to maintain stability and efficacy.

attributes.name: rems_required_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the FDA requires a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy program for this drug to ensure that benefits outweigh risks.

attributes.name: renal_dosing_adjustment_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the drug requires dosing adjustments for patients with renal impairment based on creatinine clearance or glomerular filtration rate.

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: The path by which the drug is administered into the body (e.g., Oral, Intravenous, Intramuscular, Subcutaneous, Topical, Inhalation, Ophthalmic).
attributes.references: FDA Route of Administration Terminology, HL7 FHIR

attributes.name: rxnorm_code
attributes.description: The standardized nomenclature code from the National Library of Medicine's RxNorm system, used for semantic interoperability and clinical decision support across health IT systems.

attributes.name: snomed_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) Code
attributes.description: The SNOMED CT concept identifier for the drug, enabling standardized clinical terminology and interoperability with Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems.

attributes.name: storage_temperature_range
attributes.description: The recommended temperature range for proper storage of the drug to maintain potency and safety (e.g., 2-8°C, 15-30°C, Room Temperature).

attributes.name: strength
attributes.description: The amount of active pharmaceutical ingredient per dosage unit, expressed with numeric value and unit of measure (e.g., 500 mg, 10 mg/mL, 0.5%).

attributes.name: tall_man_lettering
attributes.description: The drug name displayed with mixed-case capitalization to emphasize differences between look-alike drug names and reduce medication errors (e.g., hydrOXYzine vs hydrALAzine).

attributes.name: therapeutic_category
attributes.description: The clinical therapeutic category indicating the primary disease state or condition the drug is used to treat (e.g., Cardiovascular, Antibiotic, Analgesic, Antidiabetic).

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The standard unit used to quantify the drug for inventory, dispensing, and administration purposes (e.g., Each, Milliliter, Gram, Vial, Patch).

products.name: formulary
products.description: Defines the approved drug formulary for each health plan, payer, or facility tier. Captures formulary tier (preferred/non-preferred/specialty), prior authorization requirements, step therapy requirements, quantity limits, formulary effective and expiration dates, therapeutic alternatives, payer-specific coverage rules, and specialty drug classification. Supports formulary management, clinical decision support at point of prescribing, and prescription adjudication. Benefit plan financial details (copay/coinsurance schedules, deductible applicability, mail-order benefit rules) are sourced from the billing domain; this product owns drug-level coverage and access rules only. Sourced from Epic Willow and Cerner PharmNet formulary modules.

attributes.name: age_restriction_max
attributes.description: Maximum patient age (in years) for which this drug is covered under the formulary. Null if no maximum age restriction applies.

attributes.name: age_restriction_min
attributes.description: Minimum patient age (in years) for which this drug is covered under the formulary. Null if no minimum age restriction applies.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when this formulary entry was officially approved for inclusion in the formulary. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual or committee that approved this formulary entry (e.g., P&T Committee, Chief Pharmacy Officer).

attributes.name: clinical_review_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether clinical review by a pharmacist or physician is required before dispensing. True if clinical review is mandatory.

attributes.name: controlled_substance_schedule
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Controlled Substance Schedule
attributes.description: DEA schedule classification for controlled substances. Schedule II drugs have high abuse potential, Schedule V have lowest. Non-controlled if not a controlled substance.

attributes.name: coverage_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the drug is covered under this formulary. Conditional or restricted coverage requires additional criteria to be met.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this formulary record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: days_supply_limit
attributes.description: Maximum number of days supply that can be dispensed per prescription under this formulary. Common values are 30, 60, or 90 days.

attributes.name: diagnosis_restriction
attributes.description: ICD-10 diagnosis codes or clinical conditions for which this drug is covered. May be a comma-separated list or reference to a diagnosis group.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this formulary entry becomes active and coverage rules take effect. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this formulary entry expires and coverage rules are no longer in effect. Null for open-ended formularies. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: formulary_name
attributes.description: Business name or label for this formulary (e.g., 'Commercial Preferred Formulary 2024', 'Medicare Part D Standard Formulary').

attributes.name: formulary_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this formulary entry. Active entries are in effect, inactive are not currently used, pending are awaiting approval.

attributes.name: formulary_tier
attributes.description: The tier classification of the drug within the formulary, determining patient cost-sharing and coverage level. Tier 1 typically has lowest cost-sharing, Tier 5 for specialty drugs.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Part D Formulary Standards

attributes.name: formulary_type
attributes.description: Type or category of formulary, typically aligned with payer type or benefit plan category (e.g., commercial, Medicare Part D, Medicaid).

attributes.name: gender_restriction
attributes.description: Gender restriction for coverage of this drug under the formulary. Some drugs may be covered only for specific genders based on clinical indication.

attributes.name: generic_substitution_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether generic substitution is permitted for this drug under the formulary. True if pharmacist may substitute with generic equivalent.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this formulary record was last updated or modified. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: last_reviewed_date
attributes.description: Date when this formulary entry was last reviewed by the Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) committee or formulary management team. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: mail_order_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this drug is eligible for mail-order pharmacy fulfillment under the formulary. True if mail-order is available.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next formulary review of this entry. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments about this formulary entry, including special instructions, clinical guidance, or administrative notes for pharmacists and prescribers.

attributes.name: pharmacy_network_restriction
attributes.description: Indicates which pharmacy network tier or type is required for dispensing this drug under the formulary (e.g., specialty pharmacy only, preferred network).

attributes.name: prior_authorization_criteria
attributes.description: Detailed clinical or administrative criteria that must be met for prior authorization approval. May reference diagnosis codes, lab values, or prior treatment history.

attributes.name: prior_authorization_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether prior authorization from the payer is required before the drug can be dispensed. True if PA is mandatory.

attributes.name: quantity_limit
attributes.description: Maximum quantity of the drug that can be dispensed per prescription or per time period under this formulary. Null if no quantity limit applies.

attributes.name: refill_limit
attributes.description: Maximum number of refills allowed for this drug under the formulary. Null if no refill limit applies or unlimited refills are permitted.

attributes.name: specialty_drug_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this drug is classified as a specialty drug requiring special handling, distribution, or patient management. True if specialty drug.

attributes.name: step_therapy_protocol
attributes.description: Description of the step therapy protocol, including which alternative medications must be tried first and for how long before this drug is covered.

attributes.name: step_therapy_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether step therapy (trial of alternative medications) is required before this drug is covered. True if step therapy protocol must be followed.

attributes.name: therapeutic_alternative_available
attributes.description: Indicates whether therapeutic alternatives (drugs with similar clinical effect) are available on the formulary. True if alternatives exist.

attributes.name: therapeutic_class_code
attributes.description: Standardized therapeutic class code for the drug (e.g., AHFS, ETC, or internal classification). Used for formulary management and therapeutic interchange.

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version identifier for the formulary, used to track changes and updates over time (e.g., '2024.1', 'Q1-2024').

Sourced from Epic Willow and Cerner PharmNet.

products.name: medication_review
products.description: This association product represents the clinical review of a specific prescription during a Medication Therapy Management (MTM) session. It captures the pharmacist's assessment, interventions, and outcomes for each prescription evaluated during the MTM encounter. Each record links one MTM session to one prescription with clinical findings, drug therapy problems, interventions, and prescriber communications that exist only in the context of reviewing that specific prescription during that specific MTM session.. Existence Justification: In healthcare pharmacy operations, MTM sessions routinely involve comprehensive review of multiple prescriptions simultaneously (a patient typically has 5-15 active prescriptions reviewed in one MTM session), and individual prescriptions are reviewed repeatedly over time during different MTM encounters as part of ongoing medication safety monitoring. Pharmacists document specific clinical findings, drug therapy problems, interventions, and outcomes for each prescription within each MTM session, creating relationship data that belongs neither to the MTM session alone nor to the prescription alone.

products.name: study_drug_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the investigational product allocation between drug_master and research_study. It captures the assignment of specific drugs to specific research studies, including arm-specific dosing protocols, blinding status, randomization details, and protocol version tracking. Each record links one drug to one study with attributes that exist only in the context of this research relationship. Supports drug accountability, formulary planning, and protocol compliance workflows managed by research pharmacists.. Existence Justification: Clinical research studies routinely test multiple drugs simultaneously (combination therapy, dose-ranging arms, active comparators vs. investigational agents), and each drug participates in multiple studies across different phases, indications, and institutions. Research pharmacists actively manage study-drug assignments as operational entities with arm-specific dosing protocols, blinding requirements, randomization tracking, and protocol version linkage. The business refers to these as 'study drug assignments' or 'investigational product allocations' and manages them for drug accountability, formulary planning, and regulatory compliance.

products.name: pharmacy_network_participation
products.description: This association product represents the contractual participation relationship between pharmacy locations and payer provider networks. It captures which pharmacies are in-network for which payer networks, the terms of participation, and network-specific reimbursement arrangements. Each record links one pharmacy location to one provider network with attributes that exist only in the context of this participation agreement.. Existence Justification: Pharmacy network participation is a genuine operational many-to-many relationship in healthcare. Each pharmacy location participates in multiple payer networks simultaneously (a CVS pharmacy accepts BCBS, Aetna, UnitedHealthcare, Cigna networks), and each provider network includes hundreds to thousands of pharmacy locations. The business actively manages these participation relationships with network-specific terms including tier status, reimbursement schedules, effective dates, and participation status.

products.name: lab_order
products.description: Core transactional record of every laboratory test order placed via CPOE (Computerized Physician Order Entry) in Epic Beaker or Cerner PathNet, including orders routed to external reference laboratories (send-outs). products.name: specimen
products.description: Master record for every biological specimen collected for laboratory testing and the SSOT for specimen identity, accessioning, chain of custody, and full specimen lifecycle. Tracks specimen type (blood, urine, tissue, CSF, swab), collection method, collection date/time, collector identity and role, collection site (body location), container type, volume, accession number (LIS-assigned unique work-unit identifier), accession date/time, accession status (received, processing, resulted, archived), receiving lab location, priority, chain-of-custody status, storage location, specimen condition at receipt, number of aliquots, and disposal/retention status. Consolidates the former accession and specimen collection event concepts — the accession is the specimen's operational identity in Epic Beaker and Cerner PathNet. Supports CLIA-compliant specimen tracking from collection through accessioning, testing, and disposal.

products.name: test_result
products.description: Transactional record of every individual laboratory test result produced for a specimen, including result amendments and critical value notifications. Stores LOINC-coded test identifier, result value (numeric, text, coded), result unit of measure, reference range applied, result status lifecycle (preliminary, final, corrected, cancelled), abnormal flag (normal, low, high, critical low, critical high), result date/time, performing lab section, instrument identifier, verifying technologist. Owns the full amendment/correction history: original value, amended value, amendment reason, amending user, amendment timestamp. When a result exceeds critical thresholds, owns the critical value alert lifecycle: alert generation timestamp, notified provider, notification method (phone, secure message, EHR alert), acknowledgment timestamp, acknowledging clinician, escalation actions, and resolution notes. Consolidates the former critical_value_alert and result_amendment concepts. Supports CLIA critical value compliance, Joint Commission NPSG requirements, HIM audit requirements, and downstream clinical decision-making.

attributes.name: tertiary_test_ordering_provider_clinician_id

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical encounter or visit during which this test was ordered or resulted. Links to the visit record.

attributes.name: abnormal_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of whether the result falls outside the normal reference range. Values include normal, low, high, critical_low, critical_high, or abnormal for non-numeric results.

attributes.name: amendment_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the result was amended or corrected. Critical for audit trail and understanding result history.

attributes.name: amendment_reason
attributes.description: Documented reason for amending or correcting the result (e.g., transcription error, instrument malfunction, specimen mix-up, calculation error). Required for CLIA compliance.

attributes.name: clia_number
attributes.description: CLIA certification number of the laboratory that performed the test. Federally required identifier for all clinical laboratories performing testing on human specimens.

attributes.name: created_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when this test result record was first created in the system. Audit timestamp for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: critical_value_acknowledgment_datetime
attributes.business_glossary_term: Critical Value Acknowledgment Date and Time
attributes.description: Date and time when the provider acknowledged receipt and understanding of the critical value. Completes the critical value notification loop.

attributes.name: critical_value_alert_generated_datetime
attributes.business_glossary_term: Critical Value Alert Generated Date and Time
attributes.description: Date and time when the critical value alert was generated by the Laboratory Information System (LIS). Marks the start of the critical value notification workflow.

attributes.name: critical_value_escalation_action
attributes.description: Description of escalation actions taken if initial notification was unsuccessful (e.g., contacted backup provider, notified charge nurse, paged on-call physician).

attributes.name: critical_value_notification_datetime
attributes.business_glossary_term: Critical Value Notification Date and Time
attributes.description: Date and time when the critical value notification was successfully delivered to the provider. Used to calculate notification turnaround time.

attributes.name: critical_value_notification_method
attributes.description: Method used to notify the provider of the critical value (e.g., phone, secure message, EHR alert, page). Required for compliance documentation.

attributes.name: critical_value_resolution_note
attributes.description: Free-text note documenting the resolution of the critical value alert, including any clinical actions taken or follow-up orders placed.

attributes.name: is_amended
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this result has been amended or corrected after initial release. Triggers amendment tracking and notification workflows.

attributes.name: is_critical_value
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this result exceeds critical thresholds requiring immediate clinical notification. Triggers critical value alert workflow.

attributes.name: last_updated_datetime
attributes.business_glossary_term: Record Last Updated Date and Time
attributes.description: Date and time when this test result record was last modified. Audit timestamp for tracking changes and data quality.

attributes.name: original_result_value_numeric
attributes.description: Original numeric result value before amendment or correction. Preserved for audit trail and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: original_result_value_text
attributes.description: Original text result value before amendment or correction. Preserved for audit trail and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: performing_lab_facility
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the laboratory facility that performed the test. May be internal lab or external reference lab. Required for CLIA compliance.

attributes.name: performing_lab_section
attributes.description: Laboratory section or department that performed the test (e.g., Chemistry, Hematology, Microbiology, Pathology). Used for operational tracking and quality control.

attributes.name: result_comment
attributes.description: Additional comments, notes, or observations about the test result. May include technical notes, specimen quality issues, or other relevant information.

attributes.name: result_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the laboratory test result was produced or finalized. Represents the official result timestamp for clinical and regulatory purposes.

attributes.name: result_interpretation
attributes.description: Clinical interpretation or commentary provided by the laboratory professional regarding the result. May include clinical significance, recommendations, or contextual notes.

attributes.name: result_released_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the result was officially released from the laboratory and made available to clinicians. Used for turnaround time calculations.

attributes.name: result_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the test result. Tracks progression from preliminary through final, and captures corrections or cancellations. Critical for clinical decision-making and compliance.

attributes.name: result_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the numeric result value (e.g., mg/dL, mmol/L, cells/uL). Critical for clinical interpretation and comparison against reference ranges.
attributes.references: UCUM - Unified Code for Units of Measure

attributes.name: result_value_coded
attributes.description: Standardized coded value for the test result using terminology systems such as SNOMED CT. Enables structured data exchange and analytics.

attributes.name: result_value_numeric
attributes.description: Numeric value of the laboratory test result for quantitative tests. Stores the measured value with precision appropriate for clinical decision-making.

attributes.name: result_value_text
attributes.description: Text or string value of the laboratory test result for qualitative tests, narrative findings, or coded results. Used when result cannot be expressed numerically.

attributes.name: specimen_received_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the specimen was received in the laboratory. Used for tracking specimen handling and turnaround time metrics.

products.name: reference_range
products.description: Reference data defining normal, abnormal, and critical value thresholds for each laboratory test, stratified by patient demographics (age group, sex, pregnancy status, race/ethnicity where clinically validated) and specimen type. Includes lower and upper normal limits, critical low and critical high thresholds, panic value definitions, unit of measure, effective date range, and the authoritative source (CAP, CLIA, manufacturer insert, institutional medical director override). Used by result interpretation logic to assign abnormal flags and trigger critical value alerts in test_result. Supports CLIA-required documentation of reference range sources and periodic review.
products.reference: Lab Reference Range — CAP / CLIA

attributes.name: reference_range_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the laboratory reference range record. Primary key.

attributes.name: loinc_code_id

attributes.name: test_catalog_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.test_catalog. Business justification: Reference ranges are defined FOR specific tests in the catalog. Currently reference_range has test_code/test_name but no FK to test_catalog. Business reality: reference ranges are test-specific and sh

attributes.name: age_group
attributes.description: Age group or age range for which this reference range applies (e.g., Neonate, Infant, Child, Adolescent, Adult, Geriatric, or specific age ranges like 0-1 years, 1-12 years, 18-65 years). Reference ranges are age-dependent for many tests.

attributes.name: alert_priority
attributes.description: Priority level for clinical alerts triggered when results fall outside this reference range. Critical priority requires immediate notification within minutes; urgent within hours; routine for next business day review.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) NPSG.02.03.01 Critical Test Results

attributes.name: alert_trigger_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether results outside this reference range should trigger automated clinical alerts or notifications. True for critical value ranges requiring immediate provider notification per Joint Commission requirements.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) NPSG.02.03.01 Critical Test Results

attributes.name: clinical_significance
attributes.description: Clinical interpretation guidance describing the significance of values outside this reference range. Provides context for clinicians interpreting abnormal results (e.g., elevated values may indicate infection, dehydration, or malignancy).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this reference range record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: critical_high_threshold
attributes.description: The critical high value threshold (panic value) above which immediate clinical notification is required. Represents life-threatening high values requiring urgent intervention.
attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA), The Joint Commission (TJC) NPSG.02.03.01

attributes.name: critical_low_threshold
attributes.description: The critical low value threshold (panic value) below which immediate clinical notification is required. Represents life-threatening low values requiring urgent intervention.
attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA), The Joint Commission (TJC) NPSG.02.03.01

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date through which this reference range remains valid. Null indicates the range is currently active with no planned end date. Supports historical tracking and periodic review requirements.
attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Quality Control Requirements

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this reference range becomes valid and should be used for result interpretation. Supports versioning of reference ranges over time.
attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Quality Control Requirements

attributes.name: instrument_platform
attributes.description: Specific laboratory instrument or analyzer platform for which this reference range is validated (e.g., Roche Cobas, Abbott Architect, Siemens Atellica). Different platforms may require different reference ranges.

attributes.name: interpretation_code
attributes.description: Standardized code used by result interpretation logic to assign abnormal flags when test results fall outside this reference range. Maps to HL7 observation interpretation codes.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date when this reference range was last reviewed and validated by the laboratory medical director or quality team. CLIA and CAP require periodic review of reference ranges at least annually or when methodology changes.
attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) 42 CFR 493.1253, College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation Requirements

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this reference range record was last modified. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: lis_system_code
attributes.description: Internal system code or identifier used by the Laboratory Information System (Epic Beaker, Cerner PathNet) to reference this range in result interpretation logic and reporting.

attributes.name: lower_normal_limit
attributes.description: The lower boundary of the normal reference range. Values below this threshold are typically flagged as low or abnormal.

attributes.name: medical_director_override_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reference range represents an institutional medical director override of standard published ranges. True if the laboratory medical director has approved a deviation from manufacturer or published ranges based on local population characteristics.
attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) 42 CFR 493.1253, College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation Requirements

attributes.name: methodology
attributes.description: The analytical method or instrument platform used to establish this reference range (e.g., Spectrophotometry, Immunoassay, Mass Spectrometry, PCR). Reference ranges may vary by methodology for the same test.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review of this reference range. Supports compliance with CLIA and CAP requirements for annual review and documentation.
attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) 42 CFR 493.1253, College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation Requirements

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or special instructions related to this reference range. May include information about interfering substances, pre-analytical requirements, or special patient populations.

attributes.name: override_justification
attributes.description: Clinical justification and documentation for medical director override of standard reference ranges. Required when medical_director_override_flag is true. Includes rationale, supporting data, and approval documentation.
attributes.references: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) 42 CFR 493.1253, College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation Requirements

attributes.name: population_basis
attributes.description: Description of the reference population used to establish this range (e.g., healthy adult volunteers, local patient population, manufacturer validation study). Documents the basis for the reference interval per CLSI guidelines.

attributes.name: pregnancy_status
attributes.description: Pregnancy status for which this reference range applies. Certain laboratory values have distinct reference ranges during pregnancy (e.g., thyroid function tests, hemoglobin).

attributes.name: race_ethnicity
attributes.description: Race or ethnicity group for which this reference range applies, when clinically validated differences exist (e.g., creatinine clearance adjustments for African American patients). Only populated when evidence-based clinical guidelines support race-specific ranges.
attributes.references: CDC Race and Ethnicity Code Set, National Institutes of Health (NIH) Guidelines

attributes.name: review_status
attributes.description: Current review and approval status of this reference range. Tracks lifecycle state for quality management and compliance purposes.
attributes.references: College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation Requirements

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: Number of individuals in the reference population used to establish this range. CLSI recommends minimum 120 samples for robust reference intervals. Documents statistical validity of the range.

attributes.name: sex
attributes.description: Biological sex for which this reference range applies. Many laboratory tests have sex-specific reference ranges (e.g., hemoglobin, creatinine).

attributes.name: source_citation
attributes.description: Detailed citation or reference to the authoritative source document (e.g., CAP guideline version, manufacturer package insert identifier, peer-reviewed journal article, institutional policy document). Required for CLIA compliance and periodic review.

attributes.name: source_type
attributes.description: The type of authoritative source from which this reference range was derived. CLIA requires documentation of reference range sources.

attributes.name: statistical_method
attributes.description: Statistical method used to calculate the reference interval (e.g., parametric 95% confidence interval, non-parametric percentile method, robust method). Documents the analytical approach per CLSI standards.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The standardized unit of measure for the reference range values (e.g., mg/dL, mmol/L, g/dL, cells/mcL, IU/L). Must match the unit used in test results for proper interpretation.
attributes.references: Unified Code for Units of Measure (UCUM)

attributes.name: upper_normal_limit
attributes.description: The upper boundary of the normal reference range. Values above this threshold are typically flagged as high or abnormal.

attributes.name: culture_type
attributes.description: Classification of the microbiology culture method and target organism category (e.g., aerobic bacteria, anaerobic bacteria, fungal, acid-fast bacilli, viral).
