attributes.name: report_addendum_author_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the provider who authored the addendum or amendment. May differ from the original signing radiologist. Null for the original report.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; AHIMA Health Information Management Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: report_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiologist (provider) who performed the final attestation and signed the report. Corresponds to the interpreting physician of record for legal and billing purposes.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; AMA CPT; HIPAA 45 CFR §164; IHE RAD-28

attributes.name: report_reading_radiologist_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiologist who performed the primary interpretation of the imaging study. May differ from the signing radiologist in teaching or supervisory contexts (e.g., resident reads, attending signs). Used for productivity tracking and RVU attribution.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; ACGME Residency Program Requirements; AMA CPT; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: research_study_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to research.research_study. Business justification: Radiology reports for research subjects require linkage for endpoint adjudication, independent imaging review, safety monitoring, and regulatory submissions. Reports may be blinded for trial integrity

attributes.name: transcriptionist_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Radiology reports often dictated and transcribed by medical transcriptionists. Tracking needed for quality assurance, productivity monitoring, and error investigation when voice recognition not used.

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical encounter (visit) during which the imaging study was ordered and performed. Enables linkage to the patient visit context for clinical and revenue cycle workflows.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Encounter; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: accession_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique identifier assigned by the Radiology Information System (RIS) to the imaging order and its associated report. Used as the primary cross-system business key linking the report to the imaging order, PACS, and billing systems. Sourced from Epic Radiant and Cerner RadNet.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0008,0050); HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.identifier

attributes.name: addendum_sequence
attributes.description: Sequential number identifying the addendum within the report's amendment history. Null for the original report. Increments with each addendum or amendment added post-finalization. Used to order and display the full report amendment history.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport; HIM Documentation Standards; AHIMA Health Information Management Standards

attributes.name: addendum_text
attributes.description: Full text content of the addendum or amendment added to the report post-finalization. Contains Protected Health Information (PHI). Null for the original report. Preserves the complete amendment history as versioned child records.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; IHE RAD-28; AHIMA Health Information Management Standards; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport

attributes.name: addendum_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the addendum or amendment was authored and signed. Null for the original report. Used to track the timeline of post-final modifications.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; AHIMA Health Information Management Standards; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport

attributes.name: addendum_type
attributes.description: Classifies the type of post-final modification to the report. 'Addendum' adds new information without changing the original; 'amendment' modifies existing content; 'correction' fixes a factual error; 'retraction' withdraws the report. Null for the original report.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; AHIMA Health Information Management Standards; HIM Documentation Standards; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport

attributes.name: attestation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the signing radiologist attested and finalized the report, transitioning it to 'final' status. This is the principal business event timestamp for the report lifecycle. Required for billing, legal, and compliance purposes.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; CMS Conditions of Participation; HIPAA 45 CFR §164; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: body_part
attributes.description: Anatomical region or body part that was the subject of the imaging study (e.g., CHEST, ABDOMEN, BRAIN, KNEE). Sourced from DICOM tag (0018,0015) and RIS order. Used for clinical classification and CPT code validation.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0018,0015); SNOMED CT; ACR Index

attributes.name: contrast_administered_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether contrast agent was administered during the imaging study. Relevant for CPT code selection, billing accuracy, radiation safety, and clinical documentation of contrast reactions.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; AMA CPT; DICOM PS3.3; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: contrast_agent_name
attributes.description: Name of the contrast agent administered during the imaging study (e.g., Gadolinium, Iohexol, Gadobutrol). Null if no contrast was administered. Used for adverse event tracking, pharmacy reconciliation, and clinical documentation.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; FDA Drug Labeling; NDC; Epic Willow Pharmacy

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiology report record was first created in the source system. Represents the audit creation timestamp for the report entity. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) — Audit Controls; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF

attributes.name: critical_finding_communicated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the critical finding has been communicated to the ordering or responsible provider. Required for Joint Commission compliance. Only applicable when critical_finding_flag is True.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings

attributes.name: critical_finding_communicated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the critical finding was communicated to the ordering or responsible provider. Used to measure turnaround time compliance with Joint Commission and ACR critical results communication standards.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings

attributes.name: critical_finding_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the report contains a critical or urgent finding that requires immediate communication to the ordering provider per ACR and Joint Commission guidelines. When True, triggers a critical results notification workflow. Supports patient safety and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: dicom_study_instance_uid
attributes.description: Globally unique DICOM Study Instance UID linking this report to the corresponding image set in the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS). Enables direct navigation from the report to the source images. Sourced from DICOM tag (0020,000D).
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0020,000D); IHE RAD-28; PACS Integration Standards

attributes.name: dictation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiologist began dictating the report. Used to measure report turnaround time (TAT) from study completion to dictation. Sourced from Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet workflow timestamps.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Reporting Turnaround Time Guidelines; IHE RAD-28; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: findings_text
attributes.description: Full narrative text of the radiologist's findings section of the report, describing the imaging observations in detail. Contains Protected Health Information (PHI). This is the primary clinical content of the report and the source of truth for diagnostic observations. Sourced from Epic ClinDoc or Cerner PowerChart dictation/transcription.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.text; IHE RAD-28; ACR Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: follow_up_recommendation
attributes.description: Structured follow-up recommendation from the radiologist's impression, indicating the recommended next action (e.g., 'Follow-up CT in 3 months', 'Biopsy recommended', 'No follow-up needed'). Used for care coordination, population health management, and closing the loop on incidental findings.
attributes.references: ACR Reporting Guidelines; The Joint Commission; CMS Quality Reporting; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: impression_text
attributes.description: Radiologist's summary impression or conclusion section of the report, providing the diagnostic interpretation and clinical recommendations. Contains Protected Health Information (PHI). This is the most clinically actionable section of the report and is used for clinical decision support, CDI, and quality measurement.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.conclusion; IHE RAD-28; ACR Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: laterality
attributes.description: Indicates the side of the body examined when applicable (left, right, bilateral, or unspecified). Critical for surgical safety, billing accuracy, and clinical documentation. Sourced from DICOM tag (0020,0060) and RIS.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0020,0060); The Joint Commission National Patient Safety Goals; ICD-10-CM

attributes.name: modality_code
attributes.description: DICOM-standard code identifying the imaging modality used for the study (e.g., CT = Computed Tomography, MR = Magnetic Resonance Imaging, XR/DX/CR = X-Ray, US = Ultrasound, PT = Positron Emission Tomography, NM = Nuclear Medicine, MG = Mammography, FL = Fluoroscopy). Sourced from DICOM tag (0008,0060). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MR|XR|US|PT|NM|MG|FL|DX|CR — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0008,0060); ACR Practice Parameters; IHE RAD-28

attributes.name: preliminary_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the report was first released in preliminary status, making it available to ordering providers before final attestation. Key lifecycle event for TAT measurement and clinical workflow.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; ACR Radiology Reporting Turnaround Time Guidelines; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport

attributes.name: radiation_dose_ctdi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Radiation Dose CT Dose Index Volume (CTDIvol) mGy
attributes.description: CT Dose Index Volume (CTDIvol) in mGy representing the average radiation dose per unit length for CT studies. Null for non-CT modalities. Used alongside DLP for comprehensive radiation dose monitoring and ACR Dose Index Registry reporting.
attributes.references: ACR Dose Index Registry; NCRP Report No. 172; FDA Radiation-Emitting Products; IHE REM Profile; DICOM PS3.3

attributes.name: radiation_dose_dlp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Radiation Dose Dose Length Product (DLP) mGy·cm
attributes.description: Dose Length Product (DLP) in mGy·cm representing the total radiation dose delivered during the CT or fluoroscopy study. Null for non-ionizing modalities (MRI, Ultrasound). Used for radiation dose monitoring, ACR Dose Index Registry reporting, and patient safety compliance.
attributes.references: ACR Dose Index Registry; NCRP Report No. 172; FDA Radiation-Emitting Products; IHE REM Profile; DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0040,A124)

attributes.name: rads_category
attributes.description: Standardized ACR Reporting and Data System (RADS) assessment category assigned in the impression (e.g., BI-RADS 0-6 for mammography, LI-RADS 1-5 for liver, TI-RADS 1-5 for thyroid, Lung-RADS 1-4). Drives follow-up recommendations and quality measurement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BI-RADS 0|BI-RADS 1|BI-RADS 2|BI-RADS 3|BI-RADS 4|BI-RADS 5|BI-RADS 6|LI-RADS 1|LI-RADS 2|LI-RADS 3|LI-RADS 4|LI-RADS 5|TI-RADS 1|TI-RADS 2|TI-RADS 3|TI-RADS 4|TI-RADS 5|Lung-RADS 1|Lung-RADS 2|Lung-RADS 3|Lung-RADS 4 — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR BI-RADS Atlas; ACR LI-RADS; ACR Lung-RADS; ACR TI-RADS; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the radiology report. Drives clinical decision-making and downstream notification workflows. 'Preliminary' indicates a draft interpretation; 'final' indicates the signed, attested report; 'addendum' and 'amended' indicate post-final modifications. Aligns with HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.status.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.status; IHE RAD-28; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: ris_report_code
attributes.description: Native report identifier from the source Radiology Information System (RIS), such as Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet. Used for cross-system reconciliation, ETL lineage tracking, and source system audit.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; IHE RAD-28

attributes.name: signing_radiologist_npi
attributes.description: 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the radiologist who signed and attested the final report. Required for CMS billing, claims submission, and provider credentialing validation. Sourced from the NPPES registry.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; HIPAA 45 CFR §162.406; CMS-1500; UB-04

attributes.name: stat_priority_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the imaging order and report were designated as STAT (immediate/urgent priority), requiring expedited turnaround time. Drives workflow prioritization in the RIS and radiologist worklist. Used for TAT compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Reporting Turnaround Time Guidelines; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: study_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the imaging study was performed (image acquisition). This is the principal real-world event time for the report. Sourced from DICOM tag (0008,0020)/(0008,0030) and RIS. Used as the primary temporal anchor for TAT calculations and clinical timelines.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tags (0008,0020) and (0008,0030); IHE RAD-28; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy.started

attributes.name: study_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the imaging study protocol or procedure performed (e.g., 'CT Chest with Contrast', 'MRI Brain without Contrast'). Sourced from the RIS order and DICOM tag (0008,1030). Used for report titling and clinical context.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0008,1030); Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: template_code
attributes.description: Reference to the structured reporting template used to generate the report (e.g., ACR-standardized templates, site-specific templates). Supports structured reporting initiatives, quality measurement, and AI-assisted reporting workflows.
attributes.references: ACR Reporting and Data Systems (RADS); IHE RAD-28; RadReport Template Library

attributes.name: transcription_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the report transcription was completed (if applicable). Relevant for facilities using human transcription services rather than voice recognition. Used in TAT measurement.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; ACR Radiology Reporting Turnaround Time Guidelines; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiology report record was last modified in the source system. Used for incremental data loading, change data capture (CDC), and audit trail maintenance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) — Audit Controls; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF; ETL Best Practices

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Sequential version number of the report, starting at 1 for the initial report and incrementing with each amendment or addendum. Enables tracking of the full amendment history and identification of the current authoritative version.
attributes.references: IHE RAD-28; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport; HIM Documentation Standards

products.name: report_addendum
products.description: Tracks amendments and addenda appended to a finalized radiology report. Records addendum sequence number, addendum type (correction, clarification, clinical update), addendum text, reason for amendment, addendum author NPI, addendum datetime, original report reference, and notification status to ordering provider. Supports HIM (Health Information Management) audit requirements and CDI (Clinical Documentation Improvement) workflows.
products.reference: Radiology Report Addendum / HIM Amendment Record

attributes.name: report_addendum_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each radiology report addendum record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport; Epic Radiant Addendum Entity

attributes.name: audit_finding_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_finding. Business justification: Report addenda are audited for timeliness, appropriateness, and medical record integrity. Compliance monitors addendum practices to ensure proper documentation standards and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the healthcare facility (hospital, imaging center, outpatient clinic) where the original imaging study was performed and the addendum was issued. Supports multi-facility enterprise reporting and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; TJC; State Departments of Health

attributes.name: cda_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to interoperability.cda_document. Business justification: Report addenda generate separate CDA document versions (replacement or addendum document types) for HIE transmission. Required for regulatory compliance and ensuring downstream systems receive correct

attributes.name: cdi_query_id
attributes.description: Reference to the CDI (Clinical Documentation Improvement) query that prompted this addendum, if applicable. Links the addendum to the CDI workflow for documentation quality tracking and DRG (Diagnosis-Related Group) impact analysis.
attributes.references: AHIMA CDI Practice Guidelines; 3M Health Information Systems; TJC RC.02.01.01

attributes.name: cpt_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.cpt_code. Business justification: Addenda may reference procedure codes when clarifying exam scope or correcting billing. Supports revenue integrity audits and ensures addendum changes are reflected in charge capture systems.

attributes.name: icd10_icd_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.icd_code. Business justification: Addenda may update or clarify diagnosis codes for CDI queries, DRG impact analysis, and billing corrections. Links support amendment tracking and diagnosis code change auditing for compliance.

attributes.name: message_log_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the HL7 (Health Level Seven) ORU or MDM message used to transmit this addendum between systems (e.g., from RIS to EHR via HL7 v2.x or FHIR). Supports interoperability audit and HIE (Health Information Exchange) traceability.
attributes.references: HL7 v2.x ORU^R01; HL7 FHIR R4 MessageHeader; ONC Interoperability Rule

attributes.name: mpi_record_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient whose imaging study and original report are being amended. Required for PHI (Protected Health Information) audit trails and HIM (Health Information Management) compliance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR R4 Patient; Epic MPI

attributes.name: org_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiology department or imaging section within the facility where the addendum was issued. Supports departmental performance analytics and CDI program management.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: original_report_id
attributes.description: Reference to the finalized radiology report to which this addendum is appended. Links the addendum to its parent report for audit and CDI (Clinical Documentation Improvement) traceability.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: primary_report_clinician_id
attributes.description: Internal provider identifier for the radiologist or clinician who authored this addendum. Complements author_npi for internal system linkage to the provider master.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; HL7 FHIR R4 Practitioner

attributes.name: tertiary_report_ordering_provider_clinician_id
attributes.description: Internal provider identifier for the clinician who placed the original imaging order. Required to determine notification obligations when an addendum is issued, per ACR communication guidelines.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient encounter (visit) during which the original imaging study was ordered. Supports clinical context linkage for CDI and quality reporting.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter; Epic Radiant; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: accession_number
attributes.description: RIS (Radiology Information System)-assigned accession number of the imaging order associated with the original report. Used to correlate the addendum back to the imaging study in Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: acknowledgment_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the ordering provider acknowledged receipt of the addendum notification. Nullable until acknowledged. Critical for closed-loop communication compliance per ACR and TJC standards.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter; TJC NPSG.02.03.01; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: addendum_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the addendum was authored and entered into the RIS/EHR system. Represents the principal business event timestamp for this transaction. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport.issued; Epic Radiant; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312

attributes.name: addendum_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential integer indicating the order of this addendum relative to other addenda on the same original report (e.g., 1 = first addendum, 2 = second addendum). Supports multi-addendum tracking and version ordering.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: addendum_status
attributes.description: Current workflow lifecycle state of the addendum. 'draft' = authored but not yet signed; 'pending_review' = awaiting co-signature or peer review; 'finalized' = signed and locked; 'retracted' = addendum itself has been withdrawn.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport.status; Epic Radiant; TJC RC.02.01.01

attributes.name: addendum_text
attributes.description: Full narrative text of the addendum as authored by the radiologist. Contains PHI (Protected Health Information) and clinical findings. Supports CDI (Clinical Documentation Improvement) workflows and HIM audit requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport.conclusion; ACR Practice Parameter

attributes.name: addendum_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the addendum indicating its clinical purpose. 'correction' = factual error corrected; 'clarification' = ambiguous language clarified; 'clinical_update' = new clinical information incorporated; 'addendum' = supplemental information added; 'retraction' = prior finding retracted. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: correction|clarification|clinical_update|addendum|retraction — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; TJC RC.02.01.01; HIM Best Practices

attributes.name: addendum_word_count
attributes.description: Number of words in the addendum text. Used for documentation completeness analytics, CDI program metrics, and radiologist productivity reporting. Derived at ingestion time from addendum_text.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter; AHIMA CDI Guidelines

attributes.name: amendment_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or structured explanation of why the original report required amendment. Documents the clinical or administrative rationale (e.g., 'Transcription error in laterality', 'New clinical history provided by ordering physician'). Required for HIM audit and OIG (Office of Inspector General) compliance.
attributes.references: TJC RC.02.01.01; OIG Compliance Guidance; HIM Best Practices; AHIMA

attributes.name: amendment_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code categorizing the reason for amendment, enabling structured reporting and quality analytics. Complements the free-text amendment_reason field. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: transcription_error|laterality_error|clinical_history_update|measurement_correction|impression_revision|additional_finding|provider_request|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter; AHIMA CDI Guidelines; TJC RC.02.01.01

attributes.name: author_npi
attributes.description: 10-digit NPI (National Provider Identifier) of the radiologist or clinician who authored this addendum. Required for provider attribution, credentialing validation, and CMS (Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services) billing compliance.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; HIPAA Administrative Simplification; AMA

attributes.name: body_part
attributes.description: Anatomical body part or region examined in the original imaging study (e.g., 'CHEST', 'ABDOMEN', 'BRAIN', 'SPINE'). Derived from DICOM tag (0018,0015) BodyPartExamined. Supports anatomical-level quality and utilization analytics.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.6.3.1.1; SNOMED CT; ACR Index

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this addendum record was first created in the data platform. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking per HIPAA and HIM requirements.

attributes.name: critical_finding_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this addendum contains or introduces a critical or urgent finding requiring immediate clinical action. When True, triggers expedited notification workflows per ACR and TJC critical results communication standards.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; TJC NPSG.02.03.01; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: dicom_study_instance_uid
attributes.description: Globally unique DICOM (Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine) Study Instance UID of the imaging study associated with the original report. Enables direct linkage to PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) for image retrieval and addendum context.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.2.1; IHE Radiology Technical Framework; ACR

attributes.name: drg_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this addendum has the potential to change the DRG (Diagnosis-Related Group) assignment for the associated inpatient encounter, affecting reimbursement. True = DRG may be affected; False = no DRG impact anticipated. Supports RCM (Revenue Cycle Management) and CDI analytics.
attributes.references: CMS MS-DRG Grouper; 3M Health Information Systems; AHIMA CDI Guidelines

attributes.name: finalized_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the addendum was electronically signed and finalized by the authoring radiologist. Distinct from addendum_datetime (authoring time) — captures the attestation event for HIM audit and legal record purposes.
attributes.references: TJC RC.02.01.01; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: him_review_datetime
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Information Management (HIM) Review Date and Time
attributes.description: Date and time when the HIM department completed its review of this addendum. Nullable until HIM review is performed. Supports HIM audit trail and CDI workflow tracking.
attributes.references: AHIMA HIM Practice Standards; TJC RC.02.01.01

attributes.name: him_review_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this addendum has been flagged for review by the HIM (Health Information Management) department for coding accuracy, documentation integrity, or compliance purposes.
attributes.references: AHIMA HIM Practice Standards; TJC RC.02.01.01; OIG Compliance Guidance

attributes.name: impression_changed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the addendum materially changes the clinical impression or diagnosis of the original report. True = impression revised; False = addendum is supplemental or administrative only. Key metric for CDI quality analytics and RAC (Recovery Audit Contractor) review.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter; AHIMA CDI Guidelines; OIG Compliance Guidance

attributes.name: laterality
attributes.description: Laterality of the anatomical region examined (left, right, bilateral, or not applicable). Frequently the subject of addenda when laterality errors are identified in the original report. Supports patient safety and HIM audit workflows.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3; SNOMED CT; TJC Universal Protocol UP.01.01.01

attributes.name: modality
attributes.description: Imaging modality of the original study being amended (e.g., CT = Computed Tomography, MRI = Magnetic Resonance Imaging, XR = X-Ray, US = Ultrasound, PET = Positron Emission Tomography). Supports modality-level quality analytics and ACR benchmarking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MRI|XR|US|PET|NM|MG|FL|DX|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.3.1.1.1; ACR; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy.modality

attributes.name: notification_datetime
attributes.business_glossary_term: Ordering Provider Notification Date and Time
attributes.description: Date and time when the notification of this addendum was dispatched to the ordering provider. Nullable when notification_status is 'not_required'. Supports ACR communication audit trail.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; TJC NPSG.02.03.01

attributes.name: notification_method
attributes.description: Channel or method used to notify the ordering provider of the addendum (e.g., Epic In Basket message, secure message, phone call, fax). Supports communication audit and ACR compliance documentation.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: notification_status
attributes.description: Status of notification sent to the ordering provider regarding this addendum. 'not_required' = no notification needed per policy; 'pending' = notification queued; 'sent' = notification dispatched; 'acknowledged' = provider confirmed receipt; 'failed' = notification delivery failed. Supports ACR communication compliance.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; TJC NPSG.02.03.01; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: original_report_finalized_datetime
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Report Finalized Date and Time
attributes.description: Date and time when the original radiology report was finalized prior to this addendum. Used to calculate turnaround time between original finalization and addendum, supporting quality metrics and ACR (American College of Radiology) benchmarking.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; CMS Quality Reporting

attributes.name: peer_review_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this addendum was generated as a result of a formal peer review process (e.g., ACR RADPEER, internal quality review). True = peer review initiated; False = standard clinical addendum. Supports quality program analytics.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER; TJC MS.08.01.01; NCQA; CMS Quality Reporting

attributes.name: peer_review_score
attributes.description: ACR RADPEER concordance score assigned during peer review, if applicable. Scale: 1 = agree with interpretation; 2a/2b = minor discrepancy; 3a/3b = significant discrepancy; 4 = major discrepancy. Nullable when peer_review_flag is False.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER Scoring System; TJC MS.08.01.01; NCQA

attributes.name: source_system

SSOT for imaging equipment identity within the radiology domain. Supports equipment utilization analytics, maintenance scheduling, and regulatory compliance tracking.

Safety programs define modality-specific protocols for employee protection, calibration, and hazard m

attributes.name: primary_operator_employee_id

attributes.name: acr_accreditation_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current American College of Radiology (ACR) accreditation for this modality unit expires. Null if not accredited or not applicable. Critical for maintaining Medicare billing eligibility for advanced imaging services.

attributes.name: acr_accreditation_status

attributes.description: Current American College of Radiology (ACR) accreditation status for this imaging modality unit. ACR accreditation is required for Medicare reimbursement for advanced imaging services (CT, MRI, PET, nuclear medicine) under CMS policy. Drives billing eligibility and quality reporting.

attributes.name: ae_title

attributes.name: bore_diameter_cm
attributes.description: Inner diameter of the CT or MRI gantry bore in centimeters (e.g., 70 cm wide-bore MRI, 80 cm CT). Null for non-gantry equipment. Used for patient eligibility screening (claustrophobia, body habitus) and order routing to appropriate equipment.
attributes.references: ACR MRI Accreditation; ACR CT Accreditation; Manufacturer Specifications; Joint Commission PC.01.02.01

attributes.name: building_code
attributes.description: Facility building or wing code where the modality unit is located (e.g., 'MAIN', 'NORTH', 'MOB-A'). Supports physical asset management, maintenance routing, and emergency response planning.
attributes.references: Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; SAP S/4HANA Plant Maintenance Equipment Master

attributes.name: contrast_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this modality unit is equipped and approved for contrast-enhanced imaging procedures. Drives protocol assignment, contrast administration workflow routing, and safety checklist requirements in the RIS and EHR order management.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; Joint Commission Medication Management MM.01.01.03; Epic Radiant Protocol Master

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this modality unit record was first created in the enterprise data platform. Supports data lineage, audit trail requirements, and HIPAA Security Rule audit controls.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.312(b); ISO 27001 A.12.4; HITRUST CSF Control 09.aa

attributes.name: decommission_date
attributes.description: Date the imaging modality unit was permanently retired from clinical service. Null for active equipment. Used for asset lifecycle management, capital planning, and historical utilization analysis.
attributes.references: Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; SAP S/4HANA Asset Accounting; CMS Cost Report

attributes.name: department_name
attributes.description: Name of the clinical department or imaging section within the facility where this modality unit is assigned (e.g., 'Radiology', 'Emergency Radiology', 'Cardiac Imaging', 'Breast Imaging Center'). Used for departmental cost allocation and operational reporting.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Department Master; Cerner RadNet Location; CMS Cost Report

attributes.name: detector_type
attributes.description: Type of image detector technology used in the modality unit (e.g., 'Flat Panel', 'Curved Array', 'Photon Counting', 'CCD', 'Amorphous Silicon', 'Scintillator'). Relevant for image quality benchmarking, protocol optimization, and ACR phantom testing requirements.
attributes.references: ACR Accreditation Program; NEMA Standards; FDA 21 CFR Part 892

attributes.name: dicom_modality_code
attributes.description: Standardized DICOM modality code as defined in DICOM PS3.3 (e.g., CT, MR, US, DX, PT, NM, MG, RF, XA). Used for PACS routing, DICOM worklist matching, and interoperability with imaging systems. Critical for HL7 and FHIR image exchange.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Table C.7-5a; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy Resource; NEMA DICOM Standard

attributes.name: dose_tracking_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether automated radiation dose tracking and reporting is enabled for this modality unit, feeding the ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR) and enterprise dose management systems. Required for CMS quality reporting and MIPS measures related to radiation safety.
attributes.references: ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR); CMS MIPS Quality Measures; Joint Commission; FDA Radiation Control

attributes.name: equipment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the imaging modality by technology type, aligned with DICOM modality codes and ACR accreditation categories. Drives order routing rules, protocol assignment, and utilization reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MRI|X-ray|Ultrasound|PET-CT|PET|Fluoroscopy|Mammography|Nuclear Medicine|DEXA|Angiography — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.3.1.1.1 Modality; ACR Accreditation Program; CMS Imaging Coverage Policies

attributes.name: fda_510k_number
attributes.description: FDA 510(k) premarket notification clearance number for this imaging device model, confirming substantial equivalence to a predicate device. Supports regulatory compliance documentation and procurement validation.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 807.87; FDA 510(k) Database; OIG Compliance Program

attributes.name: fda_registration_number
attributes.description: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) device establishment registration number assigned to this imaging equipment unit under 21 CFR Part 807. Required for regulatory compliance tracking and FDA inspection readiness.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 807 Establishment Registration; FDA GUDID Database; OIG Compliance

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date the imaging modality unit was physically installed and commissioned at the facility. Used to calculate equipment age, depreciation schedules, warranty expiration, and capital replacement planning.
attributes.references: Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; SAP S/4HANA Asset Accounting; FDA 21 CFR Part 807

attributes.name: is_mobile
attributes.description: Indicates whether this modality unit is a portable or mobile imaging device (True) that can be transported to patient care areas (e.g., portable X-ray, mobile ultrasound, mobile CT), versus a fixed-installation unit (False). Affects scheduling logic, location tracking, and utilization reporting.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Portable Radiography; Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; Epic Radiant Mobile Equipment

attributes.name: last_calibration_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent calibration or quality control (QC) performance of the imaging modality unit. Required for ACR accreditation, state radiation control compliance, and Joint Commission equipment maintenance standards.
attributes.references: ACR Accreditation Program; Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; State Radiation Control Programs; FDA 21 CFR Part 820

attributes.name: last_preventive_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent scheduled preventive maintenance (PM) service performed on the modality unit by biomedical engineering or the manufacturer's field service team. Supports Joint Commission equipment maintenance compliance and uptime tracking.
attributes.references: Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; SAP S/4HANA Plant Maintenance; Infor Lawson Supply Chain

attributes.name: manufacturer
attributes.description: Name of the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of the imaging modality unit (e.g., Siemens Healthineers, GE Healthcare, Philips Healthcare, Canon Medical, Hologic). Used for vendor management, service contract tracking, and FDA device registration.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 807 Device Registration; Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; SAP S/4HANA Equipment Master

attributes.name: max_patient_weight_kg
attributes.description: Maximum patient weight in kilograms that the modality unit's table or gantry is rated to support. Critical for bariatric patient scheduling, safety screening, and order routing to appropriate equipment. Drives clinical decision support alerts in the RIS and EHR.
attributes.references: Joint Commission PC.01.02.01; ACR Practice Parameter; FDA 21 CFR Part 892; Manufacturer Specifications

attributes.name: model_name
attributes.description: Manufacturer-assigned model name or product line designation for the imaging equipment unit (e.g., SOMATOM Force, MAGNETOM Vida, Revolution CT, Ingenia Elition). Used for service contract management, software upgrade tracking, and ACR accreditation documentation.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 807; ACR Accreditation Program; Joint Commission EC.02.04.01

attributes.name: next_calibration_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date by which the next calibration or quality control test must be completed to maintain regulatory compliance and accreditation status. Drives preventive maintenance scheduling and compliance alerts.
attributes.references: ACR Accreditation Program; Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; State Radiation Control Programs

attributes.name: next_preventive_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next preventive maintenance service on the modality unit. Used by biomedical engineering and facilities management for maintenance scheduling and Joint Commission compliance.
attributes.references: Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; SAP S/4HANA Plant Maintenance PM Order

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle status of the imaging modality unit. Drives scheduling availability, order routing eligibility, and equipment utilization reporting. 'active' = available for clinical use; 'under_maintenance' = temporarily unavailable; 'decommissioned' = permanently retired from service.
attributes.references: Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; ACR Practice Parameter; Epic Radiant Equipment Status

attributes.name: pacs_node_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) Node Name
attributes.description: Name of the PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) storage node or archive destination configured for this modality unit. Defines the image routing path from the modality to the enterprise PACS for storage, retrieval, and radiologist interpretation.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.8 Network Communication; IHE Radiology Integration Profiles; Epic Radiant PACS Integration

attributes.name: radiation_emitting
attributes.description: Indicates whether this imaging modality unit emits ionizing radiation (True = ionizing radiation, e.g., CT, X-ray, PET, fluoroscopy; False = non-ionizing, e.g., MRI, ultrasound). Drives radiation dose tracking requirements, state radiation control reporting, and ALARA compliance workflows.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 1020 Radiation Control; State Radiation Control Programs; ACR Dose Index Registry; NCRP Report No. 172

attributes.name: ris_resource_code
attributes.description: Identifier for this modality unit as configured in the source Radiology Information System (RIS) — Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet. Used for system-of-record traceability, ETL reconciliation, and cross-system integration with scheduling and order management.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Equipment Master; Cerner RadNet Device Registry; IHE Scheduled Workflow (SWF) Profile

attributes.name: room_identifier
attributes.description: Physical room or suite identifier within the facility where the modality unit is installed (e.g., 'Room 3', 'Suite B-102', 'MRI Suite 1'). Used for scheduling, patient wayfinding, and facility management.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Room Master; Joint Commission Environment of Care EC.02.06.01

attributes.name: scheduled_hours_per_day
attributes.description: Standard number of hours per day this modality unit is scheduled for clinical operations. Used as the denominator for equipment utilization rate calculations, capacity planning, and staffing models in radiology operations analytics.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Operations Benchmarking; Epic Radiant Scheduling Template; CMS Imaging Utilization

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer-assigned unique serial number for the physical imaging equipment unit. Required for FDA device registration, warranty tracking, service contract management, and ACR accreditation. Stored as confidential due to its role in device security and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 807 Device Registration; Joint Commission EC.02.04.01; ACR Accreditation

attributes.name: service_contract_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current service and maintenance contract for this modality unit expires. Drives contract renewal alerts and procurement planning to ensure continuous coverage and Joint Commission compliance.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Plant Maintenance; Infor Lawson Procurement; Joint Commission EC.02.04.01

attributes.name: service_contract_number
attributes.description: Identifier for the active service and maintenance contract covering this imaging modality unit. Links to the vendor service agreement in the procurement system. Used for service dispatch, cost tracking, and contract renewal management.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Plant Maintenance; Infor Lawson Supply Chain; Joint Commission EC.02.04.01

attributes.name: shared_service_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this modality unit is shared across multiple departments, facilities, or service lines (True) versus dedicated to a single department (False). Relevant for cost allocation, scheduling priority rules, and utilization analytics in multi-entity health systems.
attributes.references: CMS Cost Report; SAP S/4HANA Cost Center Accounting; Epic Radiant Scheduling Rules

attributes.name: slice_count
attributes.description: Number of detector rows or slices for CT modality units (e.g., 16, 64, 128, 256, 320). Null for non-CT equipment. Determines CT protocol capabilities, scan speed, and clinical application eligibility (e.g., cardiac CT requires ≥64 slices). Used in equipment utilization and capability reporting.
attributes.references: ACR CT Accreditation Program; ACR-NASCI-SPR-STR Practice Parameter for Cardiac CT; Epic Radiant Protocol Master

attributes.name: software_version
attributes.description: Current installed software or firmware version on the imaging modality unit. Critical for cybersecurity patch management, FDA software as a medical device (SaMD) compliance, and protocol compatibility with PACS and RIS systems.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 820 Quality System Regulation; FDA Cybersecurity Guidance for Medical Devices; NIST Cybersecurity Framework

attributes.name: tesla_field_strength
attributes.description: Magnetic field strength in Tesla (T) for MRI modality units (e.g., 1.5, 3.0, 7.0). Null for non-MRI equipment. Determines MRI safety zone classifications, implant screening requirements, and protocol capabilities. Required for ACR MRI accreditation documentation.
attributes.references: ACR MRI Accreditation Program; ACR Manual on MR Safety; FDA 21 CFR Part 892; ASTM F2503

attributes.name: unit_code
attributes.description: Facility-assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this imaging equipment unit within the enterprise. Used as the operational business identifier in RIS scheduling, order routing, and PACS integration (e.g., CT01, MRI-3T-02). Corresponds to the equipment code in Epic Radiant and Cerner RadNet.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Equipment Master; Cerner RadNet Device Registry; ACR Practice Parameter

attributes.name: unit_name
attributes.description: Human-readable display name for the imaging modality unit as it appears in scheduling systems, worklists, and operational dashboards (e.g., 'Main Campus CT Scanner 1', 'North Wing 3T MRI'). Used by technologists and schedulers to identify equipment.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Equipment Master; Cerner RadNet; ACR Practice Parameter

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this modality unit record in the enterprise data platform. Supports change data capture (CDC), ETL incremental load processing, and audit trail requirements under HIPAA Security Rule.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.312(b); ISO 27001 A.12.4; HITRUST CSF Control 09.aa

products.name: protocol
products.description: Defines standardized acquisition protocols for each modality and clinical indication combination. Stores protocol name, modality type, clinical indication, body part, contrast requirement flag, contrast agent type, slice thickness, kVp, mAs, field of view, reconstruction algorithm, scan duration estimate, patient preparation instructions, protocol version, effective date, and approving radiologist. Enables consistent image quality and supports radiation dose optimization programs. Managed within Epic Radiant protocol library.
products.reference: Radiology Protocol / ACR Practice Parameter / Epic Radiant Protocol

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.cpt_code. Business justification: Imaging protocols are mapped to CPT codes to standardize procedure ordering, support charge capture automation, and enable protocol-to-billing reconciliation. Essential for revenue cycle optimization

attributes.name: created_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Imaging protocols authored by radiologists or medical physicists require creator tracking for audit trail, version control, and regulatory compliance. Distinct from approving_clinician_id which captur

attributes.name: loinc_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.loinc_code. Business justification: Protocols reference LOINC codes for interoperable procedure identification in HL7 messages, support standardized order entry, and enable cross-facility protocol comparison for quality benchmarking.

attributes.name: parent_protocol_id
attributes.description: Reference to the imaging_protocol_id of the parent protocol from which this protocol was derived or branched (e.g., a pediatric variant derived from an adult protocol). Supports protocol hierarchy and variant management within the Radiant protocol library.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Protocol Library; ACR Practice Parameters

attributes.name: primary_superseded_by_protocol_id
attributes.description: Reference to the imaging_protocol_id of the newer protocol version that replaced this one upon retirement. Enables forward navigation through protocol version history and ensures continuity of care documentation.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Protocol Library; ACR Practice Parameters

attributes.name: acr_appropriateness_rating
attributes.description: American College of Radiology (ACR) Appropriateness Criteria rating for this protocol-indication combination. Used for clinical decision support, prior authorization, and CMS Appropriate Use Criteria (AUC) compliance reporting under PAMA.
attributes.references: ACR Appropriateness Criteria; CMS PAMA AUC Requirements; CMS-1500 Claim Form

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the approving radiologist formally approved this protocol version for clinical use. Marks the transition from draft to active status and is used for audit trails and regulatory compliance documentation.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Standards; ACR Practice Parameters; Epic Radiant Protocol Approval Workflow

attributes.name: approving_radiologist_npi
attributes.description: National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the radiologist who reviewed and approved this protocol version. Ensures accountability for clinical protocol governance and supports credentialing verification. Links to provider registry.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; NPPES; HIPAA Administrative Simplification; Epic Radiant Protocol Approval Workflow

attributes.name: body_part
attributes.description: Anatomical region or body part targeted by this imaging protocol (e.g., 'Brain', 'Chest', 'Abdomen and Pelvis', 'Lumbar Spine'). Corresponds to the DICOM Body Part Examined attribute and SNOMED CT anatomical site codes. Used for protocol selection and PACS routing.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,0015); SNOMED CT; RSNA RadLex Anatomy

attributes.name: clinical_indication
attributes.description: The clinical reason or diagnostic question driving the imaging order for which this protocol is designed (e.g., 'Pulmonary Embolism Rule-Out', 'Abdominal Pain', 'Stroke Workup'). Maps to ICD-10 diagnosis categories and supports appropriateness criteria evaluation.
attributes.references: ICD-10-CM; ACR Appropriateness Criteria; CMS LCD Policies

attributes.name: contrast_dose_ml
attributes.description: Standard contrast agent dose in milliliters specified for this protocol. May be weight-based (documented separately in patient preparation instructions) or fixed volume. Used for pharmacy preparation and contrast utilization tracking.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; Epic Willow Pharmacy; FDA Drug Labeling

attributes.name: contrast_flow_rate_ml_per_sec
attributes.description: Injection flow rate for intravenous contrast in milliliters per second as specified in the protocol. Critical for CT angiography and dynamic phase imaging to achieve optimal vascular enhancement. Null for non-IV contrast protocols.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; RSNA Contrast Administration Guidelines

attributes.name: contrast_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether intravenous or oral contrast administration is required for this protocol. True = contrast is required; False = non-contrast study. Drives pre-procedure screening for contrast allergies, renal function checks, and pharmacy preparation.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; Epic Radiant Protocol Library; FDA Drug Safety Communications

attributes.name: contrast_route
attributes.description: Route of administration for the contrast agent specified in this protocol (e.g., intravenous for CT angiography, oral for GI studies, intrathecal for myelography). Drives nursing preparation and patient consent requirements.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; Epic Willow Pharmacy Integration; Joint Commission Medication Safety

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this protocol record was first created in the radiology data platform. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with HIPAA record retention requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; Joint Commission Record Retention Standards; ISO 27001

attributes.name: dose_optimization_program
attributes.description: Radiation dose optimization program under which this protocol was designed or benchmarked. 'image_gently' for pediatric dose reduction, 'image_wisely' for adult dose reduction, 'acr_dir' for ACR Dose Index Registry benchmarking. Supports regulatory reporting and quality improvement programs.
attributes.references: Image Gently Campaign; Image Wisely Program; ACR Dose Index Registry; NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this protocol version becomes effective and available for clinical use in the RIS. May differ from approval_date if a future activation date is set. Used for version control and ensuring technologists use the current protocol.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Protocol Library; ACR Practice Parameters; Joint Commission Standards

attributes.name: fasting_duration_hours
attributes.description: Required fasting duration in hours prior to the examination when fasting_required is True (e.g., 4 hours for contrast CT, 6 hours for PET-CT). Null when fasting is not required.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; ACR Practice Parameters; ASA Fasting Guidelines

attributes.name: fasting_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient must fast (NPO) prior to this imaging examination. True = fasting required; False = no fasting required. Drives pre-procedure patient instructions and scheduling communication.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; ACR Practice Parameters; Joint Commission Patient Safety Goals

attributes.name: field_of_view_mm
attributes.description: Field of view in millimeters defining the anatomical coverage area for image reconstruction. Determines spatial resolution and the extent of anatomy captured in the image matrix. Applicable to CT and MRI protocols.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,1164); ACR Practice Parameters; RSNA Imaging Guidelines

attributes.name: implant_screening_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether MRI implant safety screening is required before performing this protocol. True = screening required (applicable to all MRI protocols); False = not required. Drives pre-procedure safety questionnaire workflows to identify contraindicated implants, pacemakers, or metallic foreign bodies.
attributes.references: ACR MRI Safety Guidelines; FDA MRI Device Guidance; Joint Commission Patient Safety Goals

attributes.name: kvp
attributes.description: Peak kilovoltage (kVp) setting for the X-ray tube as specified in this protocol. Determines X-ray beam energy and affects image contrast and patient radiation dose. Applicable to CT, X-ray, and fluoroscopy modalities. Null for MRI and ultrasound.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,0060); ACR-AAPM Technical Standards; NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this protocol record was most recently modified in the radiology data platform. Used for change tracking, audit trails, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; Joint Commission Record Retention Standards; ISO 27001

attributes.name: magnetic_field_strength_tesla
attributes.description: Magnetic field strength in Tesla for MRI protocols (e.g., 1.5T, 3.0T, 7.0T). Determines scanner compatibility, image quality characteristics, and specific absorption rate (SAR) limits. Null for non-MRI modalities.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,0087); ACR MRI Safety Guidelines; FDA MRI Device Guidance

attributes.name: mas
attributes.description: Milliampere-seconds (mAs) setting specifying the X-ray tube current-time product for this protocol. Directly influences image noise and patient radiation dose. Used in CT and radiography protocols. Null for MRI and ultrasound.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,1152); ACR-AAPM Technical Standards; NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: modality_type
attributes.description: DICOM-standard imaging modality code for which this protocol is defined (e.g., CT = Computed Tomography, MRI = Magnetic Resonance Imaging, XR = X-Ray, US = Ultrasound, PET = Positron Emission Tomography, NM = Nuclear Medicine, MG = Mammography). Drives scheduling to the correct equipment and technologist skill set. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MRI|XR|US|PET|NM|MG|FL|DX|PT — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3; ACR Practice Parameters; Epic Radiant Modality Configuration

attributes.name: pacs_routing_code
attributes.description: Code used to route completed images to the correct reading worklist, hanging protocol, and storage location within the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS). Ensures images are delivered to the appropriate radiologist subspecialty queue for interpretation.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.4 Storage SOP Classes; Epic Radiant PACS Integration; ACR Informatics Standards

attributes.name: patient_population
attributes.description: Target patient population for which this protocol is designed. Drives protocol selection logic in the RIS based on patient age and clinical context. Pediatric and neonatal protocols use weight-based dosing and modified acquisition parameters.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters; Image Gently Campaign; Image Wisely Program; CMS Pediatric Quality Measures

attributes.name: patient_prep_instructions
attributes.description: Standardized patient preparation instructions for this protocol, including fasting requirements (e.g., NPO 4 hours), hydration instructions, medication holds (e.g., hold Metformin for contrast studies), bowel preparation, and breath-hold coaching. Displayed to scheduling staff and communicated to patients prior to the exam.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; Epic Radiant Patient Instructions; Joint Commission Patient Safety Goals

attributes.name: pitch_factor
attributes.description: Helical pitch factor for CT protocols, defined as table feed per rotation divided by total collimation. Values less than 1.0 indicate overlapping acquisitions (higher dose, better quality); values greater than 1.0 indicate faster coverage with lower dose. Null for non-helical CT and other modalities.
attributes.references: DICOM Standard PS3.3 Tag (0018,9311); ACR-AAPM Technical Standards; NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: protocol_category
attributes.description: Clinical category classifying the purpose of this imaging protocol. 'diagnostic' for standard clinical workup, 'screening' for population health programs (e.g., lung cancer screening), 'interventional' for image-guided procedures, 'research' for IRB-approved studies, 'emergency' for ED/trauma protocols, 'pediatric' for age-specific protocols.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters; CMS Coverage Determinations; IRB Research Protocols

attributes.name: protocol_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the protocol within the Radiology Information System (RIS), such as Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet. Used for order mapping, PACS integration, and cross-system reference.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Protocol Library; Cerner RadNet; ACR Practice Parameters

attributes.name: protocol_name

attributes.name: radiation_dose_ctdi_vol_mgy

attributes.name: radiation_dose_dlp_mgy_cm

Used for radiation dose optimization programs, comparison against Diagnostic Reference Levels (DRLs), and regulatory reporting to CMS and ACR Dose Index Registry.

attributes.name: radlex_code

attributes.name: reconstruction_algorithm

attributes.name: renal_function_check_required

attributes.name: retirement_date

attributes.name: ris_procedure_code

attributes.name: scan_duration_estimate_sec

attributes.name: sedation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether procedural sedation or anesthesia is required or commonly needed for this protocol (e.g., pediatric MRI, claustrophobic patients). True = sedation required; False = no sedation required. Triggers anesthesia scheduling and pre-sedation assessment workflows.

attributes.name: slice_thickness_mm
attributes.description: Nominal slice thickness in millimeters for cross-sectional imaging protocols (CT, MRI). Thinner slices provide higher spatial resolution for small structure evaluation; thicker slices reduce noise and radiation dose. Null for planar modalities.

attributes.name: total_exam_duration_min
attributes.description: Total estimated examination time in minutes including patient preparation, positioning, scanning, and post-processing. attributes.name: version

attributes.name: adverse_reaction_occurred

attributes.name: adverse_reaction_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the adverse reaction experienced by the patient following contrast administration, per ACR grading criteria. Drives escalation protocols and mandatory reporting thresholds.

attributes.name: adverse_reaction_treatment

attributes.name: agent_class
attributes.description: Classification of the contrast agent by chemical class. Drives safety screening protocols (e.g., gadolinium retention monitoring, iodine allergy screening) and ACR guideline compliance.

attributes.name: agent_osmolality_type
attributes.description: Osmolality classification of the iodinated contrast agent (low, iso, or high osmolality). Relevant for patient safety risk stratification, particularly in patients with renal impairment.

attributes.name: body_region

attributes.name: catheter_gauge

attributes.name: concentration_mg_per_ml

attributes.name: contrast_protocol_name

attributes.name: dose_amount_mg

attributes.name: dose_volume_ml

attributes.name: injection_rate_ml_per_sec
