attributes.references: FDA Dose Check (NEMA XR-25), Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert

attributes.name: dose_record_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the radiation dose record. 'preliminary' = dose data received but not yet reviewed; 'final' = reviewed and confirmed; 'amended' = corrected after finalization; 'corrected' = technical correction applied; 'cancelled' = study voided.
attributes.references: IEC 61910, ACR DIR, HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport

attributes.name: dose_registry_submission_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR) Submission Status
attributes.description: Status of submission of this dose record to the ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR). 'pending'=queued for submission; 'submitted'=transmitted to ACR DIR; 'accepted'=confirmed by ACR DIR; 'rejected'=rejected by ACR DIR (requires correction); 'not_required'=procedure not in DIR scope.
attributes.references: ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR), CMS Quality Programs, MIPS

attributes.name: dose_registry_submission_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this dose record was submitted to the ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR) or other regulatory dose registry. Supports audit trail for regulatory compliance and CMS quality program reporting.
attributes.references: ACR DIR, CMS MIPS, Joint Commission

attributes.name: drl_comparison_result
attributes.description: Result of comparing the study dose against the applicable national or institutional Diagnostic Reference Level (DRL). 'below_drl'=dose is below the reference level (optimal); 'at_drl'=dose equals reference level; 'above_drl'=dose exceeds reference level (requires review); 'not_applicable'=no DRL defined for this procedure.
attributes.references: ICRP Publication 135, ACR DIR, NCRP Report 172, CMS Quality Programs

attributes.name: effective_dose_msv
attributes.description: Estimated effective dose in millisieverts (mSv) representing the stochastic risk-weighted whole-body equivalent dose. Derived from DLP × conversion coefficient (k-factor) for CT, or from DAP for fluoroscopy. Used for patient communication, cumulative dose tracking, and ALARA compliance.
attributes.references: ICRP Publication 103, NCRP Report 160, ACR DIR, Joint Commission

attributes.name: entrance_skin_dose_mgy
attributes.description: Entrance skin dose (ESD) in milligray (mGy) for radiographic and fluoroscopic procedures. Represents the absorbed dose at the skin entry point. Critical for radiation injury risk assessment and Joint Commission threshold monitoring.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert, NCRP Report 168, IEC 60601-2-43

attributes.name: fluoroscopy_time_sec
attributes.description: Total fluoroscopy beam-on time in seconds for fluoroscopic and interventional procedures. Regulatory threshold monitoring metric; Joint Commission requires tracking and alerting when fluoroscopy time exceeds defined thresholds (e.g., 30 minutes cumulative).
attributes.references: Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert, IEC 60601-2-43, FDA 21 CFR 1020.32

attributes.name: kvp
attributes.description: Peak kilovoltage (kVp) applied to the X-ray tube during the study. Represents the energy of the X-ray beam. Used for dose optimization, protocol review, and physics quality assurance.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3, ACR Technical Standards, IEC 60601-2-44

attributes.name: modality_type
attributes.description: DICOM modality code indicating the type of imaging equipment used. CT=Computed Tomography, FL=Fluoroscopy, NM=Nuclear Medicine, DX=Digital Radiography (X-ray), MG=Mammography, XA=X-Ray Angiography, RF=Radiofluoroscopy. Determines applicable dose metrics (CTDIvol/DLP for CT, DAP/fluoroscopy time for fluoroscopy). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|FL|NM|DX|MG|XA|RF|PT|SPECT — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.3.1.1.1, ACR DIR, IEC 61910

attributes.name: number_of_exposures
attributes.description: Total count of individual X-ray exposures (radiographic frames or pulses) delivered during the study. Used for dose optimization analysis and comparison against diagnostic reference levels (DRLs).
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 TID 10011, ACR DIR, NCRP Report 172

attributes.name: patient_age_at_study
attributes.description: Patient age in whole years at the time of the imaging study. Used for pediatric dose benchmarking (pediatric patients require lower dose protocols), age-stratified DRL comparisons, and ACR DIR age-group reporting. Derived at time of study to avoid recalculation.
attributes.references: ACR DIR, NCRP Report 172, ICRP Publication 135, Pediatric Imaging Standards

attributes.name: patient_size_cm
attributes.description: Patient effective diameter or water-equivalent diameter in centimeters, used for Size-Specific Dose Estimate (SSDE) calculation in CT. Derived from scout/localizer images or patient measurements. Required for AAPM TG-204 SSDE methodology.
attributes.references: AAPM Report 204 (SSDE), AAPM Report 220, ACR DIR

attributes.name: patient_weight_kg
attributes.description: Patient body weight in kilograms at the time of the imaging study. Used for size-specific dose estimate (SSDE) calculations for CT, weight-based protocol selection, and dose normalization for benchmarking.

attributes.name: physicist_review_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dose record has been flagged for or completed a review by a qualified medical physicist. True = physicist review required or completed; False = no physicist review needed. Triggered by dose alerts, unusual protocol deviations, or regulatory requirements.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Radiation Safety Standards, ACR Practice Parameters, NCRP

attributes.name: physicist_review_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the medical physicist completed the review of this dose record. Null if physicist_review_flag is False or review is pending. Supports compliance audit trail for Joint Commission radiation safety requirements.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Radiation Safety Standards, ACR Practice Parameters

attributes.name: procedure_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the imaging procedure performed (e.g., 'CT Chest with Contrast', 'Fluoroscopic Guidance for Biopsy'). Sourced from the Charge Description Master (CDM) or RIS procedure catalog.
attributes.references: ACR DIR, CDM, Epic Radiant, Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: rdsr_uid
attributes.business_glossary_term: Radiation Dose Structured Report (RDSR) Unique Identifier (UID)
attributes.description: DICOM Radiation Dose Structured Report (RDSR) SOP Instance UID per IEC 61910 standard. Globally unique identifier for the structured dose report generated by the imaging modality. Used for PACS integration and ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR) submission.
attributes.references: IEC 61910, DICOM PS3.3 TID 10011, ACR DIR

attributes.name: reference_air_kerma_mgy
attributes.description: Reference Air Kerma (RAK) in mGy for interventional fluoroscopy procedures. Measured at the interventional reference point (IRP) per IEC 60601-2-43. Used for radiation injury risk assessment and regulatory threshold compliance.

attributes.name: scanner_manufacturer
attributes.description: Manufacturer of the imaging equipment used for the study (e.g., Siemens, GE Healthcare, Philips, Canon). Used for equipment-level dose benchmarking, physics QA, and ACR DIR equipment stratification.

attributes.name: scanner_model
attributes.description: Model name of the imaging equipment used (e.g., 'SOMATOM Force', 'Revolution CT', 'Ingenuity Elite'). Used for equipment-specific dose performance tracking and physics quality assurance.

attributes.name: scanner_station_name
attributes.description: DICOM station name or AE title of the imaging modality that generated the dose data. Used for equipment-level dose tracking, PACS routing, and physics QA within a multi-scanner facility.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3, ACR DIR, Epic Radiant

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this dose record was sourced (e.g., Epic Radiant, Cerner RadNet, third-party dose management system). Used for data lineage, ETL audit, and multi-system reconciliation in the lakehouse Silver layer.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant, Cerner RadNet, MEDITECH Expanse, IEC 61910

attributes.name: ssde_mgy
attributes.description: Size-Specific Dose Estimate (SSDE) in mGy for CT studies, calculated per AAPM TG-204 methodology by applying a size-based conversion factor to CTDIvol. Provides a more accurate patient-specific dose estimate than CTDIvol alone. Used for pediatric dose optimization and ACR DIR advanced reporting.
attributes.references: AAPM Report 204, AAPM Report 220, ACR DIR

attributes.name: study_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the imaging study was performed. Principal business event date for dose record. Used for trending, regulatory reporting, and cumulative dose period calculations.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3, ACR DIR, Joint Commission

attributes.name: study_instance_uid
attributes.description: DICOM Study Instance UID uniquely identifying the imaging study in the PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System). Enables direct linkage between dose records and DICOM image metadata for audit and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: study_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time the imaging study was performed, including timezone offset. Used for intraday workflow analysis, dose alert timing, and RDSR correlation.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3, IEC 61910, HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy

attributes.name: tube_current_mas
attributes.description: X-ray tube current-time product in milliampere-seconds (mAs) for the study. Directly influences radiation dose output. Used for protocol optimization and dose benchmarking.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3, ACR Technical Standards, IEC 60601-2-44

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this dose record was last modified in the source system or Silver layer. Used for incremental ETL processing, change data capture, and audit trail maintenance.

products.name: radiology_appointment
products.description: Radiology-specific scheduling record extending the enterprise scheduling domain with imaging-specific attributes. Captures appointment datetime, status (scheduled, arrived, in-progress, completed, cancelled, no-show), assigned modality and room, scheduled duration, patient prep instructions, insurance pre-authorization reference, scheduling source, and appointment type. Owns radiology-specific scheduling context (modality assignment, prep requirements, contrast timing) that the enterprise scheduling domain does not model. References enterprise scheduling for general appointment infrastructure. Aligns with IHE SWF (Scheduled Workflow) profile for patient and procedure scheduling in radiology.
products.reference: RIS Appointment / Epic Radiant Appointment / Cerner RadNet Schedule

attributes.name: radiology_appointment_id
attributes.description: Primary key for appointment

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the healthcare facility (hospital, outpatient imaging center, clinic) where the imaging appointment is scheduled to take place.
attributes.references: CMS Facility Certification; The Joint Commission; Epic Cadence

attributes.name: clinical_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to order.clinical_order. Business justification: Imaging appointments fulfill clinical orders. Scheduling workflows require linking appointments to orders for prep instruction delivery, authorization verification, and patient communication. Operatio

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiology technologist (RT) assigned to perform the imaging study for this appointment. Used for staffing, productivity tracking, and quality assurance.
attributes.references: ARRT (American Registry of Radiologic Technologists) Standards; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: enterprise_appointment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent enterprise scheduling appointment record. Links this radiology-specific scheduling record to the general enterprise scheduling infrastructure.
attributes.references: IHE SWF Profile; Epic Cadence; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: health_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient's active insurance plan at the time of the imaging appointment. Used for eligibility verification, pre-authorization, and revenue cycle management.
attributes.references: HIPAA X12 270/271; CMS Payer Guidelines; Epic Resolute; Cerner Revenue Cycle

attributes.name: icd10_diagnosis_icd_code_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Icd10 Diagnosis Icd Code Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.icd_code. Business justification: Appointments carry diagnosis codes for prior authorization verification at scheduling time, support medical necessity screening, and enable diagnosis-based appointment prioritization for urgent condit

attributes.name: imaging_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiology order (CPOE) that initiated this appointment. Enables traceability from scheduling back to the clinical order.
attributes.references: IHE SWF Profile; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: modality_room_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific imaging room or scanner unit assigned for this appointment. Enables room-level utilization tracking, maintenance scheduling, and capacity management.
attributes.references: IHE SWF Profile; Epic Radiant Room Management; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: mpi_record_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient receiving the imaging service. Serves as the PARTY_REFERENCE for this transaction, linking to the patient master record.
attributes.references: IHE SWF Profile; HL7 FHIR R4 Patient Resource; HIPAA §164.514

attributes.name: primary_radiology_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinician who placed the imaging order that generated this appointment. Used for referral tracking, utilization management, and RVU attribution.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; AMA CPT Guidelines; Epic Radiant Order Management

attributes.name: procedure_cpt_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.cpt_code. Business justification: Appointments are scheduled for specific CPT-coded procedures to enable resource allocation, exam duration estimation, and scheduling template management. Links support capacity planning and utilizatio

attributes.name: subject_enrollment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to research.subject_enrollment. Business justification: Research imaging appointments are scheduled per protocol visit schedules. Direct linkage to subject enrollment enables protocol compliance tracking, visit window adherence monitoring, and research bil

attributes.name: tertiary_radiology_referring_provider_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the provider who referred the patient for this imaging study, which may differ from the ordering provider. Used for referral analytics, network management, and payer reporting.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; CMS-1500 Box 17; UB-04; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical encounter or visit associated with this imaging appointment. Connects the radiology scheduling event to the broader patient visit context.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter Resource; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: accession_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier assigned by the Radiology Information System (RIS) to this imaging study appointment. Used as the primary cross-system identifier linking the RIS, PACS, and EHR for this imaging event. Conforms to DICOM accession number format.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.2.1; IHE SWF Profile; ACR DICOM Standards

attributes.name: actual_end_datetime
attributes.description: The actual date and time the imaging procedure concluded. Combined with actual_start_datetime to compute actual procedure duration for throughput and capacity analytics.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Quality Metrics; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: actual_start_datetime
attributes.description: The actual date and time the imaging procedure began (patient on table / scan initiated). Used to measure schedule adherence, wait times, and operational efficiency.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Quality Metrics; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: appointment_comment
attributes.description: Free-text clinical or operational notes associated with the imaging appointment (e.g., special patient needs, equipment requirements, interpreter needed, claustrophobia notes for MRI). Not intended for clinical documentation.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; IHE SWF Profile

attributes.name: appointment_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the radiology imaging appointment. Tracks the full lifecycle from initial scheduling through completion or cancellation. Aligns with IHE SWF appointment status codes.
attributes.references: IHE SWF Profile; HL7 FHIR R4 Appointment.status; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: appointment_type
attributes.description: Clinical classification of the imaging appointment indicating the urgency and purpose of the study. Drives scheduling priority, slot allocation, and workflow routing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: routine|urgent|stat|screening|follow_up|pre_op|research — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
attributes.references: ACR Appropriateness Criteria; IHE SWF Profile; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: auth_status
attributes.description: Current status of the insurance pre-authorization for this imaging appointment. Drives scheduling holds, revenue cycle workflows, and denial management processes.
attributes.references: CMS Prior Authorization Requirements; HIPAA X12 278; Epic Resolute; Cerner Revenue Cycle

attributes.name: body_part
attributes.description: The anatomical region or body part targeted by the imaging study (e.g., CHEST, ABDOMEN, BRAIN, KNEE). Aligns with DICOM Body Part Examined attribute and SNOMED CT anatomical terminology.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.6.3.1.5; SNOMED CT; ACR Index

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: The documented reason for appointment cancellation when appointment_status is 'cancelled'. Used for operational analytics, capacity recovery, and patient access improvement initiatives.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Quality Metrics; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: clinical_indication
attributes.description: The clinical reason or indication for the imaging study as documented by the ordering provider. Contains PHI and is used for clinical decision support, ACR appropriateness criteria evaluation, and CDI.
attributes.references: ACR Appropriateness Criteria; HIPAA §164.514; HL7 FHIR R4 ServiceRequest.reasonCode

attributes.name: contrast_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether intravenous or oral contrast agent is required for this imaging study. Drives pre-appointment prep instructions, allergy screening, renal function checks, and contrast timing workflows.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; ACR Practice Parameters; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: contrast_type
attributes.description: The route of contrast agent administration planned for this imaging study. Used for pre-procedure preparation, patient safety screening, and contrast administration documentation.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; SNOMED CT; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this imaging appointment record was first created in the system. Serves as the audit creation timestamp for data lineage, compliance, and change tracking.
attributes.references: HIPAA §164.312(b) Audit Controls; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF

attributes.name: is_portable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the imaging study is to be performed at the patient's bedside or location (portable) rather than in a dedicated imaging room. Affects equipment assignment and technologist dispatch.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: is_stat
attributes.description: Indicates whether this imaging appointment was ordered as STAT (immediate/urgent priority), requiring expedited scheduling and turnaround. Drives workflow prioritization in the RIS and PACS.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters; IHE SWF Profile; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: laterality
attributes.description: Specifies the side of the body for the imaging study when applicable (left, right, bilateral). Critical for patient safety, correct-site imaging compliance, and DICOM metadata accuracy.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.6.1.1.2; The Joint Commission Universal Protocol; SNOMED CT

attributes.name: modality_type
attributes.description: The type of imaging modality assigned for this appointment (e.g., CT, MRI, X-ray, Ultrasound, PET). Core radiology scheduling attribute that determines equipment, room, and technologist assignment. Uses DICOM modality codes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MRI|XR|US|PET|NM|MG|FL|DXA|DEXA — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.3.1.1.1 Modality; ACR DICOM Standards; IHE SWF Profile

attributes.name: no_show_reason
attributes.description: The documented reason the patient did not appear for the scheduled imaging appointment when appointment_status is 'no_show'. Used for patient outreach, access analytics, and population health management.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Quality Metrics; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: pacs_study_uid
attributes.business_glossary_term: Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) Study Instance UID
attributes.description: The globally unique DICOM Study Instance UID assigned by the PACS for the imaging study associated with this appointment. Enables direct linkage between the scheduling record and the DICOM image archive.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.2.1; IHE SWF Profile; ACR DICOM Standards

attributes.name: patient_location
attributes.business_glossary_term: Patient Location at Time of Appointment
attributes.description: The patient's physical location at the time of the imaging appointment (e.g., inpatient unit/bed, ED bay, outpatient clinic, external). Used for transport coordination and portable imaging dispatch.
attributes.references: HL7 ADT; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: prep_instructions
attributes.description: Specific pre-appointment preparation instructions communicated to the patient (e.g., NPO after midnight, bowel prep, hydration requirements, medication holds). Critical for imaging quality and patient safety.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters; Epic Radiant Patient Instructions; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: prior_auth_number
attributes.description: The pre-authorization or prior authorization reference number obtained from the patient's insurance payer before the imaging study. Required for reimbursement and revenue cycle management. Null if authorization not required or not yet obtained.
attributes.references: CMS Prior Authorization Requirements; HIPAA X12 278; AMA Prior Authorization Guidelines

attributes.name: procedure_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the imaging procedure to be performed, corresponding to the CPT code. Used for patient communication, scheduling displays, and clinical documentation.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Coding Standards; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: radiation_dose_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether radiation dose tracking is required for this imaging appointment (applicable to CT, fluoroscopy, nuclear medicine, and other ionizing radiation modalities). Drives dose monitoring workflows per ACR and Joint Commission requirements.
attributes.references: ACR Dose Index Registry; The Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert; NCRP Report 172; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: reschedule_count
attributes.description: The number of times this imaging appointment has been rescheduled. Used to identify access barriers, patient compliance issues, and scheduling inefficiencies.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Access Metrics; Epic Cadence Analytics

attributes.name: ris_appointment_code
attributes.description: The native appointment identifier from the source Radiology Information System (RIS) such as Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet. Used for cross-system reconciliation and ETL lineage tracking.
attributes.references: IHE SWF Profile; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: scheduled_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The planned duration of the imaging appointment in minutes as defined at time of scheduling. Drives modality slot blocking, throughput analysis, and schedule optimization.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters; Epic Radiant Scheduling; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: scheduled_end_datetime
attributes.description: The planned date and time the imaging appointment is expected to conclude. Used with scheduled_start_datetime to determine the reserved slot duration on the modality schedule.
attributes.references: IHE SWF Profile; HL7 FHIR R4 Appointment.end; Epic Cadence

attributes.name: scheduled_start_datetime
attributes.description: The planned date and time the imaging appointment is scheduled to begin. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for scheduling analytics, capacity planning, and patient communication.
attributes.references: IHE SWF Profile; HL7 FHIR R4 Appointment.start; Epic Cadence; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: scheduling_source
attributes.description: The channel or source through which this imaging appointment was scheduled. Used for access analytics, referral management, and patient experience reporting.
attributes.references: IHE SWF Profile; Epic Cadence; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this imaging appointment record was most recently modified. Used for incremental ETL processing, audit trails, and change data capture in the lakehouse pipeline.
attributes.references: HIPAA §164.312(b) Audit Controls; ISO 27001; HITRUST CSF

products.name: reader_assignment
products.description: Association record linking a radiologist (or teleradiology vendor) to an imaging study for interpretation. Captures assignment type (primary reader, second read, peer review, overread, teleradiology), assignment source (worklist auto-assign, manual, teleradiology vendor), vendor details when applicable (vendor name, contract ID, routing reason, vendor accession number), assignment/read start/completion datetimes, turnaround time, subspecialty match, SLA compliance, and assignment status. SSOT for radiologist-to-study assignment including teleradiology routing. Supports worklist management, TAT SLA tracking, teleradiology vendor SLA management, and radiologist productivity reporting.
products.reference: RIS Worklist Assignment / Radiologist Read Assignment

attributes.name: reader_assignment_id
attributes.description: Primary key for reader_assignment

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the facility (hospital, imaging center, outpatient clinic) where the imaging study was performed. Used for facility-level TAT reporting, worklist segmentation, and operational analytics.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; CMS Provider Enrollment; State Department of Health Facility Licensing

attributes.name: cpt_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.cpt_code. Business justification: Radiologist assignments track CPT codes for workload balancing by procedure complexity, RVU-based productivity measurement, and subspecialty matching. Essential for radiologist compensation and staffi

attributes.name: primary_reader_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiologist or reading provider assigned to interpret the imaging study. May reference an internal clinician or a teleradiology vendor reader.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; NPI Registry (CMS)

attributes.name: prior_assignment_reader_assignment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the previous reader_assignment record when this record represents a reassignment or second read. Enables chaining of assignment history for a single imaging study to support audit trails and TAT analysis.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Internal Radiology Operations Policy

attributes.name: radiology_study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the imaging study (accession) to which this reader assignment applies. Links the assignment to the specific diagnostic imaging order and PACS study.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; DICOM PS3.3

attributes.name: report_id
attributes.description: Reference to the finalized radiology report generated as the output of this reader assignment. Links the assignment record to the report document in the RIS/PACS or clinical documentation system.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; HL7 FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport

attributes.name: stark_arrangement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.stark_arrangement. Business justification: Radiologist reading assignments, especially teleradiology and overread arrangements, may involve Stark-regulated compensation. Compliance monitors whether assignment-based compensation meets fair mark

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient encounter (visit) associated with the imaging study being assigned for interpretation. Supports linkage to ADT and clinical context.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter

attributes.name: accession_number
attributes.description: The RIS-assigned accession number uniquely identifying the imaging study within the radiology information system. Used as the primary business identifier for the study in Epic Radiant, Cerner RadNet, and PACS/DICOM workflows.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0008,0050); Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: addendum_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether an addendum was appended to the original radiology report after initial signing. True if an addendum exists; False otherwise. Supports HIM audit trails and clinical documentation integrity.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Medical Record Standards; HIPAA 45 CFR §164; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: addendum_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the most recent addendum was added to the radiology report. Populated only when addendum_flag is True. Used for HIM documentation tracking and clinical audit.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Medical Record Standards; HIPAA 45 CFR §164; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: assigned_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiologist was formally assigned to the imaging study. Serves as the start of the turnaround time (TAT) clock for SLA measurement. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.
attributes.references: ACR TAT Benchmarks; Epic Radiant; CMS Radiology Quality Measures

attributes.name: assignment_source
attributes.description: Mechanism by which the radiologist was assigned to the study. Values: worklist_auto (RIS auto-assignment algorithm), manual (dispatcher or radiologist self-assignment), teleradiology_vendor (routed to external vendor), ai_routing (AI-assisted worklist routing), escalation (escalated from prior assignment). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: worklist_auto|manual|teleradiology_vendor|ai_routing|escalation|stat_escalation|protocol_override — promote to reference product if values expand]
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Worklist Management; Cerner RadNet Routing Rules

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the reader assignment. Values: assigned (radiologist notified, not yet started), in_progress (read actively underway), completed (report finalized), cancelled (assignment voided), reassigned (transferred to another reader), pending (awaiting routing confirmation).
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; ACR Radiology Reporting Standards

attributes.name: assignment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the reader assignment indicating the role of the radiologist relative to the study. Values: primary_read (initial interpretation), second_read (confirmatory read), peer_review (quality/audit read), overread (supervisory review), teleradiology (remote vendor read).
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; Epic Radiant Worklist

attributes.name: body_part
attributes.description: Anatomical body part or region examined in the imaging study, as coded in the RIS/PACS. Used for subspecialty routing, worklist filtering, and subspecialty match validation. Aligns with SNOMED CT anatomical site codes.
attributes.references: SNOMED CT Anatomical Site Hierarchy; DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0018,0015); Epic Radiant

attributes.name: contrast_used
attributes.description: Indicates whether contrast agent was administered during the imaging study. True if contrast was used; False for non-contrast studies. Relevant for CPT code selection, billing, and clinical interpretation context.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; AMA CPT Coding Standards; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the reader assignment record was first created in the RIS or data platform. Serves as the audit trail creation timestamp per HIPAA and TJC record-keeping requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; The Joint Commission (TJC) Medical Record Standards; ISO 27001

attributes.name: critical_finding_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the radiologist identified a critical or urgent finding during interpretation that requires immediate clinical communication per ACR and TJC standards. True if a critical finding was flagged; False otherwise. Drives critical result notification workflows.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; The Joint Commission (TJC) NPSG.02.03.01

attributes.name: critical_finding_notified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiologist or RIS system notified the ordering provider of a critical imaging finding. Required for TJC and ACR compliance documentation. Populated only when critical_finding_flag is True.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings

attributes.name: dictation_method
attributes.description: Method used by the radiologist to generate the report for this assignment. Values: voice_recognition (real-time speech-to-text, e.g., Nuance PowerScribe), manual_transcription (transcriptionist-assisted), structured_reporting (form-based structured data entry), template (pre-built report template).
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Nuance PowerScribe Integration; ACR Radiology Reporting Standards

attributes.name: image_count
attributes.description: Total number of DICOM image instances in the imaging study at the time of assignment. Used as a proxy for study complexity in radiologist workload and productivity analysis.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: is_teleradiology
attributes.description: Indicates whether this assignment was routed to an external teleradiology vendor rather than an internal radiologist. True for teleradiology assignments; False for internal reads. Drives vendor SLA tracking and billing differentiation.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Teleradiology; CMS Teleradiology Billing Rules

attributes.name: modality
attributes.description: The imaging modality of the study being assigned for interpretation. Standard DICOM modality codes: CT (Computed Tomography), MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging), XR/DX/CR (X-ray), US (Ultrasound), PET (Positron Emission Tomography), NM (Nuclear Medicine), MG (Mammography), FL (Fluoroscopy). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MRI|XR|US|PET|NM|MG|FL|DX|CR|DEXA|OT — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0008,0060); ACR Modality Codes; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: pacs_study_uid
attributes.business_glossary_term: Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) Study Instance UID
attributes.description: The globally unique DICOM Study Instance UID used to identify and retrieve the imaging study in the PACS. Enables direct linkage between the RIS assignment record and the PACS image archive for worklist integration and image retrieval.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0020,000D); PACS Integration Standards; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: peer_review_category
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the peer review outcome indicating the level of agreement or discrepancy between the primary read and the peer reviewer's interpretation. Supports quality improvement programs and radiologist performance monitoring.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER Peer Review Program; NCQA HEDIS Quality Measures; The Joint Commission (TJC)

attributes.name: peer_review_score
attributes.description: Radiologist peer review quality score assigned during a peer review or overread assignment. Typically uses the ACR RADPEER scoring scale (1=agree, 2=minor discrepancy, 3=significant discrepancy, 4=major discrepancy). Populated only for peer_review and overread assignment types.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER Peer Review Program; The Joint Commission (TJC) Quality Standards; NCQA

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Clinical priority level assigned to the imaging study read, driving worklist ordering and SLA target selection. Values: stat (immediate, life-threatening), urgent (expedited, clinically time-sensitive), routine (standard queue), scheduled (pre-planned elective read).
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter; Epic Radiant Priority Configuration; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: radiation_dose_dlp
attributes.description: Dose Length Product (DLP) in mGy·cm recorded for CT studies, representing the total radiation dose delivered during the imaging acquisition. Used for radiation dose tracking, ACR Dose Index Registry reporting, and patient safety compliance.
attributes.references: ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR); FDA Radiation Safety; NCRP Report No. 172; DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0040,A30A)

attributes.name: read_complete_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiologist completed the interpretation and the report was finalized or signed. Used as the end point for TAT SLA calculation.
attributes.references: ACR TAT Benchmarks; Epic Radiant; CMS Radiology Quality Measures

attributes.name: read_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiologist opened and began actively interpreting the imaging study in PACS or the RIS worklist. Used to measure time-to-read and radiologist productivity.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; ACR Radiology Reporting Standards

attributes.name: reading_site
attributes.description: Physical or virtual location from which the radiologist performed the interpretation (e.g., on-site reading room, remote home workstation, teleradiology hub). Distinct from the imaging facility; captures where the read occurred.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Teleradiology; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: reassignment_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded reason why the study was reassigned from the originally assigned radiologist to another reader. Examples include radiologist unavailability, subspecialty escalation, conflict of interest, or workload rebalancing. Populated only when assignment_status is reassigned.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Worklist Management; Internal Radiology Operations Policy

attributes.name: report_signed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiologist electronically signed and authenticated the final radiology report. Distinct from read_complete_timestamp as signing may occur after dictation/transcription. Supports HIM and compliance audit requirements.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Medical Record Standards; HIPAA 45 CFR §164; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: rvu_value
attributes.description: The total Relative Value Unit (RVU) assigned to the CPT code for this interpretation, sourced from the CMS Physician Fee Schedule. Used for radiologist productivity measurement, compensation modeling, and departmental workload reporting.
attributes.references: CMS Physician Fee Schedule; AMA RVU Update Committee (RUC); MIPS (MACRA)

attributes.name: sla_met
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reader assignment was completed within the applicable SLA target turnaround time. True if tat_minutes is less than or equal to sla_target_minutes; False otherwise. Supports SLA compliance dashboards and vendor performance management.
attributes.references: ACR TAT Benchmarks; Teleradiology Vendor SLA Contracts; CMS Radiology Quality Measures

attributes.name: sla_target_minutes
attributes.description: The contractual or operational SLA target turnaround time in minutes applicable to this assignment, based on study priority, modality, and assignment type. Sourced from the applicable SLA contract or internal policy at time of assignment.
attributes.references: ACR TAT Benchmarks; Teleradiology Vendor SLA Contracts; Epic Radiant SLA Configuration

attributes.name: subspecialty_match
attributes.description: Indicates whether the assigned radiologist's subspecialty certification matches the subspecialty required for the imaging study. True if matched; False if assigned outside subspecialty (e.g., general radiologist reading a neuroradiology study). Supports quality and credentialing compliance reporting.
attributes.references: ACR Subspecialty Certification; The Joint Commission (TJC) Credentialing Standards; Symplr

attributes.name: subspecialty_required
attributes.description: The radiologist subspecialty required to interpret this imaging study (e.g., neuroradiology, musculoskeletal, breast imaging, interventional, nuclear medicine). Drives subspecialty-based worklist routing and teleradiology vendor selection.
attributes.references: ACR Subspecialty Certification; Epic Radiant Routing Rules; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: tat_minutes
attributes.description: Calculated turnaround time in minutes from study assignment to report completion. Stored as a pre-computed operational field (not a KPI aggregate) to support SLA compliance monitoring and worklist management without requiring real-time computation.
attributes.references: ACR TAT Benchmarks; CMS Radiology Quality Measures; Epic Radiant SLA Tracking

attributes.name: teleradiology_routing_reason
attributes.description: Business reason why the study was routed to a teleradiology vendor rather than read internally. Values: after_hours (no internal radiologist available), subspecialty_gap (required subspecialty not available internally), volume_overflow (worklist capacity exceeded), coverage_gap (scheduled radiologist absent), stat_backup (emergency backup coverage).
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Teleradiology; Internal Radiology Operations Policy

attributes.name: teleradiology_vendor_name
attributes.description: Name of the external teleradiology vendor to whom the study was routed for interpretation. Populated only when is_teleradiology is True. Used for vendor performance management and contract SLA tracking.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Teleradiology; Vendor Contract Management

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the reader assignment record was most recently modified. Supports change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer ETL pipeline and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; The Joint Commission (TJC) Medical Record Standards; ISO 27001

attributes.name: vendor_accession_number
attributes.description: The accession number assigned by the teleradiology vendor's RIS to the study. Used for cross-referencing the internal RIS accession number with the vendor's system for report reconciliation and image retrieval.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3; ACR Practice Parameter for Teleradiology; Vendor RIS Integration

attributes.name: worklist_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the RIS worklist queue from which this assignment was generated or pulled. Used to trace the assignment back to its originating worklist configuration for routing audit and performance analysis.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Worklist Management; Cerner RadNet Worklist

products.name: critical_result
products.description: Tracks the communication workflow for critical and significant radiology findings requiring immediate clinical action per Joint Commission NPSG.02.03.01. Records finding description, severity level (critical, significant, incidental), notification method (phone, secure message, EHR alert), notified provider NPI, notification datetime, acknowledgment datetime, acknowledgment method, escalation flag, escalation datetime, and Joint Commission compliance status. Supports EMTALA compliance, TJC accreditation requirements, and patient safety event tracking. Aligns with HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest resource for critical result notification workflows.
products.reference: Critical Result Notification / TJC NPSG 02.03.01 / ACR Practice Parameter

attributes.name: critical_result_id
attributes.description: Primary key for critical_result

attributes.name: audit_finding_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_finding. Business justification: Critical result notification is a TJC National Patient Safety Goal and state-mandated process. Compliance audits critical result turnaround times, acknowledgment documentation, and read-back complianc

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the facility or imaging center where the study was performed and the critical finding was identified. Supports multi-facility enterprise reporting and TJC accreditation tracking at the facility level.
attributes.references: TJC Hospital Accreditation Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation; State Departments of Health — Facility Licensing

attributes.name: clinical_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to order.clinical_order. Business justification: Critical findings require closed-loop communication linking back to originating clinical orders. Joint Commission critical results notification standards require tracking from order placement through

attributes.name: cpt_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.cpt_code. Business justification: Critical findings are associated with procedure codes for quality tracking, Joint Commission compliance reporting, and critical result rate benchmarking by exam type. Supports patient safety analytics

attributes.name: demographics_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient associated with the imaging study containing the critical finding. Links to the enterprise Master Patient Index (MPI) record.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; HL7 FHIR Patient resource; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiologist who identified and reported the critical finding. Links to the provider/clinician master record for NPI resolution and accountability tracking.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.26; HL7 FHIR Practitioner

attributes.name: imaging_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiology imaging order that generated the critical finding. Links to the originating order in the RIS (Epic Radiant / Cerner RadNet).
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest; Epic Radiant Order Management

attributes.name: message_log_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to interoperability.message_log. Business justification: Critical radiology findings trigger mandatory HL7 ORU result messages to ordering providers and EHR systems for TJC compliance and patient safety. Message_log tracks notification delivery, acknowledgm

attributes.name: org_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiology department or imaging section (e.g., neuroradiology, body imaging, emergency radiology) responsible for the study. Supports departmental quality reporting and workload analytics.
attributes.references: TJC Hospital Accreditation Standards; CMS CoP §482.26; Epic Radiant Department Configuration

attributes.name: primary_critical_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the ordering or responsible provider who received the critical result notification. Required for TJC NPSG.02.03.01 compliance documentation of the notification recipient.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest.recipient; CMS CoP §482.26

attributes.name: report_id
attributes.description: Reference to the formal radiology report (final or preliminary) in which the critical finding was documented. Links to the radiology report data product for full diagnostic context and PACS/RIS integration.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport; DICOM SR; Epic Radiant Report Management

attributes.name: subject_enrollment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to research.subject_enrollment. Business justification: Critical imaging findings in research subjects trigger adverse event reporting workflows to IRBs, sponsors, and data safety monitoring boards. Direct linkage enables automated AE capture, safety signa

attributes.name: tertiary_critical_ordering_provider_clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the provider who placed the original imaging order. May differ from the notified provider if the ordering provider is unavailable. Used for accountability tracking and notification workflow routing.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest.requester; CMS CoP §482.26; Epic Radiant Order Management

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient encounter or visit during which the imaging study was performed and the critical finding was identified. Supports EMTALA compliance tracking and care coordination.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Encounter resource; EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; Epic ADT

attributes.name: accession_number
attributes.description: The RIS-assigned accession number uniquely identifying the imaging order or study that produced the critical finding. Serves as the primary business identifier linking this notification to the originating radiology order in Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 — Attribute Tag (0008,0050); HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy.identifier

attributes.name: acknowledgment_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the notified provider acknowledged receipt and understanding of the critical finding. Required for TJC NPSG.02.03.01 closed-loop communication compliance. Null if acknowledgment has not yet been received.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; HL7 FHIR Communication.received; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards

attributes.name: acknowledgment_method
attributes.description: The communication channel through which the notified provider acknowledged the critical finding. Required for TJC NPSG.02.03.01 closed-loop verification documentation. May differ from the notification method.

attributes.name: acknowledgment_turnaround_minutes
attributes.description: The elapsed time in minutes between notification_datetime and acknowledgment_datetime. Measures provider responsiveness to critical finding notifications. Used for TJC NPSG.02.03.01 compliance measurement and provider performance analytics. Null if acknowledgment has not been received.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards; NCQA Quality Measurement

attributes.name: body_part_examined
attributes.description: The anatomical body part or region examined in the imaging study that produced the critical finding. Aligns with DICOM Tag (0018,0015) and SNOMED CT anatomical site codes. Supports clinical analytics and quality reporting.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0018,0015); SNOMED CT Anatomical Structure; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy.series.bodySite

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this critical finding notification record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and Silver layer ingestion tracking per HIPAA audit control requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) — Audit Controls; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

attributes.name: dicom_study_uid
attributes.description: The globally unique DICOM Study Instance UID (0020,000D) identifying the imaging study in the PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System). Enables direct linkage to DICOM images for clinical review and audit purposes.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0020,000D) — Study Instance UID; ACR DICOM Standard; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy.identifier

attributes.name: emtala_applicable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) Applicable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether EMTALA obligations apply to this critical finding notification, typically when the patient presented through the Emergency Department. True = EMTALA applies; False = EMTALA not applicable. Supports EMTALA compliance documentation and legal risk management.
attributes.references: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; CMS EMTALA Enforcement; OIG Compliance Guidance

attributes.name: escalation_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the escalation process was initiated for this critical finding notification. Populated only when escalation_flag is True. Used to measure escalation response times and compliance with institutional escalation policies.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.26

attributes.name: escalation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the critical finding notification required escalation due to failure to reach the primary responsible provider within the defined response time threshold. True = escalation was triggered; False = no escalation required. Supports TJC NPSG.02.03.01 compliance and patient safety event tracking.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Event Reporting; OIG Compliance Guidance

attributes.name: escalation_reason
attributes.description: The reason escalation was triggered for this critical finding notification: 'no_response' (provider did not respond within threshold), 'provider_unavailable' (provider not reachable), 'wrong_contact' (incorrect contact information), 'system_failure' (notification system failure), 'other'. Supports root cause analysis and process improvement.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Event Reporting

attributes.name: finding_category
attributes.description: Clinical category of the critical finding (e.g., pulmonary embolism, intracranial hemorrhage, pneumothorax, aortic dissection, malignancy, fracture). Supports population health analytics, quality reporting, and pattern analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pulmonary_embolism|intracranial_hemorrhage|pneumothorax|aortic_dissection|malignancy|fracture|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; SNOMED CT; ICD-10-CM

attributes.name: finding_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the radiologist identified and documented the critical finding during image interpretation. This is the principal business event timestamp representing when the critical result was discovered. Critical for measuring notification turnaround time against TJC NPSG.02.03.01 compliance thresholds.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.effectiveDateTime

attributes.name: finding_description
attributes.description: Free-text clinical description of the critical or significant radiology finding requiring immediate action. Captured from the radiologist's report or preliminary read in the RIS/PACS. Constitutes Protected Health Information (PHI) under HIPAA.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; TJC NPSG.02.03.01; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.conclusion

attributes.name: finding_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the radiology finding: 'critical' (life-threatening, requires immediate action), 'significant' (clinically important, requires timely action), or 'incidental' (unexpected finding not directly related to the primary indication). Drives notification urgency and escalation workflows per TJC NPSG.02.03.01.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards

attributes.name: modality
attributes.description: The imaging modality used for the study that produced the critical finding (e.g., CT=Computed Tomography, MRI=Magnetic Resonance Imaging, XR=X-Ray, US=Ultrasound, PET=Positron Emission Tomography, NM=Nuclear Medicine, MG=Mammography, FL=Fluoroscopy). Aligns with DICOM modality codes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MRI|XR|US|PET|NM|MG|FL — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 Tag (0008,0060) — Modality; ACR DICOM Standard

attributes.name: mrn
attributes.description: The facility-assigned Medical Record Number (MRN) for the patient associated with the critical finding. Used for cross-system patient identification and audit trail in compliance with HIPAA PHI requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; Epic MPI

attributes.name: notification_attempt_count
attributes.description: The total number of notification attempts made before successful delivery or escalation. Tracks communication persistence and supports root cause analysis for notification failures and escalation triggers.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication

attributes.name: notification_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the critical finding notification was transmitted to the responsible provider. Used to calculate notification turnaround time (finding_datetime to notification_datetime) for TJC NPSG.02.03.01 compliance measurement.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; AHRQ Patient Safety Event Reporting; HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest.occurrenceDateTime

attributes.name: notification_method
attributes.description: The communication channel used to deliver the critical finding notification to the responsible provider (e.g., phone=direct telephone call, secure_message=encrypted messaging platform, ehr_alert=EHR in-basket alert, pager=numeric/alphanumeric pager, in_person=face-to-face, fax=facsimile). Aligns with HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest.medium.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest.medium; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312

attributes.name: notification_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the critical finding notification lifecycle: 'pending' (finding identified, notification not yet sent), 'notified' (notification sent, awaiting acknowledgment), 'acknowledged' (provider confirmed receipt), 'escalated' (escalation triggered due to non-response), 'failed' (notification delivery failed), 'cancelled' (notification voided). Drives workflow management and compliance dashboards.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; HL7 FHIR CommunicationRequest.status; AHRQ Patient Safety Event Tracking

attributes.name: notification_turnaround_minutes
attributes.description: The elapsed time in minutes between finding_datetime and notification_datetime. Represents the raw operational measurement of how quickly the critical finding was communicated after identification. Used for TJC NPSG.02.03.01 compliance measurement and quality dashboards. Note: this is a stored operational metric captured at notification time, not a real-time calculation.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; AHRQ Quality Indicators

attributes.name: notified_provider_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the provider who received the critical result notification. Directly supports TJC NPSG.02.03.01 documentation requirements for the receiving clinician.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162

attributes.name: pacs_system_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) Name
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the PACS system where the imaging study is archived (e.g., vendor name, system instance). Supports multi-PACS enterprise environments and image retrieval workflows.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3; ACR PACS Standards; HL7 FHIR ImagingStudy

attributes.name: patient_care_setting
attributes.description: The care setting classification of the patient at the time of the critical finding notification: 'inpatient', 'outpatient', 'emergency' (Emergency Department), 'observation', or 'ambulatory'. Influences notification protocols, escalation pathways, and regulatory reporting requirements.
attributes.references: CMS Conditions of Participation; EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; TJC Hospital Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: patient_location_at_notification
attributes.description: The patient's care location (unit, department, or facility) at the time the critical finding notification was issued (e.g., ED, ICU, outpatient clinic, inpatient floor). Supports EMTALA compliance, care coordination, and patient safety event analysis.
attributes.references: EMTALA 42 CFR §489.24; TJC NPSG.02.03.01; HL7 FHIR Location

attributes.name: patient_safety_event_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this critical finding notification has been associated with a formal patient safety event report (e.g., near-miss, adverse event). True = linked to a patient safety event; False = no patient safety event association. Supports OIG compliance, TJC accreditation, and AHRQ patient safety reporting.
attributes.references: AHRQ Patient Safety Event Reporting; TJC Sentinel Event Policy; OIG Compliance Guidance; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: radiologist_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the radiologist who identified the critical finding. Required for regulatory reporting and provider accountability under CMS and TJC standards.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; HIPAA Administrative Simplification

attributes.name: read_back_notes
attributes.description: Free-text documentation of the read-back communication, including any discrepancies noted during the read-back process. Populated when read_back_performed is True. Supports TJC NPSG.02.03.01 closed-loop communication audit trail.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; TJC Hospital Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: read_back_performed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the notified provider performed a verbal read-back of the critical finding to confirm accurate communication, as required by TJC NPSG.02.03.01 for verbal/telephone notifications. True = read-back was performed and documented; False = read-back not performed or not applicable.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; TJC Hospital Accreditation Standards RC.02.01.01

attributes.name: report_status_at_notification
attributes.description: The status of the radiology report at the time the critical finding notification was issued: 'preliminary' (initial read, not yet finalized), 'final' (attending radiologist signed report), 'addendum' (correction or addition to a finalized report). Important for clinical decision-making context and liability documentation.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.status; ACR Practice Parameter; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this critical finding notification record was sourced (e.g., epic_radiant, cerner_radnet, meditech). Supports data lineage, ETL audit, and multi-system enterprise integration.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR MessageHeader.source; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001 — Information Security Management

attributes.name: tjc_compliance_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether this critical finding notification meets The Joint Commission (TJC) National Patient Safety Goal NPSG.02.03.01 requirements for critical result communication: 'compliant' (all requirements met), 'non_compliant' (requirements not met, e.g., acknowledgment not received within threshold), 'pending_review' (under quality review), 'exception_granted' (documented exception approved). Directly supports TJC accreditation reporting.
attributes.references: TJC NPSG.02.03.01; TJC Hospital Accreditation Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this critical finding notification record was last modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental ETL processing per HIPAA audit control requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b) — Audit Controls; HITRUST CSF; ISO 27001

products.name: radiology_peer_review
products.description: Documents radiologist peer review events conducted for quality assurance and ACR accreditation compliance. attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the facility or imaging center where the original study was performed and where the peer review is attributed for accreditation and quality reporting purposes.
attributes.references: TJC Hospital Accreditation Standards; CMS Conditions of Participation; ACR RADPEER 2.0

attributes.name: coordinator_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Peer review programs have administrative coordinators (QA nurses, radiology managers) who manage case selection, distribution, and follow-up. Required for OPPE/FPPE programs and accreditation.

attributes.name: corrective_action_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.corrective_action_plan.
