Quality/compliance departments create CAPs to address systematic issues identified through peer re

attributes.name: cpt_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.cpt_code. Business justification: Peer reviews reference procedure codes for case categorization, discrepancy rate analysis by exam type, and OPPE/FPPE reporting. Links enable quality improvement targeting by procedure complexity.

attributes.name: org_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiology department or imaging section (e.g., Neuroradiology, Body Imaging, Emergency Radiology) within the facility where the peer review is attributed. Supports department-level quality metric stratification.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; TJC LD.04.04.05

attributes.name: original_report_id
attributes.description: Reference to the radiology report that was authored by the original interpreting radiologist and is being reviewed in this peer review event.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: report_addendum_id
attributes.description: Reference to the addendum or amended radiology report created as a result of this peer review, if applicable. Populated only when review_disposition is 'addendum_required' or 'report_amended'. Supports audit trail linking original and corrected reports.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; TJC RC.02.01.01; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient encounter (visit) associated with the imaging study under review. Supports clinical context linkage for quality and population health analytics.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR R4 Encounter; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: accession_number
attributes.description: The RIS-assigned accession number of the original imaging study that is the subject of this peer review. Serves as the primary business identifier linking the review to the source imaging order and PACS study.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3; ACR RADPEER 2.0; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: acr_accreditation_cycle
attributes.description: The ACR accreditation cycle year range (e.g., '2023-2026') to which this peer review event is attributed. Used to aggregate peer review volumes and discrepancy rates for ACR accreditation submission and renewal reporting.

attributes.name: acr_radpeer_score
attributes.description: The ACR RADPEER 2.0 concordance rating assigned by the reviewing radiologist on a 1–4 scale: 1 = Agree with interpretation; 2 = Disagree, but would not have changed management; 3 = Disagree, may have changed management; 4 = Disagree, would have changed management. Drives quality reporting and radiologist performance management.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0 Scoring Methodology; NCQA; TJC LD.04.04.05

attributes.name: blinded_review_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the peer review was conducted in a blinded manner, meaning the reviewing radiologist did not have access to the original report at the time of review. True = blinded review (ACR RADPEER preferred methodology); False = non-blinded review.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; ACR Practice Parameter for Peer Review

attributes.name: body_part_examined
attributes.description: The anatomical region or body part that was the primary subject of the imaging study under review, using SNOMED CT or DICOM body part terminology (e.g., CHEST, ABDOMEN, BRAIN, SPINE). Supports subspecialty-level peer review analytics.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.6.3; SNOMED CT; ACR RADPEER 2.0

attributes.name: case_conference_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this peer review case was referred to or discussed at a departmental case conference or quality committee meeting. True = case was presented at conference; False = not referred to conference. Supports TJC quality committee documentation requirements.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; TJC LD.04.04.05; TJC PI.01.01.01

attributes.name: clinical_history_available_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether adequate clinical history was available to the original interpreting radiologist at the time of interpretation. Contextual factor used in assessing the fairness and validity of the peer review discrepancy rating.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time this peer review record was first created in the data platform. Audit trail field supporting data lineage, compliance, and silver layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; HITRUST CSF; SOC 2

attributes.name: discrepancy_category
attributes.description: Classification of the interpretation discrepancy identified during peer review. 'none' = no discrepancy found (RADPEER score 1); 'minor' = discrepancy unlikely to change clinical management (RADPEER score 2); 'major' = discrepancy that may or would change clinical management (RADPEER scores 3–4). Drives escalation and reporting workflows.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; TJC LD.04.04.05; AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators

attributes.name: discrepancy_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the nature of the interpretation discrepancy identified by the reviewing radiologist. Captures the specific finding, anatomical location, and clinical significance. Protected under peer review privilege in most jurisdictions.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; State Peer Review Privilege Statutes; TJC LD.04.04.05

attributes.name: discrepancy_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the type of interpretation error or discrepancy identified. 'missed_finding' = finding present but not reported; 'mischaracterization' = finding reported but incorrectly described; 'incorrect_recommendation' = appropriate finding but wrong follow-up recommendation; 'incomplete_report' = report lacks required elements; 'wrong_anatomy' = finding attributed to incorrect anatomical location. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: missed_finding|mischaracterization|incorrect_recommendation|incomplete_report|wrong_anatomy — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings

attributes.name: educational_feedback_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the peer review event generated educational feedback to be communicated to the original interpreting radiologist. True = educational feedback was provided; False = no educational feedback generated. Supports CME tracking and radiologist performance improvement programs.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; TJC LD.04.04.05; ACGME Milestones

attributes.name: escalated_to_chair_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this peer review case was escalated to the radiology department chair or medical director due to a major discrepancy or patient safety concern. True = escalated; False = not escalated. Triggers formal performance management workflow.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; TJC LD.04.04.05; OIG Compliance Guidance

attributes.name: icd10_finding_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Finding Code
attributes.description: The ICD-10-CM diagnosis code corresponding to the primary imaging finding or discrepancy identified during peer review. Supports clinical coding alignment, quality reporting, and population health analytics.
attributes.references: WHO ICD-10-CM; CMS ICD-10 Implementation Guide; AHA Coding Clinic

attributes.name: modality_code
attributes.description: DICOM-standard modality code identifying the imaging technology used for the study under review (e.g., CT = Computed Tomography, MR = Magnetic Resonance Imaging, XR = X-Ray, US = Ultrasound, PT = PET). Used for subspecialty-stratified peer review reporting and ACR accreditation compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MR|XR|US|PT|NM|MG|FL|DX|CR — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.3.1.1.1; ACR RADPEER 2.0; ACR Accreditation Program

attributes.name: oppe_fppe_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this peer review event is being counted toward the radiologist's Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE) or Focused Professional Practice Evaluation (FPPE) for medical staff credentialing and privileging purposes. True = counts toward OPPE/FPPE; False = routine QA only.
attributes.references: TJC MS.08.01.01; TJC MS.08.01.03; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.22

attributes.name: original_radiologist_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the radiologist who authored the original interpretation being reviewed. Used for performance tracking and credentialing compliance.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA 45 CFR §162.406; ACR RADPEER 2.0

attributes.name: original_radiologist_response
attributes.description: Free-text response or rebuttal provided by the original interpreting radiologist in response to the peer review findings. Supports the formal peer review appeal and feedback loop process. Protected under peer review privilege.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; State Peer Review Privilege Statutes; TJC LD.04.04.05

attributes.name: original_report_finalized_datetime
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Report Finalized Date and Time
attributes.description: The date and time the original radiology report was finalized (signed/attested) by the interpreting radiologist. Used to calculate the lag between report finalization and peer review, and to assess timeliness of discrepancy identification.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; TJC RC.02.01.01; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: patient_safety_event_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the discrepancy identified in this peer review was determined to constitute a patient safety event requiring reporting to the facility's patient safety officer or risk management. True = patient safety event; False = not a patient safety event.
attributes.references: AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators; TJC SE.04.01.01; OIG; HHS

attributes.name: prior_study_available_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether prior imaging studies were available to the original interpreting radiologist at the time of interpretation. Relevant context for assessing the reasonableness of the original interpretation and the severity of any discrepancy.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings

attributes.name: response_datetime
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Radiologist Response Date and Time
attributes.description: The date and time the original interpreting radiologist submitted their response or acknowledgment of the peer review findings. Used to track completion of the feedback loop and compliance with departmental peer review policy timelines.

attributes.name: review_assigned_datetime
attributes.business_glossary_term: Peer Review Assigned Date and Time
attributes.description: The date and time the peer review case was assigned to the reviewing radiologist. Used to calculate turnaround time and compliance with departmental SLA targets for peer review completion.

attributes.name: review_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which the peer review was performed and the concordance score was assigned by the reviewing radiologist. Principal business event timestamp for this transaction.

attributes.name: review_disposition
attributes.description: The final action or outcome disposition resulting from the peer review. 'no_action' = review complete, no further action needed; 'feedback_provided' = educational feedback sent to original radiologist; 'addendum_required' = original report requires addendum; 'report_amended' = original report was amended; 'escalated' = referred to department leadership; 'referred_to_committee' = referred to quality or peer review committee. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: no_action|feedback_provided|addendum_required|report_amended|escalated|referred_to_committee — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; TJC LD.04.04.05; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: review_program_type
attributes.description: Identifies the quality or regulatory program under which this peer review was conducted. 'acr_radpeer' = ACR RADPEER program; 'internal_qa' = internal departmental QA; 'mips' = MIPS quality measure; 'vbp' = Value-Based Purchasing; 'tjc_required' = TJC-mandated review; 'focused_professional_practice_evaluation' = FPPE for credentialing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: acr_radpeer|internal_qa|mips|vbp|tjc_required|focused_professional_practice_evaluation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; TJC MS.08.01.01 (FPPE/OPPE); CMS MIPS; CMS VBP

attributes.name: review_status
attributes.description: Current workflow lifecycle status of the peer review event. 'pending' = assigned but not yet started; 'in_progress' = reviewer has opened the case; 'completed' = review scoring and disposition finalized; 'cancelled' = review voided; 'escalated' = referred to department chair or quality committee.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; TJC LD.04.04.05; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: review_type
attributes.description: Classification of the peer review event indicating how the case was selected for review. 'random' = randomly selected for routine QA; 'targeted' = selected due to specific criteria (modality, subspecialty); 'discrepancy' = triggered by a known or suspected interpretation discrepancy; 'prospective' = review before report finalization; 'retrospective' = review after report finalization; 'focused' = directed review for performance improvement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: random|targeted|discrepancy|prospective|retrospective|focused — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; ACR Practice Parameter for Communication of Diagnostic Imaging Findings; TJC LD.04.04.05

attributes.name: reviewer_comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments entered by the reviewing radiologist providing additional context, clinical reasoning, or recommendations beyond the structured discrepancy description. Protected under peer review privilege statutes in most jurisdictions.
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; State Peer Review Privilege Statutes; TJC LD.04.04.05

attributes.name: reviewer_radiologist_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the radiologist who performed the peer review. Must be a credentialed radiologist distinct from the original interpreter per ACR RADPEER blinding requirements.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA 45 CFR §162.406; ACR RADPEER 2.0

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this peer review record was sourced (e.g., 'epic_radiant', 'cerner_radnet', 'meditech', 'manual_entry'). Supports data lineage, ETL reconciliation, and multi-system integration governance.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; MEDITECH Expanse; HITRUST CSF

attributes.name: study_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time the imaging study was performed (acquisition datetime from PACS/DICOM metadata). Provides temporal context for the study under review and supports lag-time analytics between study acquisition and peer review.
attributes.references: DICOM PS3.3 C.7.1.1; ACR RADPEER 2.0; Epic Radiant

attributes.name: subspecialty
attributes.description: The radiology subspecialty category of the study under review. Used to ensure subspecialty-matched peer review assignments and to generate subspecialty-stratified quality metrics for ACR accreditation and departmental performance reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: neuroradiology|musculoskeletal|body|breast|cardiovascular|interventional|nuclear|pediatric|emergency — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR RADPEER 2.0; ACR Accreditation Program; ABR Subspecialty Taxonomy

attributes.name: subspecialty_matched_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reviewing radiologist's subspecialty matches the subspecialty of the imaging study under review. True = subspecialty-matched review; False = cross-subspecialty review. ACR RADPEER recommends subspecialty-matched reviews for complex studies.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time this peer review record was last modified in the data platform. Supports incremental ETL processing, audit trail, and change data capture for the silver layer.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; HITRUST CSF; SOC 2

Supports teleradiology vendor SLA management and report reconciliation workflows.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Reference to the teleradiology vendor or remote reading group to whom this study was routed. Links to the vendor master for contract and SLA management.

attributes.name: billing_responsibility

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this teleradiology case record was first created in the system, typically coinciding with the routing decision. Audit trail field for data governance and lineage.

attributes.name: critical_finding_flag

attributes.name: critical_finding_notified_datetime

attributes.name: dicom_study_uid
attributes.description: The globally unique DICOM Study Instance UID (0020,000D) that identifies the imaging study across PACS systems. Used for PACS-to-PACS transmission tracking and image retrieval reconciliation.

attributes.name: discrepancy_category
attributes.description: Classification of the reconciliation discrepancy severity when reconciliation_discrepancy_flag is True. Major discrepancies represent clinically significant differences that may affect patient management; minor discrepancies are interpretive differences without clinical impact.
attributes.references: ACR Teleradiology Practice Guidelines; AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators; Joint Commission Quality Standards

attributes.name: expected_tat_minutes
attributes.description: The contractually agreed or SLA-defined turnaround time (TAT) in minutes from study transmission to final report delivery, as specified in the vendor contract for the applicable priority level and modality.

attributes.name: final_report_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which the final, authenticated radiology report was received from the teleradiology vendor. Used to measure final TAT compliance and trigger report reconciliation workflows.
attributes.references: ACR Teleradiology Practice Guidelines; Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.26; HL7 FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport

attributes.name: final_report_text
attributes.description: The verbatim text of the final, authenticated radiology report received from the teleradiology vendor. Contains PHI and the definitive radiological interpretation. Used for clinical decision-making, reconciliation, and medical record documentation.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.26; HL7 FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport.conclusion

attributes.name: interpretation_start_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which the remote radiologist began active interpretation of the imaging study. Used to measure reading time and identify workflow bottlenecks in vendor SLA performance.

attributes.name: interpreting_radiologist_name

attributes.name: interpreting_radiologist_npi
attributes.description: The 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the remote radiologist who interpreted the imaging study on behalf of the teleradiology vendor. Required for professional component billing and credentialing verification.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Final Rule 45 CFR Part 162; HIPAA Administrative Simplification; CMS-1500 Claim Form; Symplr Credentialing

attributes.name: modality_code
attributes.description: DICOM-standard modality code identifying the imaging technology used to acquire the study (e.g., CT, MR, XR, US, PT). attributes.name: mrn

attributes.name: number_of_images
attributes.description: Total count of DICOM image instances included in the transmitted imaging study. Used to verify transmission completeness and assess study complexity for vendor workload management.

attributes.name: number_of_series
attributes.description: Total count of DICOM series included in the transmitted imaging study. Alongside number_of_images, used to assess study complexity and verify transmission completeness.

attributes.name: preliminary_report_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time at which the preliminary (wet read) radiology report was received from the teleradiology vendor. Used to measure preliminary TAT compliance against SLA thresholds.
attributes.references: ACR Teleradiology Practice Guidelines; Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.26

attributes.name: preliminary_report_text
attributes.description: The verbatim text of the preliminary (wet read) radiology report received from the teleradiology vendor. Contains PHI and clinical findings. Used for reconciliation comparison and clinical communication prior to final report availability.

attributes.name: professional_component_billed

attributes.name: reconciliation_datetime

attributes.name: reconciliation_discrepancy_flag

attributes.name: routing_reason

products.name: radiology_finding
products.description: Structured representation of discrete clinical findings extracted or coded from radiology reports, including actionable follow-up recommendations and their tracking lifecycle. SSOT for structured radiology findings and their associated follow-up tracking. Supports ACR incidental finding guidelines, population health management, and CMS quality measures. attributes.name: dicom_sop_instance_uid

attributes.name: escalation_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether this finding has been escalated beyond standard notification workflows (e.g., escalated to department chief, patient safety officer, or risk management). Supports critical finding management and patient safety reporting.

attributes.name: escalation_timestamp

attributes.name: finding_category
attributes.description: Clinical classification of the finding's significance and origin within the study context. PRIMARY = the primary indication finding; INCIDENTAL = found outside the primary indication; FOLLOW_UP_RECOMMENDED = requires further workup; CRITICAL = requires immediate communication; NORMAL = no abnormality detected.
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Committee Guidelines; HL7 FHIR Observation.category

attributes.name: finding_description
attributes.description: Human-readable clinical description of the discrete finding as documented or extracted from the radiology report (e.g., 'Solitary pulmonary nodule, right upper lobe, 8mm'). Supports clinical review, CDI workflows, and NLP validation.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Observation.valueString; ACR Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: finding_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the radiology finding record. ACTIVE = current and actionable; RESOLVED = finding addressed or no longer present; SUPERSEDED = replaced by an amended or addended finding; ENTERED_IN_ERROR = incorrectly created. Aligns with HL7 FHIR Observation.status.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Observation.status; Epic Radiant Finding Lifecycle

attributes.name: follow_up_completed_date

attributes.name: follow_up_due_date
attributes.description: Calculated or specified date by which the recommended follow-up action should be completed. Derived from study_date plus follow_up_timeframe_days or explicitly set by the radiologist. Drives follow-up tracking dashboards and patient outreach workflows.
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Committee Guidelines; CMS Quality Measures; HEDIS (Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set)

attributes.name: follow_up_modality
attributes.description: Specific imaging modality recommended for follow-up when follow_up_type is IMAGING (e.g., 'CT Chest with contrast', 'MRI Brain without contrast', 'PET/CT'). Free-text or coded value per ACR guidelines.

attributes.name: follow_up_recommended
attributes.description: Indicates whether the radiologist has recommended follow-up action for this finding. When TRUE, the follow-up recommendation fields are expected to be populated. Supports ACR incidental finding tracking and CMS quality measures.

attributes.name: follow_up_status
attributes.description: Current status of the follow-up recommendation lifecycle. PENDING = not yet acted upon; SCHEDULED = follow-up appointment or order placed; COMPLETED = follow-up performed; OVERDUE = past due date without completion; CANCELLED = follow-up cancelled; NOT_REQUIRED = no follow-up needed.
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Committee Guidelines; CMS Quality Measures; HEDIS

attributes.name: follow_up_timeframe_days

attributes.references: ACR Lung-RADS v2022; ACR Incidental Findings Committee Guidelines; CMS Quality Measures

attributes.name: follow_up_type
attributes.description: Type of follow-up action recommended by the radiologist for this finding. IMAGING = repeat or additional imaging; BIOPSY = tissue sampling; CLINICAL_EVALUATION = provider assessment; LABORATORY = lab workup; REFERRAL = specialist referral; NO_ACTION = no further action needed. attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.520; CMS Conditions of Participation; ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines

attributes.name: patient_notification_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the patient was first notified of this follow-up recommendation. Supports compliance documentation and patient communication audit trails.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.520; CMS Conditions of Participation; The Joint Commission

attributes.name: population_health_cohort
attributes.description: Population health management cohort or program to which this follow-up recommendation is attributed (e.g., Lung Cancer Screening Program, Incidental Pulmonary Nodule Registry, Adrenal Incidentaloma Program). Supports ACO and population health analytics.
attributes.references: CMS ACO Quality Measures; NCQA HEDIS; Epic Healthy Planet

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Clinical urgency classification of the follow-up recommendation indicating how quickly action must be taken. Drives escalation workflows, patient notification timelines, and provider alert routing.
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines; The Joint Commission Critical Results Reporting; CMS Quality Measures

attributes.name: recommendation_date
attributes.description: Date and time when the follow-up recommendation was formally issued by the radiologist in the finalized report. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for lifecycle and compliance tracking.
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport; The Joint Commission

attributes.name: recommendation_number
attributes.description: Externally visible business identifier for this follow-up recommendation, used in patient communications, provider notifications, and tracking workflows. Format: FU-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines; Epic Radiant Tracking Module

attributes.name: recommendation_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the follow-up recommendation. Drives population health management dashboards and CMS quality measure reporting.
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines; CMS Quality Measures; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: recommendation_text
attributes.description: Free-text narrative of the follow-up recommendation as authored by the radiologist in the report. Contains Protected Health Information (PHI) and clinical detail supporting the recommended action.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport

attributes.name: recommendation_type
attributes.description: Category of action recommended by the radiologist. Classifies the nature of the follow-up required (e.g., repeat imaging, biopsy, specialist referral). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: repeat_imaging|biopsy|clinical_correlation|specialist_referral|lab_workup|clinical_follow_up|surveillance — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines; ACR RadLex; SNOMED CT

attributes.name: recommended_due_date
attributes.description: Calculated target date by which the follow-up action should be completed, derived from the recommendation date plus the recommended timeframe. Used for overdue tracking, escalation triggers, and patient outreach scheduling.
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines; CMS Quality Measures; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: recommended_modality
attributes.description: Imaging modality recommended for the follow-up study (e.g., CT, MRI, ultrasound). Used for scheduling, resource planning, and modality-specific workflow routing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CT|MRI|ultrasound|PET|X-ray|mammography|fluoroscopy|nuclear_medicine — promote to reference product if additional modalities are needed]
attributes.references: ACR Appropriateness Criteria; Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet

attributes.name: recommended_timeframe_days
attributes.description: Number of days within which the follow-up action should be completed, as specified by the radiologist or derived from ACR incidental finding guidelines (e.g., 90 days for a 6–8 mm pulmonary nodule). Drives escalation and overdue tracking.
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines; Fleischner Society Guidelines; CMS Quality Measures

attributes.name: report_finalized_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the radiology report containing this recommendation was finalized and signed by the interpreting radiologist. Used for turnaround time measurement and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; ACR Practice Parameters; The Joint Commission Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: ris_recommendation_code
attributes.description: Native identifier for this follow-up recommendation as assigned by the source Radiology Information System (RIS) such as Epic Radiant or Cerner RadNet. Supports system-of-record traceability and cross-system reconciliation.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest

attributes.name: scheduled_date
attributes.description: Date on which the follow-up action (imaging, biopsy, referral appointment) has been scheduled. Populated when recommendation_status transitions to scheduled. Used for compliance gap analysis.
attributes.references: Epic Cadence; Cerner RadNet; ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this follow-up recommendation was sourced (e.g., Epic Radiant, Cerner RadNet). Supports data lineage, ETL audit, and multi-system reconciliation in the lakehouse.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant; Cerner RadNet; MEDITECH Expanse; HITRUST CSF

attributes.name: specialist_referral_type
attributes.description: Specialty or service to which the patient is referred when recommendation_type is specialist_referral (e.g., pulmonology, oncology, endocrinology, interventional radiology). Supports referral management and care coordination workflows.
attributes.references: ACR Incidental Findings Guidelines; Salesforce Health Cloud Referral Management; CMS Quality Measures

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this follow-up recommendation record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, audit compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing.

products.name: interventional_procedure
products.description: Master record for interventional radiology (IR) procedures performed under imaging guidance. Covers vascular, non-vascular, neuro-IR, and oncologic interventions. Captures procedure details, imaging guidance modality, anesthesia type, pre/post diagnoses (ICD-10), complications, specimen collection, fluoroscopy time, radiation dose, and implant tracking (UDI). Supports IR case management, complication tracking, device surveillance, and procedural billing. Integrates with OR scheduling for hybrid suite procedures. Aligns with HL7 FHIR Procedure resource and IHE RAD profiles for interventional reporting.

attributes.name: access_site

attributes.name: accession_number

attributes.description: Type of anesthesia or sedation administered during the interventional procedure. Impacts OR scheduling, anesthesia billing, and patient safety monitoring requirements.

attributes.name: asa_classification
attributes.business_glossary_term: American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Physical Status Classification
attributes.description: ASA physical status classification assigned to the patient prior to the procedure, reflecting overall health and anesthetic risk. Required for anesthesia billing, risk-adjusted outcome reporting, and case complexity analysis.
attributes.references: ASA Physical Status Classification System; CMS Anesthesia Billing Guidelines; Joint Commission Pre-Procedure Assessment Standards

attributes.name: body_region
attributes.description: Anatomical body region or organ system targeted by the intervention (e.g., 'hepatic', 'renal', 'pulmonary', 'peripheral vascular', 'spine'). Used for procedure classification, PACS routing, and quality reporting.
attributes.references: SNOMED CT Body Structure Hierarchy; ACR Radiology Coding Source; IHE RAD

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Reason the procedure was cancelled (e.g., 'patient declined', 'clinical contraindication', 'equipment failure', 'scheduling conflict'). Required for operational improvement and suite utilization reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: patient-declined|clinical-contraindication|equipment-failure|scheduling-conflict|insurance-denial|patient-no-show|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Cancellation Codes; CMS Conditions of Participation; Joint Commission PI Standards

attributes.name: cancelled_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time the procedure was cancelled, if applicable. Used for suite utilization analysis, cancellation rate reporting, and downstream order management.
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Cancellation Workflow; CMS Conditions of Participation; Joint Commission OR Scheduling Standards

attributes.name: complication_occurred
attributes.description: Indicates whether a procedural complication was documented during or immediately following the interventional procedure. Triggers complication detail capture and quality event reporting workflows.
attributes.references: SIR Quality Improvement Standards; AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators; Joint Commission Sentinel Event Reporting; CMS Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting

attributes.name: complication_severity
attributes.description: SIR severity grade of the documented complication: minor (no therapy required), moderate (nominal therapy required), major (major therapy required or permanent adverse sequelae), or death. Used for quality benchmarking and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: SIR Quality Improvement Standards — Severity Classification; CMS Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting; AHRQ PSI-11

attributes.name: complication_type
attributes.description: Standardized classification of the procedural complication using SIR severity grading (e.g., 'hemorrhage', 'vessel perforation', 'contrast reaction', 'infection', 'pneumothorax'). Required for SIR quality benchmarking and adverse event reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: hemorrhage|vessel-perforation|contrast-reaction|infection|pneumothorax|nerve-injury|device-malfunction|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SIR Quality Improvement Standards — Complication Classification; AHRQ PSI; Joint Commission Sentinel Event

attributes.name: contrast_agent_used
attributes.description: Indicates whether an iodinated or gadolinium-based contrast agent was administered during the interventional procedure. Drives contrast reaction monitoring, nephrotoxicity risk documentation, and billing for contrast administration.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; FDA Drug Safety Communications; HL7 FHIR MedicationAdministration

attributes.name: contrast_volume_ml
attributes.description: Total volume of contrast agent administered in milliliters during the procedure. Used for nephrotoxicity risk stratification (contrast-to-creatinine ratio), adverse event documentation, and quality benchmarking.
attributes.references: ACR Manual on Contrast Media; SIR Quality Improvement Standards; AHRQ Patient Safety Indicators

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the interventional procedure record was first created in the source system (RIS/EHR). Audit trail field for data lineage and HIPAA audit log compliance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312(b); ISO 27001 A.12.4; HITRUST CSF Control 09.aa

attributes.name: device_name
attributes.description: Commercial or generic name of the primary medical device or implant used (e.g., 'Wallstent Endoprosthesis', 'Greenfield IVC Filter', 'Port-a-Cath'). Supports supply chain reconciliation and device surveillance.
attributes.references: FDA GUDID; Infor Lawson Supply Chain Inventory; Joint Commission Implant Tracking

attributes.name: device_udi
attributes.description: FDA-assigned Unique Device Identifier (UDI) for the primary implant or device placed during the procedure. Mandatory for device surveillance, recall management, and FDA GUDID registry compliance.
attributes.references: FDA UDI Rule 21 CFR §830; FDA GUDID Database; Joint Commission RC.02.01.07; HL7 FHIR Device Resource

attributes.name: fluoroscopy_time_minutes
attributes.description: Total cumulative fluoroscopy time in minutes recorded during the procedure. Mandatory for radiation dose documentation, ALARA compliance, and Joint Commission radiation safety reporting.
attributes.references: ACR-SIR Practice Parameter on Fluoroscopy; FDA 21 CFR §1020.32; Joint Commission Radiation Safety Standards; NCRP Report No. 168

attributes.name: icd10_post_procedure_diagnosis_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Post-Procedure Diagnosis Code
attributes.description: ICD-10-CM diagnosis code assigned after the procedure, reflecting findings confirmed or revised during the intervention. May differ from pre-procedure diagnosis and is used for DRG grouping and CDI.
attributes.references: WHO ICD-10-CM; 3M Health Information Systems Grouping; CMS DRG Definitions Manual

attributes.name: imaging_guidance_modality
attributes.description: Imaging modality used to guide the interventional procedure in real time (e.g., fluoroscopy for vascular interventions, CT for biopsies, ultrasound for drainage). Drives radiation dose tracking and CPT guidance code selection.
attributes.references: ACR Practice Parameters for Interventional Radiology; IHE RAD Profiles; DICOM PS3.3

attributes.name: implant_used
attributes.description: Indicates whether a medical device or implant (stent, coil, filter, catheter, port) was placed during the procedure. Triggers UDI capture requirements per FDA 21st Century Cures Act and device surveillance workflows.
attributes.references: FDA UDI Rule 21 CFR §830; FDA 21st Century Cures Act; Joint Commission Implant Tracking Standards

attributes.name: laterality
attributes.description: Anatomical side of the body on which the interventional procedure was performed. Required for correct-site surgery compliance, ICD-10 coding, and wrong-site event prevention per Joint Commission Universal Protocol.
attributes.references: Joint Commission Universal Protocol; ICD-10-CM Laterality Guidelines; AHRQ Patient Safety Standards

attributes.name: performing_provider_npi
attributes.description: 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the interventional radiologist who performed the procedure. Required on professional claims (CMS-1500) and for provider credentialing verification.
attributes.references: CMS NPI Registry; HIPAA 45 CFR §162.402; CMS-1500 Claim Form

attributes.name: procedure_approach
attributes.description: Technique or approach used to access the target anatomy during the interventional procedure. Impacts CPT code selection, complication risk stratification, and case complexity scoring. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: percutaneous|endovascular|endoscopic|open-hybrid|transarterial|transvenous|transhepatic — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AMA CPT Code Set; SIR Procedure Classification; IHE RAD Interventional Reporting

attributes.name: procedure_category
attributes.description: High-level clinical category of the interventional radiology procedure. Supports case mix analysis, resource planning, and complication benchmarking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: vascular|non-vascular|neuro-IR|oncologic|drainage|biopsy|embolization|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR) Quality Improvement Standards; IHE RAD Profiles

attributes.name: procedure_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the interventional procedure was completed (dressing applied, catheter removed, or patient left the IR suite). Used with start timestamp to calculate procedure duration for suite utilization and staffing analytics.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Procedure.performedPeriod.end; CMS Conditions of Participation; Epic OpTime Case Duration

attributes.name: procedure_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the interventional procedure as documented in the RIS/EHR (e.g., 'Percutaneous Transhepatic Cholangiography', 'TIPS Procedure', 'Uterine Fibroid Embolization').
attributes.references: Epic Radiant Procedure Dictionary; Cerner RadNet Procedure Master

attributes.name: procedure_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the interventional procedure was initiated (first incision, needle insertion, or catheter placement). Principal business event timestamp for case duration calculation and OR/suite utilization reporting.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Procedure.performedPeriod.start; CMS Conditions of Participation; Joint Commission OR Documentation Standards

attributes.name: procedure_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the interventional procedure, aligned with HL7 FHIR Procedure.status value set. Drives workflow routing in the RIS and case management dashboards.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Procedure Resource R4 — status value set; Epic Radiant Procedure Status

attributes.name: radiation_dose_dap_gycm2
attributes.description: Dose-area product (DAP) in Gy·cm² representing the total radiation energy delivered, accounting for field size. Complementary to RAK for stochastic risk estimation and dose registry reporting.
attributes.references: ACR Dose Index Registry (DIR); NCRP Report No. 168; DICOM Radiation Dose Structured Report (RDSR); IEC 60601-2-43

attributes.name: radiation_dose_kerma_mgy
attributes.description: Total reference air kerma (RAK) in milligrays (mGy) delivered to the patient during the procedure. Primary radiation dose metric for fluoroscopy-guided interventions per ACR and Joint Commission dose tracking requirements.
attributes.references: ACR-SIR Radiation Dose Management; NCRP Report No. 168; Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert #47; IEC 60601-2-43

attributes.name: report_finalized_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the interventional radiology procedure report was finalized (signed) by the interpreting radiologist. Used for turnaround time (TAT) measurement and regulatory reporting on result communication.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Reporting Standards; Joint Commission RC.02.01.01; CMS Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current status of the interventional radiology procedure report in the RIS/PACS workflow. Drives report distribution, result notification, and HIM documentation completion tracking.
attributes.references: ACR Radiology Reporting Standards; HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport.status; Epic Radiant Report Workflow

attributes.name: secondary_cpt_codes
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of additional CPT codes for add-on procedures, guidance codes, or concurrent services performed during the same IR session (e.g., imaging guidance CPT 77012 alongside a biopsy CPT).

attributes.name: specimen_collected
attributes.description: Indicates whether a tissue or fluid specimen was collected during the procedure (e.g., biopsy core, aspirate, cytology). Triggers downstream laboratory order linkage and pathology workflow.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR Specimen Resource R4; CAP Laboratory Accreditation Standards; Epic Beaker LIS Integration

attributes.name: specimen_type
attributes.description: Type of specimen collected during the interventional procedure. Used for pathology order routing, LIS integration, and quality reporting on diagnostic yield.
attributes.references: SNOMED CT Specimen Hierarchy; CAP Cancer Protocols; HL7 FHIR Specimen.type; Epic Beaker

attributes.name: technical_success
attributes.description: Indicates whether the procedure achieved its intended technical endpoint as defined by the performing interventionalist (e.g., successful vessel recanalization, complete embolization, adequate drainage). Core quality metric for IR outcome reporting.
attributes.references: SIR Quality Improvement Standards; ACR Practice Parameters; HEDIS Procedural Quality Measures

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

Supports workflow analytics, SLA compliance auditing, and RIS process improvement.

products.name: report_distribution
products.description: This association product represents the distribution event between radiology reports and external trading partners. It captures the transmission of a finalized radiology report to an external entity (HIE, referring provider, specialist, payer, patient portal) via interoperability standards. Each record links one report to one trading partner with transmission metadata, delivery status, acknowledgment tracking, and SLA compliance monitoring that exist only in the context of this specific distribution event.. Existence Justification: In healthcare interoperability operations, a single finalized radiology report is routinely distributed to multiple external trading partners (referring providers, specialists, HIEs, patient portals, payers) based on care coordination needs, regulatory requirements, and data sharing agreements. Each trading partner may receive hundreds or thousands of reports over time. The distribution relationship is an operational business process actively managed by interoperability teams, tracking transmission status, acknowledgments, retries, and SLA compliance per partner per report.

products.name: transmission
products.description: This association product represents the transmission event between an imaging study and an external trading partner. It captures the operational act of sending DICOM study data to external entities (referring facilities, specialists, teleradiology vendors, HIEs) for care coordination, second opinions, or regulatory reporting. Each record links one imaging study to one trading partner with transmission-specific metadata including delivery status, acknowledgments, retry attempts, and SLA compliance tracking. SSOT for outbound imaging study distribution to external partners.. Existence Justification: In healthcare radiology operations, a single imaging study is routinely transmitted to multiple external trading partners for different clinical purposes: the referring facility receives results, a specialist receives images for consultation, a teleradiology vendor provides after-hours interpretation, and an HIE receives data for regional care coordination. Conversely, each trading partner receives thousands of imaging studies over time from the healthcare organization. The transmission relationship is an operational business process actively managed by radiology IT and PACS administrators, with each transmission tracked for delivery status, acknowledgments, retry attempts, and SLA compliance per the data sharing agreement.

products.name: network_modality_participation
products.description: This association product represents the contractual participation of imaging modalities in payer-defined provider networks. It captures the business relationship where healthcare facilities contract specific imaging equipment into insurance networks, establishing in-network status, reimbursement rates, and authorization requirements. Each record links one modality to one provider_network with attributes that exist only in the context of this network participation agreement.. Existence Justification: Healthcare facilities contract specific imaging modalities into multiple payer-defined provider networks simultaneously, and each provider network includes multiple modalities across different facilities and equipment types. Payers actively manage these network participation relationships with modality-specific contracted rates, authorization requirements, credentialing verification, and network adequacy tracking. This is an operational business process where network managers create, update, and terminate modality participation agreements as part of network design and provider contracting.

attributes.name: scheduled_end_time
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the appointment is scheduled to end, including timezone.

attributes.name: scheduled_start_time
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the appointment is scheduled to begin, including timezone.

attributes.name: start_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time when the provider began the clinical encounter. May differ from scheduled start time.

attributes.name: telehealth_access_code
attributes.description: The meeting ID, access code, or PIN required to join the telehealth session. Used for platforms that require separate authentication.

attributes.name: telehealth_connection_status
attributes.description: Real-time or final status of the telehealth session connection. Tracks technical success of the virtual visit.

attributes.name: telehealth_platform
attributes.description: The technology platform or vendor used to conduct the virtual visit (e.g., Epic Video Visit, Zoom for Healthcare, Amwell, Doxy.me). Null for in-person appointments.

attributes.name: telehealth_session_url
attributes.description: The unique web link or meeting URL provided to the patient and provider to join the virtual visit. Contains session-specific access credentials.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this appointment record was last modified. Audit trail for record changes.

attributes.name: visit_modality
attributes.description: The mode of interaction for the appointment. Distinguishes traditional in-person visits from telehealth and asynchronous digital encounters.

attributes.name: visit_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded description of the clinical reason or chief complaint for the appointment as stated by the patient or referring provider.

attributes.name: visit_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized clinical code representing the reason for the visit. May use ICD-10, SNOMED CT, or internal reason code taxonomy.

products.name: appointment_type
products.description: Reference catalog of all appointment types defined across care settings (e.g., new patient visit, follow-up, annual wellness, pre-op, post-op, telehealth, urgent care). Includes CPT/visit type code mapping, default duration, care setting applicability, specialty association, and scheduling rules. Drives appointment booking logic and capacity planning in Epic Cadence and Cerner Millennium.
products.reference: Epic Cadence Visit Type / HL7 FHIR AppointmentType

attributes.name: appointment_type_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the appointment type. Primary key.

attributes.name: board_certification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to provider.board_certification. attributes.name: cdm_entry_id

attributes.name: compliance_policy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.policy. Business justification: Each appointment type governed by policies defining referral requirements, prior authorization rules, billing class restrictions, and patient eligibility criteria. Standard healthcare governance model

attributes.name: cpt_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.cpt_code. Business justification: Appointment types map to CPT codes for RVU calculation, billing class determination, default duration estimation, and reimbursement forecasting. Core to scheduling configuration and revenue cycle.

attributes.name: allows_self_scheduling

attributes.name: appointment_type_name

attributes.name: appointment_type_status

attributes.name: billing_class

attributes.name: cancellation_notice_hours

attributes.name: care_setting

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: default_duration_minutes

attributes.name: effective_end_date

attributes.name: effective_start_date

attributes.name: equipment_required

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: maximum_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Maximum allowable duration in minutes for this appointment type. Prevents over-allocation of provider time and supports throughput optimization.

attributes.name: minimum_duration_minutes

attributes.name: no_show_penalty_applies
attributes.description: Indicates whether a no-show penalty or fee applies to this appointment type. Supports revenue protection and patient accountability.

attributes.name: patient_class
attributes.description: Classification of the patient relationship for this appointment type (e.g., new patient, established patient, return visit). Impacts billing and documentation requirements.

attributes.name: preparation_instructions
attributes.description: Instructions provided to patients before the appointment (e.g., fasting requirements, medication holds, forms to complete). Supports patient education and visit readiness.
attributes.references: Epic MyChart Patient Instructions, Clinical Protocols

attributes.name: quality_measure_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this appointment type is subject to quality measurement and reporting requirements (e.g., HEDIS, MIPS, CAHPS).
attributes.references: NCQA HEDIS, CMS MIPS, CAHPS Survey

attributes.name: reminder_lead_time_days
attributes.description: Number of days before the appointment when automated reminders should be sent to patients. Supports no-show reduction and patient engagement.
attributes.references: Epic Cadence Reminder Configuration, Patient Access Strategy

attributes.name: requires_interpreter
attributes.description: Indicates whether this appointment type typically requires interpreter services. Supports resource allocation and compliance with language access requirements.
attributes.references: Title VI Civil Rights Act, CLAS Standards

attributes.name: requires_referral
attributes.description: Indicates whether this appointment type requires a referral from a Primary Care Physician (PCP) or other provider. Used for authorization and scheduling validation.
attributes.references: Payer Referral Requirements, Epic Cadence Scheduling Rules

attributes.name: room_type_required
attributes.description: The type of clinical room or facility space required for this appointment type (e.g., exam room, procedure room, operating room, telehealth station).
attributes.references: Epic OpTime Configuration, Facility Management Standards

attributes.name: rvu_malpractice

attributes.references: CMS Physician Fee Schedule, RBRVS Methodology

attributes.name: rvu_practice_expense

attributes.references: AMA Specialty Taxonomy, Epic Provider Master File

attributes.description: Clinical and administrative staff roles required to support this appointment type (e.g., physician, nurse, medical assistant, anesthesiologist). Comma-separated list.
attributes.references: Epic Cadence Scheduling Rules, Workforce Management Standards

attributes.name: visit_type_code
attributes.description: Standard visit type code used for billing and revenue cycle integration. Maps to charge capture and claim submission workflows.
attributes.references: Epic Resolute Professional Billing, Cerner Revenue Cycle

attributes.name: waitlist_eligible

products.name: schedule_template
products.description: Provider and resource schedule templates defining recurring availability patterns (daily, weekly, rotating) plus real-time availability exceptions, overrides, and leave records. For templates: captures template name, effective date range, applicable provider or resource, time block definitions, appointment type slots, session duration, and recurrence rules. For availability exceptions: captures provider NPI, exception type (vacation, CME, administrative, on-call, blocked, emergency override), start/end datetime, care setting, reason for unavailability, and approval status. SSOT for all provider/resource availability — both the recurring blueprint and its real-time modifications. Aligns with HL7 FHIR Schedule resource. Used by Epic Cadence and OpTime to generate open scheduling slots.
products.reference: Epic Cadence Schedule Template / OpTime Block Template

attributes.name: schedule_template_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the schedule template record. Primary key.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the facility or location where this schedule template is applicable.

attributes.name: compliance_policy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.policy. Business justification: Schedule templates must comply with regulatory policies governing work hour limits, rest periods, credentialing requirements, and fair access rules. Real compliance need in healthcare scheduling.

attributes.name: primary_schedule_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system account that created this schedule template record.

attributes.name: schedulable_resource_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the resource (room, equipment, facility) to which this template applies. Null if template applies to a provider.

attributes.name: tertiary_schedule_approved_by_user_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user who approved this schedule template. Null if not yet approved or approval is not required.

attributes.name: workforce_org_unit_id
attributes.description: Code identifying the clinical or operational department that owns this schedule template (e.g., Cardiology, Orthopedics, Radiology).

attributes.name: appointment_type_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the type of appointments this template supports (e.g., 'NEW_PATIENT', 'FOLLOW_UP', 'PROCEDURE', 'CONSULT').

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Approval status of the schedule template. Templates may require administrative or clinical approval before becoming active.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this schedule template was approved. Null if not yet approved or approval is not required.

attributes.name: auto_confirm_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether appointments scheduled under this template are automatically confirmed or require manual confirmation. True auto-confirms; False requires manual review.

attributes.name: buffer_time_minutes
attributes.description: Buffer time in minutes added between consecutive appointment slots to allow for provider preparation, documentation, or patient transition.

attributes.name: cancellation_policy_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the cancellation policy applicable to appointments scheduled under this template (e.g., '24_HOUR', '48_HOUR', 'NO_SHOW_FEE').

attributes.name: care_setting
attributes.description: The care delivery setting where this schedule template is used (outpatient clinic, surgical suite, emergency department, telehealth, etc.).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this schedule template record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: day_of_week
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of days of the week this template applies to (e.g., 'Monday,Wednesday,Friday'). Used for weekly recurrence patterns. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Monday|Tuesday|Wednesday|Thursday|Friday|Saturday|Sunday — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this schedule template expires and stops generating appointment slots. Null indicates open-ended template.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this schedule template becomes active and begins generating appointment slots.

attributes.name: insurance_type_accepted
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of insurance types accepted for appointments scheduled under this template (e.g., 'MEDICARE,MEDICAID,COMMERCIAL'). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: medicare|medicaid|commercial|self_pay|workers_comp|tricare|va — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: max_slots_per_session
attributes.description: Maximum number of appointment slots that can be scheduled within a single session. Used for capacity planning and overbooking control.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this schedule template record was last modified.

attributes.name: no_show_tracking_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether no-show events are tracked for appointments scheduled under this template. True enables tracking; False does not.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments about this schedule template, including special instructions, restrictions, or administrative remarks.

attributes.name: overbooking_allowed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether overbooking (scheduling beyond max_slots_per_session) is permitted for this template. True allows overbooking; False enforces strict capacity limits.

attributes.name: overbooking_limit
attributes.description: Maximum number of additional slots that can be overbooked beyond max_slots_per_session. Null if overbooking is not allowed.

attributes.name: patient_class
attributes.description: Classification of patients eligible for appointments under this template (e.g., 'NEW', 'ESTABLISHED', 'REFERRAL', 'SELF_PAY'). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new|established|referral|self_pay|medicare|medicaid|commercial — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Priority classification for appointments scheduled under this template. Determines scheduling urgency and slot allocation rules.

attributes.name: provider_npi
attributes.description: Ten-digit National Provider Identifier for the provider to whom this template applies. Null if template applies to a non-provider resource.

attributes.name: recurrence_pattern
attributes.description: Defines how the template recurs over time: daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, rotating shift, or custom pattern.

attributes.name: recurrence_rule
attributes.description: Detailed recurrence rule in iCalendar RRULE format or system-specific notation defining the exact repeat logic (e.g., 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR').

attributes.name: reminder_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether automated appointment reminders (SMS, email, phone) are sent for appointments scheduled under this template. True enables reminders; False disables.

attributes.name: reminder_lead_time_hours
attributes.description: Number of hours before the appointment when the reminder is sent. Null if reminders are not enabled.

attributes.name: service_type_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the type of clinical service provided during appointments scheduled under this template (e.g., 'OFFICE_VISIT', 'SURGERY', 'DIAGNOSTIC').

attributes.name: session_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the scheduled session in minutes. Calculated as the difference between session start and end times.

attributes.name: session_end_time
attributes.description: Time of day when the scheduled session ends, in HH:MM 24-hour format (e.g., '17:00', '21:00').

attributes.name: session_start_time
attributes.description: Time of day when the scheduled session begins, in HH:MM 24-hour format (e.g., '08:00', '13:30').

attributes.name: slot_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Duration of each individual appointment slot within the session, in minutes (e.g., 15, 30, 60). Determines how many slots are generated per session.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system from which this schedule template record originated (e.g., 'Epic Cadence', 'Cerner Scheduling', 'OpTime').

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this schedule template in the source system. Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: specialty_code
attributes.description: Medical specialty or service line code associated with this schedule template (e.g., 'CARDIO', 'ORTHO', 'PEDS').

attributes.name: telehealth_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this schedule template supports telehealth/virtual appointments. True enables telehealth; False restricts to in-person only.

attributes.name: template_name
attributes.description: Business-friendly name for the schedule template (e.g., 'Dr. Smith Monday Clinic', 'OR 3 Weekday Block').

attributes.name: template_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the schedule template. Active templates are used for slot generation; inactive/retired templates are historical.

attributes.name: template_type
attributes.description: Classification of the schedule template indicating whether it applies to a provider, resource, facility, equipment, room, or staff member.

attributes.name: waitlist_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a waitlist is maintained for this schedule template when all slots are filled. True enables waitlist management; False does not.

products.name: open_slot
products.description: Individual available scheduling slots generated from schedule templates for providers, rooms, and equipment. Captures slot date/time, duration, slot type, care setting, resource assignment, appointment type eligibility, hold status, and remaining capacity. Represents the real-time inventory of bookable time — aligns with HL7 FHIR Slot resource. Consumed by appointment booking workflows, patient self-scheduling (Epic MyChart), and patient access teams in Epic Cadence and Cerner scheduling.
products.reference: Epic Cadence Slot / HL7 FHIR Slot Resource

attributes.name: open_slot_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the open scheduling slot. Primary key for the open_slot data product.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the healthcare facility (hospital, clinic, outpatient center) where the slot is available. Links to the facility master data product. Critical for multi-site organizations.

attributes.name: clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the healthcare provider (physician, nurse practitioner, therapist) assigned to this slot. Links to the provider master data product. Used for provider-specific appointment booking.

attributes.name: equipment_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to specialized medical equipment required for this slot. Links to the equipment resource data product. Examples include MRI machines, surgical robots, dialysis machines. Null if no specific equipment is required.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to research.research_study. Business justification: Research studies reserve dedicated appointment slots for trial participants to ensure protocol visit availability and prevent scheduling conflicts with standard care. Study coordinators block slots sp

attributes.name: room_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific room or treatment space allocated for this slot. Links to the room resource data product. Used for surgical scheduling (OpTime) and procedure room allocation.

attributes.name: schedule_template_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent schedule template from which this slot was generated. Links to the schedule data product that defines recurring availability patterns for providers, rooms, or equipment.

attributes.name: appointment_type_eligibility
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of appointment types that are eligible to be booked in this slot. Examples include new patient, follow-up, annual physical, procedure. Enforces business rules for slot utilization.

attributes.name: block_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation for why the slot is blocked or unavailable. Examples include provider time off, equipment maintenance, facility closure, administrative time. Null if slot is available for booking.

attributes.name: block_type
attributes.description: Categorization of the reason the slot is blocked. Used for reporting on non-clinical time utilization and capacity planning. Null if slot is not blocked.

attributes.name: care_setting
attributes.description: The care delivery environment where the slot is available. Distinguishes between outpatient clinics, inpatient units, emergency department (ED), operating room (OR), telehealth, and home health settings.

attributes.name: comment
attributes.description: Free-text notes or special instructions associated with the slot. May include preparation requirements, patient instructions, or scheduling coordinator notes. Visible to scheduling staff and potentially to patients.

attributes.name: created_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when this slot record was first created in the scheduling system. Used for audit trail and slot generation tracking.

attributes.name: hold_expiration_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when a held slot will automatically be released if not confirmed. Null if slot is not currently held. Used to prevent indefinite slot blocking and optimize capacity utilization.

attributes.name: hold_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation for why the slot is held. Examples include pending insurance authorization, awaiting patient callback, reserved for urgent referral. Null if slot is not held.

attributes.name: hold_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the slot is currently held for a specific patient or referral. Held slots are temporarily reserved pending confirmation. Expired holds are automatically released after a configured timeout period.

attributes.name: insurance_eligibility
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of insurance types or payer groups accepted for this slot. Examples include Medicare, Medicaid, commercial, self-pay. Used for payer-specific access management and network compliance.

attributes.name: last_modified_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when this slot record was last updated. Tracks changes to slot status, capacity, or configuration. Critical for real-time slot availability synchronization.

attributes.name: max_capacity
attributes.description: The maximum number of appointments that can be booked in this slot. Typically 1 for individual provider appointments, but may be higher for group visits, classes, or high-volume clinics.

attributes.name: online_booking_cutoff_hours
attributes.description: The minimum number of hours in advance that a patient must book this slot online. Prevents same-day or last-minute online bookings. Null if no cutoff applies or online booking is disabled.

attributes.name: online_booking_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this slot is available for patient self-scheduling through online portals such as Epic MyChart or Cerner patient portal. False restricts booking to staff-assisted scheduling only.

attributes.name: overbook_allowed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this slot can be overbooked beyond its max_capacity. True allows scheduling additional appointments when slot is full, typically used for urgent or walk-in patients. False enforces strict capacity limits.

attributes.name: patient_type_eligibility
attributes.description: Defines which patient types can book this slot. Examples include established patient only, new patient only, pediatric, adult, geriatric. Used to enforce age restrictions and patient relationship requirements.

attributes.name: remaining_capacity
attributes.description: The number of appointments that can still be booked in this slot. Supports overbooking scenarios where multiple patients can be scheduled in the same time slot. Value of 0 indicates slot is fully booked.

attributes.name: slot_category
attributes.description: Broad categorization of the slot for grouping and filtering purposes. Examples include outpatient, surgical, diagnostic, telehealth, emergency. Used for capacity planning and reporting.

attributes.name: slot_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The length of the slot in minutes, calculated as the difference between slot_end_datetime and slot_start_datetime. Standard durations vary by appointment type and provider specialty.
attributes.references: Derived from HL7 FHIR Slot.start and Slot.end

attributes.name: slot_end_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the slot ends. Represents the latest time an appointment can conclude in this slot. Used to calculate slot duration and prevent overbooking.

attributes.name: slot_identifier
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for the slot, typically generated from schedule template and date/time. Used for external reference and display in Epic Cadence and Cerner scheduling interfaces.

attributes.name: slot_start_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the slot begins. Represents the earliest time an appointment can start in this slot. Critical for patient scheduling and resource allocation.

attributes.name: slot_status
attributes.description: Current availability status of the slot. Free indicates bookable, busy indicates occupied, busy-unavailable indicates blocked, busy-tentative indicates held pending confirmation. Aligns with HL7 FHIR SlotStatus value set.

attributes.name: slot_type
attributes.description: Classification of the slot indicating the kind of appointment or service that can be booked. Examples include new patient visit, follow-up, procedure, telehealth, walk-in. Sourced from Epic Cadence visit type or Cerner appointment type configuration.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this slot was sourced. Examples include Epic Cadence for outpatient scheduling, OpTime for surgical scheduling, Cerner scheduling for inpatient appointments.

attributes.name: source_system_identifier
attributes.description: The unique identifier for this slot in the source operational system. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and bidirectional synchronization between lakehouse and operational systems.

attributes.name: specialty
attributes.description: The medical specialty or service line associated with this slot. Examples include cardiology, orthopedics, primary care, radiology. Used for specialty-specific appointment routing and capacity analysis.

attributes.name: waitlist_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether patients can be added to a waitlist for this slot if it is fully booked. True enables waitlist management for high-demand slots. Used for cancellation backfill and access optimization.

products.name: schedulable_resource
products.description: Master catalog of all resources that can be scheduled across care settings: providers (physicians, APPs, therapists), rooms (exam, OR suite, procedure, imaging, infusion bay), equipment (MRI, CT, C-arm, surgical robot, laser, perfusion pump), and care teams. Captures resource type, name, NPI (for providers), location/facility, building/floor/unit (for rooms), room capacity and configuration, specialty, equipment asset ID, maintenance windows, sterilization cycle requirements, minimum turnover time, active/inactive status, and scheduling constraints. SSOT for resource identity within the scheduling domain. Links to workforce domain (provider master), facility domain (location/room master), and supply domain (equipment asset master) via cross-domain FKs.

products.name: capacity_utilization
products.description: Operational capacity planning and actual utilization records for scheduling resources across all care settings, including OR block utilization. For planning: captures planning period, department, specialty, target visit/case volume, available provider hours/FTE, target utilization rate, and plan status. For OR block utilization: captures block reference, actual cases performed, total scheduled vs. used minutes, released minutes, add-on cases, turnover time between cases, first-case on-time start flag, and utilization percentage. For variance analysis: captures actual vs. planned variance, trend indicators, and reallocation recommendations. SSOT for all scheduling capacity planning and utilization measurement. Supports patient access strategy, OR efficiency reporting, block reallocation decisions, surgical throughput optimization, surgeon/service-level block performance scorecards, and operational throughput optimization.
products.reference: Epic Healthy Planet Capacity / Operational Planning

attributes.name: capacity_utilization_id

attributes.name: workforce_org_unit_id

attributes.name: actual_visit_volume

attributes.name: add_on_case_count

attributes.name: available_fte

attributes.name: available_hours

attributes.name: available_minutes

attributes.name: cancellation_count

attributes.name: care_setting
attributes.description: Care setting context for the capacity plan: outpatient clinic, inpatient unit, emergency department, surgical suite, procedural area, or telehealth.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: first_case_on_time_start_flag

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: no_show_count
attributes.description: Number of patient no-shows during the period, impacting actual utilization.

attributes.name: notes
