attributes.name: overbooking_count
attributes.description: Number of instances where capacity was overbooked beyond available slots or time.

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current status of the capacity plan: draft (in development), approved (ready for execution), active (currently in effect), completed (period ended), or cancelled.

attributes.name: plan_type
attributes.description: Type of capacity record: capacity planning for future periods, OR block utilization for surgical blocks, resource utilization for general scheduling resources, or variance analysis comparing planned vs actual.

attributes.name: planning_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the planning or measurement period for this capacity record.

attributes.name: planning_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the planning or measurement period for this capacity record.

attributes.name: provider_npi

attributes.name: reallocation_recommendation

attributes.name: released_minutes

attributes.name: scheduled_hours

attributes.name: scheduled_minutes

attributes.name: specialty_code

attributes.name: target_case_volume

attributes.name: target_utilization_rate_pct
attributes.description: Target utilization rate as a percentage of available capacity (e.g., 85.00 represents 85% target utilization).

attributes.name: target_visit_volume
attributes.description: Planned number of patient visits or appointments for the planning period.

attributes.name: trend_indicator

products.name: block_utilization
products.description: Transactional records capturing actual utilization of OR block time against allocated block schedules. Captures block reference, actual cases performed, total scheduled minutes, total used minutes, released minutes, add-on cases, turnover time between cases, first-case on-time start flag, and utilization percentage. Supports OR efficiency reporting, block reallocation decisions, surgical throughput optimization, and surgeon/service-level block performance scorecards.

attributes.name: allocated_minutes

attributes.name: block_overrun_minutes

products.name: booking_rule
products.description: Business rules governing appointment and surgical case scheduling logic. Captures rule type (lead time, eligibility, constraint, prerequisite, conflict), applicable appointment types, applicable providers/departments/specialties, rule parameters (minimum/maximum lead times, same-day booking eligibility, double-booking policies, overbooking limits, age/gender restrictions, required pre-visit orders, insurance/authorization requirements), effective date range, override authority level (staff, supervisor, physician), and rule priority/precedence. Drives automated scheduling validation and exception handling in Epic Cadence and OpTime. Versioned to support audit trail of rule changes.
products.reference: Epic Cadence Scheduling Rules / OpTime Scheduling Constraints

attributes.name: booking_rule_id
attributes.description: Primary key for booking_rule

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific facility or care site to which this rule applies. Null indicates the rule applies enterprise-wide across all facilities.

attributes.name: clinician_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific provider to whom this rule applies. Null indicates the rule applies to all providers or is provider-agnostic.

attributes.name: compliance_policy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.policy. Business justification: Booking rules implement compliance policies including authorization requirements, age restrictions, insurance eligibility, and referral mandates. Policy enforcement mechanism in scheduling systems.

attributes.name: primary_booking_appointment_type_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific appointment type to which this rule applies. Null indicates the rule applies to all appointment types.

attributes.name: primary_booking_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user who approved this scheduling rule for activation. Null for draft or unapproved rules. Supports governance and accountability.

attributes.name: superseded_rule_booking_rule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the previous version of this rule that was replaced. Null for initial rule versions. Maintains lineage for rule versioning and audit trail.

attributes.name: workforce_org_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific department to which this rule applies. Null indicates the rule applies across all departments.

attributes.name: applies_to_surgical_cases
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rule applies to surgical case scheduling in Epic OpTime. True enforces the rule for Operating Room (OR) scheduling, false exempts surgical cases.

attributes.name: applies_to_telehealth
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rule applies to telehealth virtual appointments. True enforces the rule for telehealth visits, false exempts telehealth from this rule.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this scheduling rule was approved for activation. Null for draft or unapproved rules. Supports audit trail and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: business_justification
attributes.description: Rationale for implementing this scheduling rule, including clinical, operational, financial, or regulatory drivers. Used for governance and audit purposes.

attributes.name: care_setting
attributes.description: Type of care environment to which this rule applies. Null indicates the rule applies across all care settings.

attributes.name: conflict_rule_type
attributes.description: Type of scheduling conflict this rule prevents. Same day block prevents multiple appointments on the same day, same week block prevents appointments in the same week, concurrent block prevents overlapping appointments, sequential required enforces appointment ordering.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this scheduling rule record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: double_booking_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether multiple appointments can be scheduled in the same time slot for the same provider or resource. True permits double booking, false enforces single appointment per slot.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the scheduling rule expires and ceases enforcement. Null indicates an open-ended rule with no planned expiration.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the scheduling rule becomes active and begins enforcement in scheduling systems. Supports versioning and temporal validity of rule changes.

attributes.name: enforcement_mode
attributes.description: Defines how strictly the rule is enforced in scheduling systems. Hard block prevents scheduling, soft warning allows override with acknowledgment, advisory provides guidance without enforcement.

attributes.name: gender_restriction
attributes.description: Gender requirement for patients scheduling under this rule. Used for gender-specific procedures and services. Any indicates no gender restriction.

attributes.name: insurance_type_required
attributes.description: Specific insurance plan type or payer category required for scheduling under this rule. Null indicates no insurance restriction. Used to enforce payer-specific access rules.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this scheduling rule record was most recently updated. Supports change tracking and audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: maximum_lead_time_days
attributes.description: Maximum number of days in advance that an appointment can be scheduled. Used to control booking horizon and prevent excessive future scheduling.

attributes.name: maximum_patient_age_years
attributes.description: Maximum patient age in years permitted to schedule under this rule. Used to enforce age-appropriate care restrictions. Null indicates no maximum age limit.

attributes.name: minimum_lead_time_days
attributes.description: Minimum number of days in advance that an appointment must be scheduled. Used to enforce advance booking requirements for procedures requiring preparation or authorization.

attributes.name: minimum_patient_age_years
attributes.description: Minimum patient age in years required to schedule under this rule. Used to enforce age-appropriate care restrictions. Null indicates no minimum age requirement.

attributes.name: overbooking_limit
attributes.description: Maximum number of appointments that can be scheduled beyond standard capacity for a given time slot. Used to manage no-show risk and optimize throughput. Null indicates no overbooking permitted.

attributes.name: override_authority_level
attributes.description: Minimum user role or authority level required to override this rule during scheduling. Defines escalation hierarchy for exception handling.

attributes.name: patient_class
attributes.description: Classification of patient visit type to which this rule applies. Null indicates the rule applies to all patient classes.

attributes.name: regulatory_requirement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rule is mandated by external regulatory or accreditation requirements. True identifies rules that cannot be waived without compliance risk.
attributes.references: The Joint Commission (TJC) Standards, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Conditions of Participation

attributes.name: required_pre_visit_orders
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of order types or procedure codes that must be completed before the appointment. Used to enforce prerequisite testing or preparation requirements.

attributes.name: requires_prior_authorization
attributes.description: Indicates whether insurance prior authorization must be obtained before scheduling. True enforces authorization validation, false permits scheduling without authorization.
attributes.references: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Prior Authorization Requirements

attributes.name: requires_referral
attributes.description: Indicates whether a valid referral order is required before scheduling. True enforces referral validation, false permits direct scheduling.

attributes.name: rule_category
attributes.description: Broad classification of the rule by business domain. Temporal rules govern timing, clinical rules enforce medical protocols, administrative rules manage workflow, financial rules ensure payment compliance, operational rules optimize resource use, and regulatory rules enforce compliance requirements.

attributes.name: rule_code
attributes.description: Business-assigned unique code for the scheduling rule, used for reference in Epic Cadence and OpTime scheduling systems.

attributes.name: rule_description
attributes.description: Detailed business explanation of the scheduling rule, its purpose, and enforcement logic. Provides context for schedulers and system administrators.

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the scheduling rule for display and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: rule_priority
attributes.description: Numeric priority ranking used to resolve conflicts when multiple rules apply to the same scheduling scenario. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Rules with higher priority take precedence in enforcement.

attributes.name: rule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the scheduling rule. Active rules are enforced in scheduling systems, inactive rules are retired, suspended rules are temporarily disabled, draft rules are under development, and pending approval rules await governance review.

attributes.name: rule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the scheduling rule governing its purpose and enforcement logic. Lead time rules control advance booking windows, eligibility rules determine patient qualification, constraint rules enforce scheduling restrictions, prerequisite rules require prior conditions, conflict rules prevent incompatible bookings, and capacity rules manage overbooking limits.

attributes.name: same_day_booking_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether appointments can be scheduled on the same day as the request. True allows same-day scheduling, false requires advance booking per minimum lead time rules.

attributes.name: self_scheduling_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether patients can book appointments directly through online portals without staff intervention. True permits patient self-service scheduling, false requires staff-assisted booking.

attributes.name: specialty_code
attributes.description: Medical specialty to which this rule applies, using standard specialty taxonomy codes. Null indicates the rule is specialty-agnostic.
attributes.references: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Specialty Taxonomy

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number for this rule, incremented with each modification. Supports audit trail and change tracking for rule evolution.

attributes.name: effective_start_date

attributes.name: gender_preference_provider

attributes.name: group_visit_eligible_flag

attributes.name: mrn

attributes.name: opt_out_reminders_flag

attributes.name: preference_notes

attributes.name: preference_source

attributes.name: preference_status

products.name: case_material_usage
products.description: This association product represents the consumption transaction between surgical_case and material_master. It captures the operational record of every supply item, implant, medication, or consumable used during a surgical procedure. Each record links one surgical case to one material item with usage-specific attributes including quantities consumed, lot/serial traceability for regulatory compliance (UDI), billable status, waste tracking, and per-case cost allocation. This is the SSOT for surgical supply consumption, cost accounting, and regulatory device tracking.. Existence Justification: In healthcare operations, each surgical case consumes multiple materials (sutures, implants, medications, disposables), and each material item is used across many different surgical cases over time. Operating room staff actively document material usage during and after each procedure, capturing case-specific consumption data including quantities, lot/serial numbers for regulatory traceability, billable status, waste tracking, and per-case costs. This is a core operational transaction managed as part of perioperative workflows.

products.name: appointment_prior_auth_requirement
products.description: This association product represents the payer-specific prior authorization requirement configuration for appointment types. It captures which appointment types require prior authorization under which payer rules, including the effective period, turnaround expectations, submission methods, and clinical criteria specific to each appointment-type-payer combination. Each record links one appointment type to one prior authorization rule with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship.. Existence Justification: In healthcare operations, prior authorization requirements are configured at the intersection of appointment types and payer rules. One appointment type (e.g., MRI, specialist consultation) requires prior authorization from multiple payers, each with different turnaround times, submission methods, and clinical criteria. Conversely, one payer's prior authorization rule applies to multiple appointment types. This is an operational configuration that scheduling staff and utilization management teams actively manage, with effective dates, termination dates, and payer-specific submission requirements that belong to the relationship itself.

attributes.description: Reference to the clinical guideline, medical policy, or evidence-based criteria document that applies to prior authorization for this appointment type under this payer rule. May be appointment-type-specific criteria. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this appointment type prior authorization requirement record was created in the system.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this prior authorization requirement becomes active for this appointment type under this payer rule. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: last_updated_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this appointment type prior authorization requirement record was last modified.

attributes.name: requires_prior_authorization
attributes.description: Indicates whether this appointment type requires prior authorization from the payer before scheduling. Supports revenue cycle compliance and denial prevention. [Moved from appointment_type: This boolean flag on appointment_type is too coarse-grained. Prior authorization requirements are payer-specific and time-bound, not universal to the appointment type. The flag should be replaced by a query against this association to determine if PA is required for a given appointment type, payer, and date combination.]
attributes.references: Payer Authorization Requirements, CMS Coverage Policies

attributes.name: submission_method
attributes.description: Allowed method(s) for submitting the prior authorization request for this appointment type under this payer rule: portal, fax, phone, EDI 278, or multiple. May be appointment-type-specific override of base rule submission method. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which this prior authorization requirement is no longer active for this appointment type under this payer rule. Null indicates ongoing requirement. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: turnaround_time_hours
attributes.description: Standard turnaround time in hours for the payer to respond to a prior authorization request for this appointment type. May differ from the base rule turnaround time if appointment-specific SLAs exist. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.

products.name: reminder_template
products.description: Master reference table for reminder_template. Referenced by reminder_template_id.

attributes.name: reminder_template_id
attributes.description: Primary key for reminder_template

attributes.name: appointment_type_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific appointment type or visit category that this reminder template is designed to support.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the healthcare facility or location where this reminder template is used for appointment scheduling.

attributes.name: org_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical or administrative department that owns and manages this reminder template.

attributes.name: specialty_id
attributes.description: Reference to the medical specialty or service line for which this reminder template is configured.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who approved this reminder template for production use.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this reminder template was approved for production use.

attributes.name: cancellation_instructions
attributes.description: Text instructions provided to the patient on how to cancel or reschedule the appointment, including contact information and deadlines.

attributes.name: confirmation_deadline_hours
attributes.description: Number of hours before the appointment by which the patient must confirm, used for capacity planning and waitlist management.

attributes.name: contact_email
attributes.description: Email address provided in the reminder for patients to contact the scheduling department or care team regarding their appointment.

attributes.name: contact_phone
attributes.description: Phone number provided in the reminder for patients to call with questions, confirmations, or cancellations related to their appointment.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this reminder template record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: delivery_channel
attributes.description: Communication channel through which the reminder is delivered to the patient or responsible party.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this reminder template is no longer active and should not be used for new appointments. Null indicates no end date.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this reminder template becomes active and available for use in scheduling workflows.

attributes.name: include_copay_estimate
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reminder should include an estimated copay or out-of-pocket cost for the appointment.

attributes.name: include_insurance_reminder
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reminder should include instructions to bring insurance cards and verify coverage before the appointment.

attributes.name: include_provider_info
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reminder message should include provider name, credentials, and contact information.

attributes.name: is_default
attributes.description: Indicates whether this template is the default reminder template for its associated appointment type, specialty, or department.

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: ISO 639-1 language code (with optional ISO 3166-1 country code) indicating the language of the reminder message content.

attributes.name: location_details
attributes.description: Detailed information about the appointment location including building name, floor, department, parking instructions, and check-in procedures.

attributes.name: max_send_attempts
attributes.description: Maximum number of times the system should attempt to deliver the reminder if initial delivery fails.

attributes.name: message_body
attributes.description: Full text content of the reminder message, including placeholders for dynamic data such as patient name, appointment date, location, and provider.

attributes.name: message_subject
attributes.description: Subject line or title of the reminder message, used primarily for email and portal notifications.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last modified this reminder template record.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this reminder template record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Administrative notes or comments about the reminder template, including usage guidelines, change history, or special considerations.

attributes.name: preparation_instructions
attributes.description: Clinical or administrative instructions for patient preparation before the appointment, such as fasting requirements, medication holds, or documentation to bring.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Priority classification of the reminder indicating urgency and importance for delivery and patient response.

attributes.name: requires_confirmation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reminder requires the patient to confirm or respond to the appointment notification.

attributes.name: retry_interval_minutes
attributes.description: Number of minutes to wait between retry attempts if reminder delivery fails.

attributes.name: send_time_preference
attributes.description: Preferred time of day (HH:MM format) when the reminder should be sent, respecting patient communication preferences and operational hours.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the reminder template indicating whether it is available for use in scheduling workflows.

attributes.name: template_code
attributes.description: Unique business code or identifier for the reminder template, used for system integration and external reference.

attributes.name: template_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the reminder template used for identification and selection in scheduling workflows.

attributes.name: template_type
attributes.description: Classification of the reminder template based on the type of appointment or care event it supports.

attributes.name: trigger_timing_days
attributes.description: Number of days before the scheduled appointment when the reminder should be sent. Negative values indicate days after the appointment.

attributes.name: trigger_timing_hours
attributes.description: Number of hours before the scheduled appointment when the reminder should be sent, used for same-day or precise timing requirements.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of the reminder template, incremented when content or configuration is updated to maintain audit trail and change history.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who created this reminder template record.

attributes.name: parent_reminder_template_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on reminder_template (parent_reminder_template_id)

domains.name: billing
domains.description: SSOT for all revenue cycle management (RCM) activities. Owns charge capture, CDM (Charge Description Master), professional and facility billing (CMS-1500, UB-04), coding (ICD-10, CPT, DRG), claim generation, payment posting, patient statements, collections, bad debt, contractual adjustments, ERA/EOB processing, and denial management. Integrates with Epic Resolute PB/HB, 3M HIS, and Cerner Revenue Cycle.
domains.references: UB-04, CMS-1500, CMS Billing Guidelines, HIPAA Transaction Standards, AMA CPT

products.name: charge
products.description: Core transactional record of every billable charge captured in the revenue cycle. Represents a single billable service, procedure, supply, or accommodation generated from clinical activity. Owns charge code (CDM reference), quantity, unit price, revenue code, service date, posting date, charge status, voided/corrected flag, and originating department. SSOT for charge capture in Epic Resolute PB/HB and Cerner Revenue Cycle. Links to encounter, rendering provider, CDM entry, and fee schedule for expected reimbursement.

attributes.description: Reference to the patient encounter or visit during which this charge was generated. Links the charge to the clinical episode of care.

attributes.name: charge_category
attributes.description: High-level grouping of the charge for financial reporting and analytics. Examples include surgical services, diagnostic imaging, laboratory, pharmacy, room and board.

attributes.name: charge_code
attributes.description: Internal charge code from the Charge Description Master (CDM). Maps to procedure codes, revenue codes, and pricing schedules. Core reference for billing and reimbursement.

attributes.name: charge_number
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for the charge. May be used for charge reconciliation, audit trails, and external communication. Typically system-generated or derived from encounter number and line sequence.
attributes.references: Epic Resolute Professional Billing (PB) Charge Master

attributes.name: charge_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the charge in the revenue cycle. Indicates whether the charge is awaiting review, posted to account, submitted on claim, paid by payer, or voided/corrected. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|posted|billed|paid|adjusted|voided|corrected|on_hold|denied — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Epic Resolute Professional Billing (PB) Charge Status Workflow

attributes.name: charge_type
attributes.description: Classification of the charge based on billing type. Determines claim form (CMS-1500 vs UB-04), revenue recognition rules, and reporting category.

attributes.name: correction_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why the charge was corrected. Examples: incorrect code, incorrect quantity, incorrect provider. Required for compliance and audit purposes when is_corrected is true.
attributes.references: Healthcare Financial Management Association (HFMA) Revenue Cycle Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the charge record was first created in the billing system. Used for audit trail, charge lag analysis, and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: diagnosis_pointer
attributes.description: Reference to the diagnosis code(s) that justify medical necessity for this charge. Typically a comma-separated list of pointers (e.g., 1,2,3) linking to diagnosis codes on the claim.

attributes.name: drug_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for pharmaceutical charges. Examples: ML (milliliters), GR (grams), UN (units), F2 (international units). Required for NDC billing.

attributes.name: expected_reimbursement_amount
attributes.description: Estimated payment amount based on payer contract, fee schedule, or payment methodology. Used for revenue forecasting and variance analysis. May be derived from DRG grouper, fee schedule lookup, or contract rate.

attributes.name: gross_charge_amount
attributes.description: Total charge amount before any adjustments, discounts, or contractual allowances. Calculated as quantity multiplied by unit price. Represents the full standard charge.

attributes.name: hold_date
attributes.description: Date the charge was placed on hold. Used to track charge lag and identify revenue cycle bottlenecks.
attributes.references: Healthcare Financial Management Association (HFMA) Revenue Cycle Standards

attributes.name: hold_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why the charge is on hold and not released for billing. Examples: pending authorization, missing documentation, coding review required, medical necessity review.
attributes.references: Healthcare Financial Management Association (HFMA) Revenue Cycle Standards

attributes.name: implant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this charge represents an implantable device from the case cart requiring UDI documentation and FDA tracking. Used for regulatory compliance and implant registry reporting.

attributes.name: is_billable
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this charge should be included on patient claims. Some charges may be tracked for cost accounting but not billed to payers (e.g., bundled services, courtesy charges).

attributes.name: is_corrected
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this charge is a correction of a previously posted charge. Corrected charges replace original charges and maintain audit trail linkage.

attributes.name: is_patient_responsible
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the patient has financial responsibility for this charge. Used to determine patient statement inclusion and collections workflow.
attributes.references: Healthcare Financial Management Association (HFMA) Patient Financial Communications Standards

attributes.name: is_voided
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this charge has been voided and should not be included in financial reporting or claim submission. Voided charges are retained for audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: modifier_1
attributes.description: First CPT or HCPCS modifier providing additional information about the service performed. Used to indicate special circumstances, bilateral procedures, or multiple procedures.

attributes.name: modifier_2
attributes.description: Second CPT or HCPCS modifier providing additional information about the service performed.

attributes.name: modifier_3
attributes.description: Third CPT or HCPCS modifier providing additional information about the service performed.

attributes.name: modifier_4
attributes.description: Fourth CPT or HCPCS modifier providing additional information about the service performed.

attributes.name: ndc_code
attributes.description: National Drug Code for pharmaceutical charges. Required for drug billing to Medicare Part B and Medicaid. Identifies the specific drug product, manufacturer, and package size.

attributes.name: place_of_service_code
attributes.description: Two-digit code identifying the location where the service was provided. Required on professional claims. Examples: 11 (office), 21 (inpatient hospital), 22 (outpatient hospital), 23 (emergency department).
attributes.references: CMS Place of Service Code Set

attributes.name: posting_date
attributes.description: Date the charge was posted to the patient account in the billing system. Used for revenue cycle reporting, aging analysis, and financial period assignment. May differ from service date due to charge lag.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: Number of units of the service or supply provided. Used to calculate extended charge amount. May represent minutes, units, visits, or other unit of measure depending on the charge type.

attributes.name: quantity_used
attributes.description: Number of units of the supply item consumed from this specific case cart and billed on this charge. May differ from quantity picked if partial usage or waste occurred. Used for supply chain reconciliation and charge validation.

attributes.name: released_date
attributes.description: Date the charge was released from hold and made available for claim submission. Used to calculate days in accounts receivable and charge lag metrics.
attributes.references: Healthcare Financial Management Association (HFMA) Revenue Cycle Standards

attributes.name: revenue_code
attributes.description: Three-digit code used on UB-04 facility claims to classify the type of service or accommodation provided. Required for hospital billing.
attributes.references: National Uniform Billing Committee (NUBC) Revenue Code Standard

attributes.name: service_date
attributes.description: Date on which the billable service or supply was provided to the patient. Used for claim submission, timely filing, and revenue recognition. Critical for determining billing period and payer coverage.

attributes.name: service_end_time
attributes.description: Timestamp when the service ended. Used for time-based billing, anesthesia minutes, and critical care time tracking.

attributes.name: service_start_time
attributes.description: Timestamp when the service began. Used for time-based billing, anesthesia minutes, and critical care time tracking.

attributes.name: unit_price
attributes.description: Price per unit of the service or supply as defined in the Charge Description Master (CDM) or fee schedule. Used to calculate gross charge amount before adjustments.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the charge record was last modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and incremental data processing.

attributes.name: void_date
attributes.description: Date the charge was voided in the billing system. Used for audit trail and financial period reconciliation.

attributes.name: void_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why the charge was voided. Examples: duplicate charge, service not performed, incorrect patient, incorrect code. Required for compliance and audit purposes when is_voided is true.
attributes.references: Healthcare Financial Management Association (HFMA) Revenue Cycle Standards

attributes.name: waste_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the supply item from this case cart was opened but not used (wasted) versus actually consumed. Critical for supply chain waste tracking and determining whether the charge should be billed to the patient or absorbed as facility cost.

products.name: cdm_entry
products.description: Charge Description Master (CDM) — the authoritative catalog of all billable items offered by the healthcare organization. Each entry defines a service or supply with its CDM code, description, revenue code, default CPT/HCPCS code, charge amount, cost center, department, active status, and effective/expiration dates. Managed in Epic Resolute HB and 3M HIS. Serves as the pricing and coding reference for charge capture.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: last_price_update_date

products.name: billing_coverage
products.description: Insurance coverage record linking a patient to a specific payer plan for a defined benefit period, including the complete history of real-time and batch eligibility verification transactions. Owns payer ID, plan name, plan type (HMO, PPO, POS, Medicare, Medicaid), member ID, group number, subscriber ID, subscriber relationship, coverage effective/termination dates, coordination of benefits (COB) order (primary/secondary/tertiary), copay amount, deductible amount, out-of-pocket maximum, and eligibility verification events (verification date, verification method — real-time 270/271, manual, batch — payer response status, coverage active flag, deductible met amount, out-of-pocket met amount, copay amount returned, verification source system). SSOT for patient insurance eligibility, coverage verification, benefit details, and all eligibility verification transactions — there is no separate eligibility check entity. Supports front-end revenue cycle eligibility workflows and reduces claim denials due to eligibility issues.
products.reference: Insurance Coverage / Eligibility Record

attributes.description: Reference to the patient visit or encounter associated with this write-off.

attributes.name: amount
attributes.description: The monetary value of the balance permanently written off from the patient account or invoice, expressed in US dollars (USD). This is the principal amount forgiven or deemed uncollectible.

attributes.name: appeal_date
attributes.description: The date on which an appeal was filed to contest or reverse this write-off.

attributes.name: appeal_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this write-off is subject to an active appeal or dispute process. True if under appeal, False otherwise.
attributes.references: CMS Appeals Process, Internal Revenue Cycle Standards

attributes.name: appeal_status
attributes.description: Current status of the appeal process: pending (under review), approved (write-off reversed), denied (write-off upheld), or withdrawn (appeal abandoned).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the write-off was formally approved by the authorizing user or manager.

attributes.name: approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this write-off requires managerial or executive approval based on amount thresholds or policy rules. True if approval is required, False otherwise.

attributes.name: bad_debt_referral_date
attributes.description: The date on which the account was referred to a collection agency or written off as bad debt, marking the transition from active collection to write-off.
attributes.references: GAAP Revenue Recognition, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA)

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: The cost center or department code associated with this write-off for internal financial tracking and allocation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this write-off record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: discount_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage discount applied to the original balance as part of the charity care or financial assistance program. For example, 100.00 represents a full write-off, 50.00 represents a 50% discount.

attributes.name: fpl_percentage
attributes.description: The patient or guarantor household income expressed as a percentage of the Federal Poverty Level, used to determine charity care eligibility. For example, 150.00 represents 150% of FPL.
attributes.references: IRS 501(r) Charity Care Requirements, HHS Poverty Guidelines

attributes.name: gl_account_code
attributes.description: The general ledger account code to which this write-off is posted for financial reporting, such as bad debt expense or charity care.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this write-off record was last updated or modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing additional context, justification, or documentation for this write-off, used for audit and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: original_balance
attributes.description: The original outstanding balance on the account or invoice before the write-off was applied, providing context for the write-off magnitude.

attributes.name: posting_date
attributes.description: The date on which the write-off was posted to the general ledger and financial reporting systems.

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the specific reason for the write-off, aligned with internal revenue cycle coding standards or external regulatory codes.
attributes.references: HIPAA Claim Adjustment Reason Codes (CARC), Internal RCM Standards

attributes.name: reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual explanation of why the balance was written off, providing context for audit and compliance review.

attributes.name: remaining_balance
attributes.description: The balance remaining on the account or invoice after this write-off is applied. May be zero if the write-off clears the account.

attributes.name: revenue_code
attributes.description: The UB-04 revenue code associated with the original charges being written off, providing service line detail.
attributes.references: UB-04 Billing Standards, CMS Revenue Code List

attributes.name: reversal_date
attributes.description: The date on which this write-off was reversed, restoring the balance to the account.

attributes.name: reversal_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this write-off has been reversed or undone. True if reversed, False if still active.

attributes.name: reversal_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why the write-off was reversed, such as 'Patient payment received' or 'Insurance appeal successful'.

attributes.name: service_date
attributes.description: The date of service or encounter for which the charges were originally incurred, providing historical context for the write-off.

attributes.name: write_off_category
attributes.description: Broader categorization of the write-off for financial reporting and analytics: patient responsibility (self-pay), insurance denial (payer refusal), uncompensated care (charity or bad debt), policy adjustment (internal policy), or audit adjustment (external audit finding).

attributes.name: write_off_date
attributes.description: The business date on which the write-off was officially recorded and the balance was removed from active accounts receivable.

attributes.name: write_off_number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique identifier or control number for this write-off transaction, used for tracking and audit purposes.

attributes.name: write_off_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the write-off: pending (awaiting approval), approved (authorized but not yet posted), posted (applied to account), reversed (undone), or under review (being audited or appealed).

attributes.name: write_off_type
attributes.description: Classification of the write-off by its nature: bad debt (uncollectible patient balance), charity care (financial assistance), small balance (below collection threshold), administrative (system correction), RAC recoupment (Recovery Audit Contractor adjustment), or contractual dispute (payer disagreement).
attributes.references: GAAP Revenue Recognition, IRS 501(r) Charity Care Requirements

products.name: payment_plan
products.description: Structured installment payment arrangement established between the healthcare organization and a patient or guarantor for an outstanding balance. Owns plan type (standard, interest-free, hardship), total plan amount, installment amount, installment frequency, plan start date, plan end date, number of installments, installments paid, remaining balance, plan status (active, completed, defaulted, cancelled), and enrollment channel. Supports patient financial engagement and self-pay collections.
products.reference: Patient Payment Plan / Installment Agreement

attributes.name: payment_plan_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the payment plan. Primary key.

attributes.name: compliance_policy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.policy. Business justification: Payment plans must comply with financial assistance policies, state regulations governing patient billing practices, and IRS 501(r) requirements. Required for demonstrating compliant billing practices

attributes.name: guarantor_id
attributes.description: Reference to the guarantor who is financially responsible for this payment plan.

attributes.name: mpi_record_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient who is the primary party responsible for this payment plan.

attributes.name: patient_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient account for which this payment plan was established.

attributes.name: primary_payment_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user or staff member who approved the payment plan, typically a financial counselor, billing manager, or revenue cycle specialist.

attributes.name: tertiary_payment_last_modified_by_user_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user or system process that most recently modified the payment plan record.

attributes.name: actual_completion_date
attributes.description: Actual date when the payment plan was completed, either through full payment or early payoff. Null if plan is still active or was cancelled/defaulted.

attributes.name: agreement_signed_date
attributes.description: Date when the payment plan agreement was signed by the patient or guarantor.

attributes.name: agreement_signed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patient or guarantor has signed the payment plan agreement. True means a signed agreement is on file, false means signature is pending or not required.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the payment plan was reviewed and approved by authorized staff.

attributes.name: auto_pay_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether automatic recurring payments are enabled for this payment plan. True means installments are automatically charged to the stored payment method on the due date, false means manual payment is required.

attributes.name: cancellation_date
attributes.description: Date when the payment plan was cancelled by either the patient or the healthcare organization.

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation of why the payment plan was cancelled, including patient request, non-compliance, account paid in full, or administrative reasons.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the payment plan record was first created in the system. Represents the audit trail for record creation.

attributes.name: default_date
attributes.description: Date when the payment plan was declared in default due to missed payments exceeding the grace period.

attributes.name: default_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why the payment plan defaulted, such as consecutive missed payments, insufficient funds, or patient non-response.

attributes.name: down_payment_amount
attributes.description: Initial payment made at the time of plan enrollment, if required. This amount is applied to the balance before installments begin. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date when the payment plan is expected to be completed based on the original terms. Nullable for open-ended plans.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the payment plan becomes active and the first installment is due. This is the binding start date of the agreement.

attributes.name: enrollment_channel
attributes.description: Channel through which the patient or guarantor enrolled in the payment plan. Patient portal indicates online self-service enrollment, phone indicates enrollment via call center, in-person indicates enrollment at a facility registration or billing desk, mail indicates paper application, email indicates enrollment via email correspondence, and mobile app indicates enrollment through a mobile application.

attributes.name: enrollment_date
attributes.description: Date when the patient or guarantor enrolled in the payment plan.

attributes.name: finance_charge_amount
attributes.description: Total finance charges or interest applied to the payment plan over its lifetime. Zero for interest-free plans. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: financial_assistance_program_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the financial assistance or charity care program under which this payment plan was approved, if applicable. Links to the organizations financial assistance policy and eligibility criteria.

attributes.name: grace_period_days
attributes.description: Number of days after the installment due date during which a late payment can be made without penalty or default.

attributes.name: installment_amount
attributes.description: Fixed amount due for each scheduled installment payment. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: installment_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which installment payments are scheduled. Weekly indicates every 7 days, biweekly every 14 days, monthly on the same day each month, quarterly every 3 months, and custom indicates a non-standard schedule.

attributes.name: installments_paid
attributes.description: Count of installment payments that have been successfully received and posted to date.

attributes.name: installments_remaining
attributes.description: Count of installment payments still outstanding to complete the payment plan.

attributes.name: interest_rate_percentage
attributes.description: Annual percentage rate (APR) applied to the payment plan balance, if applicable. Zero for interest-free plans. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5.00 for 5%).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the payment plan record was most recently updated. Represents the audit trail for record modification.

attributes.name: last_payment_amount
attributes.description: Amount of the most recent installment payment received. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: last_payment_date
attributes.description: Date when the most recent installment payment was received and posted.

attributes.name: late_fee_amount
attributes.description: Standard late fee charged for each missed or late installment payment, as defined in the payment plan agreement. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: missed_payments_count
attributes.description: Total number of installment payments that were missed or not received by the due date during the life of the payment plan.

attributes.name: next_payment_due_date
attributes.description: Date when the next scheduled installment payment is due. Null if plan is completed, cancelled, or defaulted.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes and comments related to the payment plan, including special arrangements, patient circumstances, or administrative instructions.

attributes.name: number_of_installments
attributes.description: Total number of scheduled installment payments required to complete the payment plan.

attributes.name: original_balance_amount
attributes.description: Total outstanding patient balance at the time the payment plan was established. This is the starting principal amount before any plan payments are applied. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: payment_method
attributes.description: Primary payment instrument used for installment payments. Credit card and debit card indicate card-based payments, ACH (Automated Clearing House) indicates electronic bank transfer, check indicates paper check, cash indicates in-person cash payment, and money order indicates certified payment instrument.
attributes.references: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS)

attributes.name: plan_number
attributes.description: Externally visible unique business identifier for the payment plan, used in patient communications and statements.

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the payment plan. Pending indicates awaiting approval or first payment, active indicates plan is in good standing with payments being made, completed indicates all installments paid in full, defaulted indicates missed payments beyond grace period, cancelled indicates plan was terminated by patient or organization, suspended indicates temporarily paused by mutual agreement.

attributes.name: plan_type
attributes.description: Classification of the payment plan based on terms and eligibility criteria. Standard plans follow default terms, interest-free plans waive interest charges, hardship plans are for patients with demonstrated financial need, extended plans have longer durations, short-term plans are for smaller balances, and custom plans have negotiated terms.

attributes.name: remaining_balance_amount
attributes.description: Current outstanding balance on the payment plan after all payments to date have been applied. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: total_paid_amount
attributes.description: Cumulative sum of all payments received and applied to this payment plan to date, including down payment and all installments. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: total_plan_amount
attributes.description: Total amount to be paid under the payment plan, including any interest, fees, or finance charges. May equal original balance for interest-free plans. Expressed in USD.

products.name: rac_audit
products.description: Post-payment audit record tracking CMS-initiated, payer-initiated, or internal audits of submitted claims and billing records. Covers RAC (Recovery Audit Contractor), MAC (Medicare Administrative Contractor), OIG (Office of Inspector General), ZPIC (Zone Program Integrity Contractor), and internal compliance audits. Owns audit type, audit contractor name, audit request date, records requested, audit period, findings type (overpayment, underpayment, no finding), finding amount, appeal filed flag, appeal level, appeal outcome, recoupment amount, recoupment date, and compliance resolution status. SSOT for post-payment audit management, compliance tracking, and audit response workflow in the billing domain.
products.reference: RAC Audit / Post-Payment Review

attributes.name: mpi_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the patient whose care or billing was audited.

attributes.name: payer_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the insurance payer or government program that initiated or sponsored the audit (e.g., Medicare, Medicaid, commercial payer).

attributes.name: primary_rac_employee_id
attributes.description: Internal user ID of the compliance officer, revenue cycle analyst, or HIM professional assigned to manage the audit response and resolution.

attributes.name: response_cda_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to interoperability.cda_document. Tracking which CDA document was submitted in response to each audit enables audit management, r

attributes.name: tertiary_rac_last_modified_by_user_employee_id
attributes.description: User ID of the individual who last modified this audit record.

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the patient visit or encounter associated with the audited claim or billing record.

attributes.name: appeal_decision_date
attributes.description: Date the appeal decision was issued by the reviewing authority (MAC, QIC, ALJ, Appeals Council, or Federal Court).

attributes.name: appeal_filed_date
attributes.description: Date the organization filed an appeal of the audit findings. Typically must be within 120 days of determination letter for Medicare RAC audits.

attributes.name: appeal_filed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the organization filed an appeal of the audit findings. True if appeal was filed, False if no appeal.

attributes.name: appeal_level
attributes.description: Current level in the Medicare appeals process. Redetermination (Level 1), Reconsideration by QIC (Level 2), ALJ Hearing (Level 3), Medicare Appeals Council Review (Level 4), Federal Court (Level 5).

attributes.name: appeal_outcome_amount
attributes.description: Final monetary amount after appeal resolution. May differ from original finding_amount if appeal was partially or fully favorable.

attributes.name: appeal_status
attributes.description: Current status or outcome of the appeal. Pending (under review), upheld (original finding affirmed), overturned (finding reversed), partially favorable (partial reversal), withdrawn, or dismissed.

attributes.name: audit_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting audit details, correspondence with auditor, internal review findings, and resolution activities.

attributes.name: audit_number
attributes.description: External audit reference number assigned by the auditing contractor or agency. Business identifier for tracking and correspondence.

attributes.name: audit_period_end_date
attributes.description: Ending date of the service period under audit review. Defines the temporal scope of claims and billing records subject to audit.

attributes.name: audit_period_start_date
attributes.description: Beginning date of the service period under audit review. Defines the temporal scope of claims and billing records subject to audit.

attributes.name: audit_request_date
attributes.description: Date the audit request or Additional Documentation Request (ADR) was received by the organization. Principal business event timestamp for the audit lifecycle.

attributes.name: audit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the audit. Tracks progression from initial request through resolution and closure. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: requested|in_progress|findings_issued|appeal_filed|appeal_pending|resolved|closed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: audit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the audit program. RAC (Recovery Audit Contractor), MAC (Medicare Administrative Contractor), OIG (Office of Inspector General), ZPIC (Zone Program Integrity Contractor), UPIC (Unified Program Integrity Contractor), internal compliance, payer audit, state Medicaid, or quality review. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rac|mac|oig|zpic|upic|internal_compliance|payer_audit|state_medicaid|quality_review — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: compliance_resolution_status
attributes.description: Status of internal compliance remediation activities in response to audit findings. Tracks corrective action plan development, implementation, and validation.

attributes.name: contractor_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Geographic or organizational jurisdiction of the auditing contractor (e.g., Region A, Region B, statewide, national).

attributes.name: contractor_name
attributes.description: Name of the auditing organization or contractor conducting the audit (e.g., Cotiviti, Performant, HMS, or internal compliance department).

attributes.name: corrective_action_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of corrective actions taken to remediate audit findings and prevent recurrence (e.g., staff training, policy updates, system enhancements, coding review process changes).

attributes.name: corrective_action_plan_date
attributes.description: Date the organization submitted or finalized a corrective action plan to address systemic issues identified in the audit.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this audit record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record creation.

attributes.name: extrapolation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the auditor applied statistical extrapolation to project findings from a sample to a larger population of claims. True if extrapolation was used, False otherwise.

attributes.name: extrapolation_sample_size
attributes.description: Number of claims in the statistical sample used for extrapolation, if extrapolation_flag is True.

attributes.name: extrapolation_universe_size
attributes.description: Total number of claims in the population to which sample findings were extrapolated, if extrapolation_flag is True.

attributes.name: finding_amount
attributes.description: Total monetary amount identified in the audit finding. Positive for overpayments (amounts owed to payer), negative for underpayments (amounts owed to provider).

attributes.name: finding_type
attributes.description: Classification of the audit finding. Overpayment (provider must refund), underpayment (provider owed additional payment), no finding (claim upheld), documentation deficiency, coding error, medical necessity denial, or coverage denial. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: overpayment|underpayment|no_finding|documentation_deficiency|coding_error|medical_necessity|coverage_denial — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: findings_issued_date
attributes.description: Date the auditor issued formal findings, determination letter, or demand letter communicating audit results.

attributes.name: interest_amount
attributes.description: Interest charges applied to overpayment amounts per statutory requirements. Calculated from date of overpayment to date of recoupment.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this audit record was last updated. Audit trail for record modification.

attributes.name: overpayment_amount
attributes.description: Amount determined to have been overpaid to the provider and subject to recoupment. Subset of finding_amount when finding_type is overpayment.

attributes.name: records_requested_count
attributes.description: Number of medical records, claims, or billing documents requested by the auditor for review.

attributes.name: records_submitted_count
attributes.description: Number of medical records, claims, or billing documents actually submitted to the auditor in response to the request.

attributes.name: recoupment_amount
attributes.description: Actual amount recouped or offset from future payments by the payer. May differ from overpayment_amount if partial recoupment, payment plan, or appeal adjustments occurred.

attributes.name: recoupment_date
attributes.description: Date the payer initiated recoupment or offset of the overpayment amount from provider payments.

attributes.name: recoupment_method
attributes.description: Method by which the overpayment was recovered. Offset (deducted from future payments), direct payment (check or EFT), installment plan (extended payment agreement), settlement (negotiated amount), or waived.

attributes.name: response_due_date
attributes.description: Deadline by which the organization must submit requested documentation to the auditor. Typically 45 days from ADR receipt for RAC audits.

attributes.name: response_submitted_date
attributes.description: Date the organization submitted the requested documentation to the auditor.

attributes.name: underpayment_amount
attributes.description: Amount determined to have been underpaid to the provider and subject to additional reimbursement. Subset of finding_amount when finding_type is underpayment.

products.name: invoice_coverage_billing
products.description: This association product represents the claim submission event between an invoice and a specific insurance coverage in the coordination of benefits (COB) sequence. It captures the billing lifecycle for each payer in the COB order (primary, secondary, tertiary). Each record links one invoice to one coverage with submission-specific attributes including amounts billed, allowed, paid, patient responsibility, adjudication dates, and claim status. This is the operational record of each claim filing required by CMS and payer regulations for multi-coverage scenarios.. Existence Justification: In healthcare billing, a single invoice is routinely submitted to multiple insurance coverages in sequence (primary, secondary, tertiary) as mandated by Coordination of Benefits (COB) regulations. Each submission is a distinct operational event with its own amounts, dates, claim status, payer control numbers, and adjudication outcomes. Conversely, a single coverage receives claims from many different invoices over time. This is not an analytical correlation—it is an actively managed business process with regulatory requirements, tracked lifecycle states, and dedicated staff (claims specialists) who monitor submission status, handle denials, and manage appeals for each invoice-coverage pairing.

products.name: billing_network_participation
products.description: This association product represents the contractual network participation relationship between insurance coverage plans and care delivery sites. It captures payer-facility network contracts that determine whether a care site is in-network or out-of-network for a specific payer plan, along with authorization requirements, referral rules, and contract effective periods. Each record links one coverage (representing a payer plan) to one care site with contract terms that exist only in the context of this payer-facility network relationship. This is the operational SSOT for network status determination during patient registration, eligibility verification, and claims adjudication workflows.. Existence Justification: In healthcare revenue cycle operations, payer organizations establish network contracts with multiple care delivery sites across an integrated delivery network, and each care site participates in network agreements with multiple payers. Network participation is an actively managed contractual relationship with specific terms (in-network status, authorization requirements, contracted rates, effective dates) that vary by each unique payer-facility pair. Revenue cycle staff query network participation during patient registration to determine coverage implications, and contract management teams maintain these relationships as payers and facilities negotiate, renew, or terminate network agreements.

products.name: invoice_line_item

It captures study-specific billing policies, reimbursement rates, and coverage determinations for each billable service used in a research protocol. Each record links one CDM entry to one research study with attributes that define whether the service is billed as research versus standard-of-care, the negotiated reimbursement rate for that study, and the effective period for those billing rules.. Healthcare billing operations must maintain study-specific coverage rules, reimbursement rates, and effective dates for each service-study combination to ensure compliant charge routing and accurate claims submission.

attributes.name: submitted_timestamp

attributes.name: total_allowed_amount

attributes.name: total_paid_amount
attributes.description: Total amount paid by the payer to the provider for this claim, after applying deductibles, coinsurance, and other patient responsibility amounts.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time this claim record was last modified in the revenue cycle management system.

attributes.name: modifier_3

attributes.name: modifier_4

attributes.references: AMA CPT Modifier List, CMS HCPCS Modifiers

attributes.name: ndc_code

attributes.name: ordering_provider_npi

attributes.name: outlier_payment_amount

attributes.name: paid_amount

attributes.name: paid_date
attributes.description: The date payment was issued by the payer for this line item, typically matching the remittance advice date.

attributes.name: procedure_code

attributes.description: The CPT or HCPCS code representing the specific billable service or procedure performed. Five-character alphanumeric code used for billing and reimbursement.

attributes.name: remark_code
attributes.description: Supplemental code providing additional explanation or context for the line item adjudication decision, often used alongside denial reason codes.

attributes.name: revenue_code

attributes.name: service_description

attributes.name: service_from_date
attributes.description: The start date of the service period for this line item. Represents the first date the service was rendered.

attributes.name: service_to_date
attributes.description: The end date of the service period for this line item. For single-day services, this matches the service from date.

attributes.name: units_of_service
attributes.description: The quantity of services rendered for this line item. May represent days, visits, procedures, or other unit measures depending on the service type.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

Supports up to 25 diagnosis codes per claim per UB-04 and CMS-1500 specifications. Critical for DRG assignment, quality reporting, and RAC audit defense.

attributes.name: chronic_condition_flag

attributes.references: CMS Chronic Conditions Data Warehouse, HEDIS Chronic Condition Measures

attributes.name: coding_source

attributes.name: coding_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this diagnosis code was assigned or last validated by a coder. Used for coding turnaround time (TAT) measurement and compliance audits.

attributes.name: complication_flag

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: denial_risk_flag

attributes.name: diagnosis_category

attributes.name: diagnosis_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) Diagnosis Code

attributes.name: diagnosis_pointer

attributes.name: diagnosis_sequence

attributes.name: diagnosis_version

attributes.name: drg_grouper_flag

attributes.name: encounter_type

attributes.name: hac_flag

attributes.name: laterality
attributes.description: Anatomical side affected by the diagnosis (e.g., left femur fracture, right eye cataract). Required for certain ICD-10-CM codes to achieve specificity.

attributes.name: poa_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the diagnosis was present at the time of inpatient admission. Y=Yes, N=No, U=Unknown, W=Clinically Undetermined, 1=Exempt. Required for inpatient claims per CMS Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) reporting.
attributes.references: CMS Present on Admission Reporting Guidelines, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines Appendix I

attributes.name: quality_measure_flag

attributes.references: CMS Quality Measure Specifications, HEDIS Technical Specifications, NCQA

attributes.name: submission_method

attributes.name: submission_number

attributes.name: submission_status

attributes.name: submission_timestamp

attributes.name: submission_type
attributes.description: Categorizes the nature of the submission: original (first submission), resubmission (after denial or rejection), corrected (error correction), void (cancellation), or replacement (supersedes prior submission).

attributes.name: submitter_contact_email
attributes.description: Email address of the submitter contact person for electronic correspondence regarding this submission.

attributes.name: submitter_contact_name
attributes.description: Name of the individual contact person at the submitting organization responsible for this submission. Used for follow-up and inquiries.

attributes.name: submitter_contact_phone
attributes.description: Phone number of the submitter contact person for inquiries and follow-up regarding this submission.

attributes.name: submitter_organization_name
attributes.description: Name of the organization or billing service that submitted the claim. May differ from the rendering provider organization.

attributes.name: timely_filing_deadline
attributes.description: The contractual deadline by which the claim must be submitted to the payer to comply with timely filing requirements. Used for submission prioritization and compliance monitoring.

attributes.name: transmission_control_number
attributes.description: Unique control number assigned to the transmission envelope (ISA/GS level in EDI 837). Used for transmission-level tracking and reconciliation.

attributes.name: transmission_file_name
attributes.description: Name of the electronic file (e.g., EDI 837 file) that contained this claim submission. Used for technical audit trails and file-level reconciliation.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this submission record was last modified. Used for audit trails, change tracking, and data synchronization.

products.name: status_history
products.description: Lifecycle status history for each claim, recording every status transition from creation through final adjudication or write-off. Captures status code, status description, status category (payer-defined vs. internal), effective timestamp, source system, user or automated process that triggered the transition, and associated payer response codes. Supports real-time claim tracking per ANSI X12 276/277 transaction sets and enables SLA monitoring for timely filing compliance.
products.reference: ANSI X12 276/277 Claim Status

attributes.name: status_history_id
attributes.description: Primary key for status_history

attributes.name: claim_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent claim for which this status transition was recorded. Links to the claim master record.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: The identifier of the user who manually triggered this status transition. Null if the transition was automated or system-generated. Used for accountability and audit trail in Revenue Cycle Management (RCM).

attributes.name: appeal_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this status transition is associated with an appeal or reconsideration request. True if the status change is part of an appeal workflow; False otherwise. Supports denial management and appeals tracking.

attributes.name: check_or_eft_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Check or Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) Number
attributes.description: The check number or Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) trace number associated with the payment that triggered this status transition to a paid state. Null if no payment was issued. Used for payment reconciliation and cash application.

attributes.name: clearinghouse_trace_number
attributes.description: The unique trace or reference number assigned by the clearinghouse for this status update transaction. Used for troubleshooting and reconciliation with clearinghouse reports.

attributes.name: coordination_of_benefits_sequence
attributes.description: The payer sequence number in coordination of benefits (COB) scenarios (1 for primary, 2 for secondary, 3 for tertiary). Indicates which payer this status applies to when multiple payers are involved.

attributes.name: corrected_claim_indicator

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: days_in_prior_status

attributes.name: denial_category
attributes.description: High-level categorization of the denial reason when the status represents a denial. Null if not a denial status. Supports denial management analytics and root cause analysis.
attributes.references: CMS Claims Processing Manual, NCCI Edits

attributes.name: effective_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when this status became effective for the claim. Represents the real-world business event time of the status transition, critical for Service Level Agreement (SLA) monitoring and timely filing compliance tracking.

attributes.name: is_final_status
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this status represents a terminal state in the claim lifecycle (e.g., fully paid, denied and closed, written off). True if no further status transitions are expected; False if the claim remains in an active workflow state.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this status history record was last modified. Typically immutable for status history records, but may be updated if corrections or annotations are applied.
attributes.references: HITRUST CSF - Audit Logging, SOC 2 - Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: payer_response_code

attributes.name: payer_response_description

attributes.name: prior_status_code

attributes.name: remittance_date

attributes.name: sla_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this status transition occurred within the defined Service Level Agreement (SLA) timeframe for the claim type and payer contract. attributes.references: CMS Timely Filing Requirements, Payer Contract Terms

attributes.name: source_system

attributes.name: status_category
attributes.description: Classification of the status origin: whether it is a payer-defined status received via Electronic Remittance Advice (ERA) or 277 response, an internal workflow state, a system-generated transition, or a manual override by revenue cycle staff.
attributes.references: ANSI X12 835 - Healthcare Claim Payment/Advice, ANSI X12 277 - Claim Status Notification

attributes.name: status_code
attributes.description: The standardized code representing the claim status at this point in time. Aligns with ANSI X12 277 Claim Status Category Codes and internal workflow states.

attributes.name: status_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the claim status, providing context for the status code (e.g., 'Submitted to Payer', 'Pending Additional Information', 'Adjudicated - Paid', 'Denied - Medical Necessity').

attributes.name: status_reason
attributes.description: Internal reason or note explaining why this status transition occurred, particularly for manual overrides, appeals, or corrected claims. Supports denial management and Recovery Audit Contractor (RAC) audit responses.

attributes.name: transaction_set_identifier
attributes.description: The ANSI X12 transaction set control number or identifier associated with the Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) transaction that triggered this status change (e.g., 277 response, 835 ERA). Enables correlation with source EDI files for audit and reconciliation.
attributes.references: ANSI X12 Standards - Transaction Set Control

attributes.name: triggered_by_process
attributes.description: The name of the automated process, batch job, or workflow engine that triggered this status transition (e.g., 'Nightly Clearinghouse Sync', 'ERA Import Job', 'Auto-Denial Workflow'). Null if manually triggered.

attributes.name: void_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this status transition represents a voided or cancelled claim submission (frequency type code 8 in ANSI X12 837). True if the claim was voided; False otherwise.

attributes.name: work_queue_assignment
attributes.description: The name of the revenue cycle work queue or team to which this claim was assigned following this status transition (e.g., 'Denials Management', 'Prior Auth Follow-Up', 'Payment Posting', 'Appeals'). Supports workflow routing and workload balancing.

SSOT for all ERA transactions received from Medicare, Medicaid, HMO, PPO, and commercial payers. Enables automated payment posting, contractual adjustment calculation, and reconciliation against expected reimbursement per payer contracts.
